# SideCut — repository memory

## 80.6.28 (October 30, 2026 · 9:43 PM EDT): the pages follow the source

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"The playlists and Albums should be in here in streaming, THE BUTTONS SHOULD DO
  WHAT THEY SHOULD IF IM IN STREAMING IT DOES STREAMING ALL, STREAMING PLAYLISTS AND ALBUMS, IF IM IN
  DOWNLOADS, REGULAR ALBUMS AND REGULAR PLAYLISTS SHOULD SHOW"*. Two things: the streaming lists need a
  place of their own, and the buttons have to belong to the source that is on.
- **WHY THE BUTTONS DID NOT.** The side rail had two page glyphs (Library, Albums) and one source switch.
  The streaming **playlists** had no page at all - they were a row of chips under the shelf - so on the
  source there was no button that showed every one of them. Worse, the **Library pill**'s two halves
  (`#playlistsHalf`, `#albumsHalf`) called `navigate('playlists')` / `navigate('albums')`, which set the
  *downloaded* half and rendered the downloaded list - behind a shelf that stays on top of it. On the
  source those two halves therefore changed nothing you could see.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** (1) **The rail is three pages**: Songs, Playlists, Albums, each with its own glyph
  (`plist` is a new path - ruled lines with a mark, so a playlist is not the library glyph again), and the
  source switch still sits under a hairline where it was. (2) **All three stay in the source**:
  `scShelfOpenTab()` maps the third tab and never writes `scShelf.src`; the switch is still the only thing
  that flips it. (3) **A streaming playlists page** in `scStreamRender()`, drawn with `scShelfGrid('pl',
  ...)` the way the albums page is drawn with `'al'` - a cover, a name, a count per tile, a **New
  playlist** button, the *From the source* pill, and the line that says a hold deletes a playlist. The
  tiles were already wired for open and for the two-second hold, so the page inherits both. (4) **The pill
  follows the source**: on the source its halves open the source's Songs and Albums pages; on the device
  they do what they always did. In single-button mode the one pill flips the source's pages instead of the
  half underneath the shelf. (5) **The device's three pages are the library's three**: Songs lands on All
  Songs (it used to land on whatever playlist was last used, which is not what the word says), Playlists
  on the playlist strip, Albums on the albums.
- **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE.** The switch still does not move a page; a page glyph still never
  changes the source. Nothing was removed from the shelf: the chips and the *Streaming albums* row are
  still on the songs page, so the way that exists keeps working. No downloaded list, album, playlist or
  setting is written by any of this; the only state touched is `scShelf.page` and, on the device side,
  which list the library shows.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** `dev/patch-80628.py` over the released 80.6.27 page: `--check` **1** before, 10 steps
  applied, a second run a no-op, `--check` **0**. `dev/check-80628.cjs` passes **39 checks**, and the ones
  that matter are run, not read: `scShelfOpenTab` in four states (Playlists on the source keeps
  `src = 's'` and paints once; the page already up only marks; Albums on the device stays on the device;
  Songs on the source stays on the source), and `scShelfGrid('pl', ...)` against fake lists (one tile per
  playlist, name and count on it, "1 song" not "1 songs", no album tile on the playlists page, and an
  empty page that says so). It also proves the songs/albums halves of the pill are decided *before* the
  downloaded `navigate()` on the source, that the playlists page is decided before any single list page is
  drawn, and that every inline script still compiles. OTA rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/`
  **1169865** bytes at v80.6.28, the `ota-play/` channel (**1138844** bytes) untouched.
- **NOT CLAIMED.** There is no phone and no browser here. Nobody has tapped the new third glyph, swiped
  the rail with three glyphs on it, or watched the pill switch pages on a real screen. The logic, the
  mapping and the drawn markup are proven; the look of a three-glyph rail is not.
## 80.6.27 (October 30, 2026 · 9:37 PM EDT): the record player takes you to the song that is playing

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"if your streaming a song it should take you to the song if you click on the
  record player not some random song"*. He is describing one tap that answered with two different songs.
- **WHY IT LANDED ON ANOTHER SONG.** The tap on the mini turntable calls `openAlbumForCurrentSong()`, and
  that function can only see the **downloaded deck**: it reads `queue[queueIndex]` and `allTracks`. A
  stream never touches either - the streaming module deliberately keeps its own `<audio>`, its own store
  and its own lists so a dead stream cannot take the real player with it. So while the source was playing,
  the tap resolved whatever the deck had played *last*, and opened the album for it. That is the random
  song: not a wrong guess, but a different player's state being read as if it were the current one.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** (1) **The tap asks the stream first.** `openAlbumForCurrentSong()` now starts with
  `scStreamPhoneOwns() && scStreamJumpToPlaying()` and returns when that takes the tap, so the downloaded
  queue is never consulted while the source owns the bar. The device path below is untouched. (2)
  **`scStreamPlayingList(id)`** finds the list the streaming song is actually in - the list already on
  screen first (that is the one meant), then the albums, then the playlists - and answers `{kind, name}` or
  `null`. (3) **`scStreamJumpToPlaying()`** puts the source on, opens that list, and on the next frame
  finds the row whose `data-hold` is that song, scrolls the shelf's own pane to it and lights it for a
  moment. A song in no list still opens the streaming shelf, which is where the playing song is drawn -
  the tap never answers with nothing. It scrolls with `smoothScrollIn` and, failing that, by writing
  `scrollTop` on `#scStreamBlock`; `scrollIntoView` is still never used, because on Android it bubbles out
  of the pane and lifts the whole app.
- **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE.** The tap does not start, stop or re-resolve the stream, does not
  open a list the song is not in, and does not invent a list for a loose song. It navigates; it does not
  play. The long press for the turntable angle and the whole device-side resolution are unchanged.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** `dev/patch-80627.py` over the released 80.6.26 page: `--check` **1** before, 4 steps
  applied, a second run a no-op, `--check` **0**. `dev/check-80627.cjs` passes **43 checks**, and it runs
  the code rather than reading it: the resolver in six states (the open list wins over an album that also
  holds the song; albums are tried before playlists; a loose song resolves to nothing; a numeric id in the
  store still matches the string from the row), and the jump against a fake shelf - the album opens, the
  right row is scrolled to and lit while the one above it is not, the light comes off again, the shelf is
  only repainted when it is not already up, the source comes on when the tap starts from the device side,
  a loose song opens the shelf instead of a list, an empty shelf scrolls nothing and does not throw, and a
  stream that does not own the bar does not take the tap at all. It also proves the guard sits *before*
  the downloaded queue is read, which is the whole bug. All seven inline scripts compile. OTA rebuilt to a
  true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1168596** bytes at v80.6.27, the `ota-play/` channel (**1138844**
  bytes) untouched.
- **NOT CLAIMED.** There is no phone and no browser here: no record player was tapped with a stream
  playing, and the scroll and the light were never watched on a screen. The wiring and the logic are
  proven; the feel of the tap is not.
## 80.6.26 (October 30, 2026 · 9:17 PM EDT): the streaming albums are a page, and a list is held to delete

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"no the streaming albums should be easy to see and it shouldn't go to
  regular downloaded albums, fix that and make it possible to delete a streaming album or playlist by
  holding on it for 2 seconds"*. Two requests, and the first is a correction of the last release.
- **WHY ALBUMS COULD NOT BE SEEN.** 80.6.26's predecessor made both page glyphs leave the source
  (`scShelf.src = 'd'`) so the downloaded songs were reachable from them. The cost was the other half of
  the same switch: while the source was on, the **Albums** glyph opened the downloaded albums, and the
  streaming albums existed only as one row (`#scStreamAlLink`) inside the streaming library. The page
  named after albums could not open it.
- **WHY A LIST COULD NOT BE DELETED.** `scStreamHold()` - the two-second hold that opens a row's popup -
  was wired to song rows only (`.scs-row`, `.scsp-row`). Album tiles and playlist chips got a click and
  nothing else, so a list made by mistake was permanent: no sheet, no delete, no way back.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** (1) **The glyph keeps the source.** `scShelfOpenTab()` no longer writes `src`; the
  switch is the source and Library/Albums are its two pages, so on the source, Albums *is* the streaming
  albums page. Re-tapping the page already up still only moves the mark. (2) **The page says what it is**:
  a coral *From the source* pill beside the title, and the line under it now says holding an album for two
  seconds deletes it. (3) **`scStreamHoldList()`** arms the same two-second timer on the album tiles and
  the playlist chips, cancels on `pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`pointerleave`, blocks the context menu and
  swallows the click that follows a hold in the capture phase - so a hold never also opens. (4)
  **`scStreamLibMenu()`** opens the app's own `scStreamSheet()` with *Open* and a danger row named for what
  it deletes. (5) **`scStreamLibDelete()`** is the one delete path: it removes the named list, closes the
  page if that list was the one on screen, saves and repaints, and offers the app's `toastWithUndo()` -
  which puts the list back **in the place it was**, not at the end of the row.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** `dev/patch-80626.py` over the released 80.6.25 page: `--check` **1** before, 7 steps
  applied, a second run a no-op, `--check` **0**. `dev/check-80626.cjs` passes **46 checks**, and it does
  not only read text - it runs the handlers: the glyph truth table (source + Albums keeps `src = 's'`;
  the page already up only marks; a list on that page yields; the device side stays on the device), and
  the delete against a fake shelf (the named album goes and the playlists do not, the open page closes,
  one save and one paint, undo restores it at index 0, a missing name deletes nothing, and the same path
  deletes a playlist). The release is on the page with its computed Eastern stamp, and all seven inline
  scripts compile. OTA rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1167008** bytes at v80.6.26, the
  `ota-play/` channel (**1138844** bytes) untouched, as it has been since it was held.
- **NOT CLAIMED.** There is no phone and no browser here: no album tile was held for two real seconds, no
  sheet was tapped, no undo was pressed on a device. What is proven is the wiring and the logic, not the
  feel of the hold under a thumb.
## 80.6.25 (October 30, 2026 · 9:04 PM EDT): the side rail holds still, and the songs are one tap away

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"WHY DO THE SIDE BUTTONS KEEP MOVING AND ITS NOT LETTING ME ACCESS MT
  DOWNLOADED SONGS FROM THE BUTTONS"*. Both halves are the 80.6.23 side rail, and neither is the
  flicker that release repaired: no code left repositions the rail, and nothing in it is rebuilt per tap
  any more.
- **WHY THEY MOVED.** The pill is `position:fixed` with a `backdrop-filter`, floating over a list that
  scrolls under it - so its backdrop is re-sampled on every frame of a scroll, and on a WebView a fixed,
  blurred layer visibly judders against the moving page. The 80.6.23 mark also still wrote the source
  glyph as `innerHTML` on every pass (`scShelfMark` was fixed for the *building*, not for the *marking*),
  which replaces the node under the thumb and repaints the pill from the inside out.
- **WHY THE SONGS WERE UNREACHABLE.** `scShelf.page` and `scShelf.src` are two fields: with the switch on
  the source, the **Library** and **Albums** glyphs drew the streaming set - the two buttons named after
  the library opened something that was not it. The only way home was the third glyph, whose icon showed
  where you *already were*: standing on the device side it showed the device arrow, so tapping the one
  arrow that means "your downloaded songs" switched you *away* from them, and flipping back kept whichever
  page was up, so from streaming albums you landed on device albums.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** Library and Albums leave the source: a tap on either lands on what is downloaded. The
  switch's icon is the destination (device arrow on the source, waveform on the device) and its label and
  title follow. Flipping to the device comes home to the song list. The switch is built once with both
  icons and one `on` class decides which is drawn - no `innerHTML`, and a glyph is restyled only when its
  mark actually changes. The rail is a 96% opaque pill with no `backdrop-filter`, so scrolling under it
  repaints nothing of it. Position, size, gaps, `pointer-events` and `data-shelf` are untouched.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** `dev/patch-80625.py` over the released 80.6.24 page: `--check` **1** before, 8 steps
  applied, `--check` **0** after, a second run a no-op. `dev/check-80625.cjs` passes **29 checks** - the
  pill has no blur, the switch is built with both icons and marked by class only, no `innerHTML` survives
  in `scShelfMark`, the device arrow is what shows on the source, both page glyphs set `src = 'd'`, the
  device side resets to the song list, the streaming entry point still switches the source on, the release
  is on the page with its Eastern stamp, and all seven inline scripts compile. OTA rebuilt to a true fixed
  point - root + `ota/` **1166209** bytes at v80.6.25, the `ota-play/` channel (**1138844** bytes)
  untouched, as it has been since it was held. **Not claimed:** there is no phone and no browser here, so
  the rail was not scrolled under, no glyph was tapped and no downloaded list was seen - what is verified
  is that the pill no longer asks to be re-blurred or rewritten, and that the path from either page glyph
  to the downloaded songs no longer depends on the switch.
## 80.6.24 (October 30, 2026 · 7:05 PM EDT): the patch notes carry their day and their time

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"WHAT THE HELL DID YOU SO WOTH THE PACTCH NOTES IT SHOULD BE OCTOBER 30th
  2026 AND THE TIME IN EST"* - and the notes were wrong: twelve releases were stamped with a bare day.
- **THE REPAIR.** Every 80.x changelog entry before 80.6.12 carries the day it landed *and* the Eastern
  time it landed at (`October 29, 2026 · 8:04 PM EDT`): 55 entries from 80.0 on, 230 of the page's
  entries with a literal `·` and 173 with the escaped `\u00b7` - both render the same. The twelve from
  80.6.12 through 80.6.23 were stamped with a bare `2026-10-30`: no clock on it at all, and for nine of
  them the wrong day, because they landed on the *evening of October 29* Eastern and were dated the
  30th. Each of the twelve now carries the Eastern time of its own release commit: 80.6.12 at 8:04 PM,
  80.6.13 at 9:14, 80.6.14 at 9:37, 80.6.15 at 9:46, 80.6.16 at 10:24, 80.6.17 at 10:37, 80.6.18 at
  10:46, 80.6.19 at 10:54, 80.6.20 at 11:10 (all October 29), then 80.6.21 at 7:26 AM, 80.6.22 at
  5:20 PM and 80.6.23 at 6:25 PM on October 30.
- **THE CLOCK IS EASTERN, AND THE LABEL IS EDT.** October 30 is still daylight time in New York - the
  change back to EST is in November - so the label stays `EDT`, the same label as every 80.x entry before
  these. The time shown is Eastern, which is what was asked for; if the letters themselves are wanted as
  `EST`, that is one word in the next payload and every release to follow.
- **NOTHING ELSE MOVED.** No song, list, album, rail or player code is touched: the payload replaces
  twelve `date:` values that are only ever drawn as text on the changelog screen (`entry.date`, at the
  release row - nothing parses it), adds this release's entry, and bumps the version. The change is in
  the notes themselves, which is the point.
- **WHERE IT WENT WRONG.** The nine payloads from 80.6.12 on each wrote `date: '2026-10-30'` by hand
  instead of computing the Eastern stamp at apply time - which is what `eastern()` in this payload does,
  and what `dev/release-record.py` has always done for this file. The verifier now fails a release that
  writes a bare ISO day again: `check-80624.cjs` asserts that no entry is a `YYYY-MM-DD`, that all 55
  entries from 80.0 on carry a day and an Eastern clock, that the twelve repaired stamps and this one run
  forward in time, and that the 361 older entries - written in four other shapes before 57.0 - are not
  touched by the repair.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** `dev/patch-80624.py` over a fresh clone of the released 80.6.23 page: fourteen steps
  (twelve dates, the version, the entry), a second run a no-op with `--check` 0. `dev/check-80624.cjs`
  passes **28 checks**, including a compile of all seven inline scripts, so the page whose notes changed
  is still the page that boots. OTA rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1164892** bytes at
  v80.6.24, `ota-play/` still HELD (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** no browser and no phone here, so
  the changelog screen was not opened on a device; what is verified is the strings the screen draws and
  that the page still parses.
## 80.6.23 (October 30, 2026 · 6:25 PM EDT): streaming moves into the library and the albums

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"the buttons shouldn't glitch when you through the selections, there should
  be add to a playlist and add to album option in streaming or wait we can merge the streaming into the
  actual albums and library, with another side button icon that has streaming albums streaming playlists
  so you can switch between them, this would replace the side buttons there rn"*. Three asks: the rail
  stops glitching, the streaming page offers both kinds of list, and streaming stops being a place of its
  own.
- **THE FLICKER WAS TWO BUGS.** `scShelfRender()` reassigned `rail.innerHTML` on every render, which
  throws away the element that was just tapped: its press animation never ran, and a `position:fixed` rail
  with a backdrop blur settled visibly each time a glyph was chosen. And `scShelfOpenTab()` called
  `navigate('library')` and then `renderTabs()` and `renderList()` itself - while `navigate()` already
  paints both (`if(isLibrary){ renderTabs(); renderList(); }`) - so every tab tap drew its page twice in
  one frame: the strip scrolled, jumped back and scrolled again. The rail is now built once
  (`data-built`) and `scShelfMark()` only moves the `.on` class and the source glyph; `scShelfApply()` is
  the single painter, and the hand paint is a fallback for a page with no `navigate()` to ask. Tapping the
  page that is already up repaints nothing.
- **STREAMING IS A SOURCE, NOT A PAGE.** The rail's three glyphs (streaming / library / albums) are two
  pages and a switch: `library`, `albums`, a hairline, then a glyph that flips `scShelf.src` between `'d'`
  (what is on this device) and `'s'` (what plays from the source). With the switch on streaming, the
  Albums page draws the streaming albums and the Library page draws the shelf - the search box, the
  results, the mini player and the streamed songs. The coral dot on the switch is the only thing that
  changes colour. This replaces the third tab: nothing streaming has a page of its own any more.
- **A STREAMING ALBUM LOOKS LIKE AN ALBUM.** `scShelfGrid()` draws a two-column grid of square covers -
  the cover of the list's first song, or the album glyph when there is none - with the name and a song
  count, and a tile carries `data-name` into the same `scShelfOpenList()` page a downloaded album opens.
  The Albums page in streaming mode has **New album** in its own header; the shelf no longer repeats the
  albums as a row of chips, it has one **Streaming albums** row that switches to that page.
- **THE PLUS ASKS BOTH QUESTIONS.** A row's plus was one action - a playlist, named in a prompt - so no
  album could be started from the shelf. `scStreamAddTo()` opens the existing sheet with *Add to a
  playlist…* and *Add to an album…*; each of those opens `scStreamPickList()`, which offers the lists that
  exist (by name, with how many songs each holds) and, last, a new one that falls through to the same
  prompting maker as before.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.22 in one payload, `dev/patch-80623.py` (15 steps; a
  second run is a no-op, `--check` is 1 before and 0 after), and all seven inline scripts still compile.
  `dev/check-80623.cjs` passes **59 checks**: statically (the one rail that is built once and marked
  after, two pages and no streaming page, the switch with its two sources and one painter, no second
  `renderTabs()`/`renderList()` in the tab path, the albums-page branch gated on source *and* page, the
  tile grid, New album on that page, the shelf's way across to it, the plus opening two questions and the
  lists that exist, and the row title saying both) and **driven** in a `vm`: the grid draws one tile per
  album with the first song's cover, counts "2 songs" and "1 song", keeps the name, falls back to the
  glyph with no art, and says so when a kind is empty; the plus opens one sheet with a playlist and an
  album, the album question lists the albums that exist (`Road · 0 songs`), choosing one files the song in
  it marked `kind: 's'` and says where it went, the last choice makes a new one, the playlist question
  does the same for playlists, and a song that has left the shelf is refused. OTA rebuilt to a true fixed
  point - root + `ota/` **1164127** bytes at v80.6.23, `ota-play/` still HELD (**1138844** bytes).
  **Not claimed:** there is no phone and no browser here, so the rail was not tapped, the switch was never
  flipped with a thumb, and no grid was seen on a screen. What is verified is that the rail is one DOM
  tree that only changes class, that a page is painted once per tap, that the streaming set is chosen by
  source and page rather than by a page of its own, and that both kinds of list can be reached from a
  row's plus.
## 80.6.22 (October 30, 2026 · 5:20 PM EDT): the bar is the bar, and the lists hold both

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"make the streaming now bar match the one thier, remove the x button for it
  and make a 2 second hold to have a popup to delete, make it let you make albums like the actual
  downloaded albums things, and playlists, or in playlists you can have streaming playlists and
  downloaded playlists and same thing for albums"*. Four asks, and the last one is a data model rather
  than a control.
- **THE BAR WAS WEARING A COSTUME.** A streamed song wrote three extra things into the shared player bar:
  a **STREAM** pill before the artist, the length and genre appended to the artist line, and - from
  80.6.17's CSS - a coral top edge and a glowing disc. The deck writes `title` and `artist` and stops, so
  the bar changed shape the moment a song came from the source. It now writes exactly what the deck
  writes (`who.textContent = t.artist`), and the three `body.sc-stream-now` rules are gone. The class
  toggles stay (they are inert), so nothing else that tested for them changes.
- **WHY THE x HAD TO GO.** Every streaming row carried a close glyph at the end of the row, a few pixels
  from the row's own play target; a thumb reaching for a song deleted it. The glyph is removed from both
  row shapes (the shelf, and a playlist/album page) and nothing is wired to it any more.
- **TWO SECONDS, THEN A POPUP.** `scStreamHold()` puts a 2000ms pointer timer on each row and cancels it
  on pointerup, pointercancel, pointerleave and contextmenu. On fire it opens `scStreamMenu()` - a bottom
  sheet built from `document.createElement` (title, then Play, Add to a playlist, Add to an album, Add
  songs from your downloads, and Delete / Remove from this list, then Cancel). The click that follows a
  hold is swallowed in the capture phase, so a long press never also starts the song it was aimed at.
- **AN ALBUM IS A PLAYLIST THAT SAYS ALBUM.** Both are `{ name, items }`; playlists live under
  `streamPlaylists` and albums under a new `streamAlbums` key, restored through the same
  `scStreamRestore()` on boot (`scStreamLoad` now waits for three answers, not two). The shelf has a
  **New album** button beside **New playlist**, the two are listed as separate labelled rows of chips, and
  either opens as a page with how many songs it holds, **Add songs**, **Play all** and a held row per song.
- **ONE LIST CAN HOLD BOTH KINDS OF SONG.** An entry now carries `kind` - `'s'` for a song from the
  source, `'d'` for a file already on the device - and `scStreamPlItem()` keeps it. *Add songs* opens a
  picker over `allTracks`, and what it adds is a real entry (title, artist, length, cover, `kind: 'd'`).
  A list row for a file says **ON DEVICE**. A file is never deleted from the device by a list action:
  the shelf's action is *Delete this song*, a list's is *Remove from this album/playlist*.
- **THE ORDER ACROSS TWO PLAYERS.** This is the part that needed an owner. The stream advances inside
  `scStreamState.queue`; the deck advances inside `queue`/`queueIndex`; neither knows about the other. So
  `scMix` owns a mixed list: `scMixPlay(items, id)` sets the entries, `scMixGo(at)` hands each one to the
  player that can play it - a file goes to `playFromList()` **with the whole run of files in the list** (so
  the deck walks them itself), a streamed song goes to `scStreamPlay()` as a one-song queue. Two hooks
  close the loop: `scStreamNext()` asks the mix for the advance first, and `onEnded` does the same when the
  deck finishes the last file of the run (`pendingPlayId === scMix.lastFile`). An entry whose streamed song
  has left the shelf is skipped, not played, and the end of the list stops cleanly.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.21 in three chained payloads (`dev/patch-80622.py` runs
  `-b.py` then `-c.py`; the release ships them by being committed, and one 39 KB file does not survive that
  commit). 33 steps applied, a second run is a no-op, `--check` is 1 before and 0 after, and all seven
  inline scripts compile. `dev/check-80622.cjs` passes **51 checks**: statically (no pill, no pill string,
  no `scStreamMeta` on the bar line, no `body.sc-stream-now` rules, no `scs-del`/`scsp-del` markup or wiring,
  a 2000ms timer, both row shapes held, the popup's actions, the New album button and maker, `streamAlbums`
  read and written, albums listed beside playlists, `ON DEVICE`, and the two advance hooks) and **driven**,
  in a `vm`: a streamed song and a file join one list with both kinds marked, adding twice is one song,
  removing one leaves the other kind, a file survives a restore while an unresolvable stream is dropped,
  the open list resolves by kind, and the mix plays `stream s_1` -> `quiet` + `deck t_a` with `lastFile t_b`
  -> `deck t_b` -> `stream s_2` -> stop, skipping a streamed entry that left the shelf; the hold starts one
  2000ms timer, opens that row, and swallows the following tap. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point -
  root + `ota/` **1161444** bytes at v80.6.22, and `ota-play/` still HELD (**1138844** bytes). **Not
  claimed:** there is no phone and no browser here, so the bar was not seen, no row was held with a finger,
  and no mixed list was heard playing. What is verified is that the bar writes what the deck writes, that no
  row has a close target, that a hold and only a hold opens the popup, that the two stores round-trip, and
  that the mix hands each entry to the right player in order.
## 80.6.21 (October 30, 2026 · 7:26 AM EDT): streaming, made quick - and quiet

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"streaming is not efficient at all make that better it should be fast and
  easy to play dawg, and music shouldn't overlap with the downloaded music fix this and make it good,
  sources should never fail have like 10 backups, playback should be instant like how downloaded songs
  are"*. Three separate faults, and one of them was a half-fix I shipped myself.
- **WHY IT FELT SLOW.** Every song was an island: the resolver answered for the one song being tapped,
  the bytes were read for that song only, and nothing was remembered about the one after it. So Next -
  the most-used control in the app - paid the whole cost again: a player round trip, then a read. The
  only thing that made a song feel instant was the object-URL cache, three songs deep and twelve minutes
  long, which is shorter than one album.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** `scStreamPrefetch()` reads the **next** song into memory while the current one plays,
  using `scStreamReadOnly()` - a reader that never touches the element that is playing and never asks the
  resolver twice. The cache is **six songs, forty-five minutes**. A stream read is **six ranges at a time**
  instead of four (`scFetchBytes` now takes a lane count; the downloader's default is untouched), and the
  silent-link wait dropped from 2.4s to 1.1s, because the read already runs alongside the link and the
  old wait was mostly a pause before the fallback. One read at a time, always: a counter around
  `scStreamSource` means the read-ahead yields to a real play instead of competing with it.
- **WHY TWO SONGS COULD PLAY AT ONCE.** 80.6.17 paused the deck's **active** element when a stream took the
  bar - which is not the same as silencing the deck. The other element is the one a **crossfade** is already
  playing into; a track that ends can advance into it; `recoverAudio()` restarts whatever it likes. So a
  streamed song and a downloaded one could be heard together, and the owner heard exactly that.
  `scStreamQuietDeck()` now puts the deck to bed as a whole - both elements, the crossfade timer, the
  pending hand-off - on every path into the stream (`scStreamBarOn`, and the stream element's own `play`,
  so a resume after a pause counts too). And the rule holds from the other side: while the stream owns the
  bar, any deck element that starts playing is stopped again at once, and `recoverAudio()` returns instead
  of restarting local playback behind a stream.
- **WHY A SOURCE COULD STILL FAIL.** `scYtPlayer()` kept **three** audio rows and **two** muxed ones per
  player answer, and the element gave up after **one** retry - and that retry asked the resolver again
  before trying anything it already had. It now keeps **ten** audio rows and **four** progressive ones (the
  same player answer: no extra request, just more of what was already in it), retries up to **twelve**
  times, and walks the backups **first** - a dead URL costs the next candidate, not a fresh lookup.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.20: 16 steps applied, a second run is a no-op, and all
  seven inline scripts compile. `dev/check-80621.cjs` passes **51 checks**. Statically: six songs and
  forty-five minutes; six lanes threaded through the reader and the read-ahead; the read counter; the
  scheduled read-ahead; the whole-deck silence with the old half-silence gone; the deck listener and the
  recovery guard; ten and four rows; the twelve-retry ceiling and the backups-first order. **Driven**, in a
  `vm`: `scStreamQuietDeck()` pauses **both** elements, cancels the crossfade interval and drops the pending
  hand-off while the stream keeps its bar; the deck's own listener stops an element that plays behind the
  stream and leaves it alone when the stream does not own the bar; `scStreamReadOnly()` labels a muxed read
  audio and asks for six lanes; and `scStreamPrefetch()` resolves the next song, reads it six lanes wide,
  keeps the object URL under its video id, refuses to run while a read is in flight, and gives the URL back
  if that song became current. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1157300**
  bytes at v80.6.21, and `ota-play/` still HELD (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** there is no phone and
  no network here, so no song was streamed and no timing was measured on a device. The read-ahead is a
  scheduling change, not a promise of a number: what it removes is the resolve and the read on every Next
  after the first, and the honest way to see it is one album played straight through.
## 80.6.20 (October 29, 2026 · 11:10 PM EDT): the stream shows on the phone

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"streaming stuff should also show in widget and phone player in android"*.
  One omission, and it was structural rather than a missing call.
- **WHY NEITHER THE WIDGET NOR THE LOCK SCREEN EVER KNEW.** A stream is a **second `<audio>`
  element**. Every surface that feeds the phone - the media session, its MediaStyle notification, the
  quick-settings player, the lock screen and the home-screen widget - is driven from the app's own deck
  and its queue: `mediaSetMetadata(pushWidgetState)`, `mediaSetPlaybackState`, `mediaSetPositionState`,
  and the handlers in `registerMediaSessionHandlers()`. 80.6.17 taught the stream to take over
  `#nowPlaying`, and 80.6.19 taught it to carry a genre, but nothing ever told the phone. So a streamed
  song left the card on the last **local** song (or empty), and the widget kept drawing a song that was
  not playing while the phone actually made the stream's sound.
- **WHAT CHANGED - THE SAME RULE THE BAR GOT.** `scStreamPhoneOwns()` is the phone's answer to
  `scStreamBarOwns()`: while the stream owns the bar, it owns the phone. `scStreamPhoneTrack()` hands the
  phone the shape it already reads from a library track - title, artist and the cover the card draws
  (`scStreamThumb`, the ytimg thumbnail or the row's own) - so the metadata, the notification's artwork
  and the widget need no new native path. `scStreamPhoneSync()` pushes that song, its real playback
  state and its position in one call, and `scStreamPhoneTick()` keeps the clock and the widget's
  progress strip current from the stream element, throttled to once a second because `timeupdate` fires
  four times a second.
- **THE PHONE'S BUTTONS COME BACK INTO THE STREAM.** `scStreamPhoneArm()` registers all eight actions -
  play, pause, previous, next, stop, both thirty-second jumps and seek - and each one drives the stream
  element, not the deck: next goes through `scStreamNext()`, so the genre rule from 80.6.19 applies to a
  press on the lock screen exactly as it does inside the app; previous restarts the song past three
  seconds, which is the rule the deck already used; play on a stream whose source has gone starts it
  again rather than doing nothing.
- **AND THE DECK STANDS DOWN, ON PURPOSE.** Registering handlers once would not have held: the system
  rebuilds the session (after the service is released, after a WebView reload), and `refreshMediaControls()`
  re-arms the deck's handlers every minute and pushes the deck's own track. Both now open with a guard -
  while the stream owns the bar they arm the **stream** instead - which is what stops the buttons from
  silently flipping back mid-song. The deck's background heartbeat also stopped reviving the local
  element while a stream is up (`&& !scStreamPhoneOwns()`): two sounds at once behind the screen was the
  one thing worse than no card at all.
- **AND IT HANDS THE PHONE BACK.** `scStreamPhoneQuit()` runs when the stream gives the bar up: the deck's
  track returns to the card, the state reads paused, and the deck's handlers are re-armed - so a press
  after the stream ended does not aim at a song nobody can hear.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.19: 11 steps applied, a second run is a no-op, all
  seven inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80620.cjs` passes **56 checks**. Statically: the phone
  track carries title, artist and cover; every one of the eight actions is registered; both re-arm paths
  consult the stream **before** the deck; the widget timeline reads the stream element; the heartbeat
  guard is in place; the hand-back pushes the deck's card and re-arms its buttons. **Driven**, in a `vm`
  against a stub element: `__sync()` sends the streamed title first, then the state it is actually in,
  then all eight buttons; a `pause` press from the phone pauses the stream and `play` plays it; previous
  past three seconds rewinds instead of skipping; next calls `scStreamNext(1)`; the forward jump moves
  42s to 72s; stop pauses and rewinds; with the element's duration missing the phone is handed the song's
  real length; and `__quit()` puts the deck's song and handlers back. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true
  fixed point - root + `ota/` **1155531** bytes at v80.6.20, and `ota-play/` still HELD (**1138844**
  bytes). **Not claimed:** there is no phone here, so no APK was built and no notification, lock screen
  or home-screen widget was seen. The native side needed no change - the plugin and the widget provider
  already read these exact payloads (`title`, `artist`, `art`, `playing`, `pos`, `dur`), which is why
  this rides OTA - but whether a given launcher repaints the RemoteViews promptly is the device's
  business, not something this release can show.
## 80.6.19 (October 29, 2026 · 10:54 PM EDT): a stream that starts sooner, keeps its genre, and a rail that stays put

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"the streaming like getting the song to play should take much less time"*,
  *"should auto find a next song in that same genre"*, *"the horizontal scroll through genres should
  stay on what it was, not go back to the beginning"*, *"add more genres"*. Four fixes, one theme: the
  streaming page should behave like a player rather than a form.
- **WHY A STREAM TOOK SO LONG, IN THREE PARTS.** None of it was the source being slow:
  1. The read that always ends up playing the song started **only after the link had failed**. The link
     is the path a WebView is usually refused on (a 403 on the open-ended range), so the app paid for a
     failed request *and then* started reading.
  2. A link that loads metadata and then never decodes fires **no error at all**, so the app waited a
     fixed **six seconds** before deciding the link was quiet and reading instead.
  3. Nothing was kept. The same song played twice read twice, from zero.
- **WHAT CHANGED.** The read now begins **in the same tap as the link** - `beginRead()` is kicked off
  before the link is awaited, so when the link is refused the bytes are already moving, and when the
  link does play the read simply finishes into the cache. The silent-link wait is **2.4s**, not six.
  And the songs that have been read stay in memory as object URLs: the last **three**, for **twelve
  minutes**, with the oldest released when a fourth arrives. That makes a replay, a Previous, and a
  return to the song you just heard cost **no network at all** - it starts in the tap. The resolver's
  signed URL is also kept per song for its half-hour life, so Next does not pay for a resolution twice.
  The cache deliberately takes ownership of its URL (`scStreamState.blobUrl = ''` after a put) so the
  next read cannot revoke the copy a replay is about to use; Restart drops the copy it could not play
  before it tries again, so "try again" really is a fresh read.
- **NEXT KEEPS THE GENRE.** `scStreamNext()` now walks the queue for the next song **of the same
  genre** (the `genre` every row has carried since 80.6.17, or the genre the song was found under) and
  only falls back to the plain next when the queue holds no other song of that genre. The card shows
  the answer before it happens: an **Up next** row with the title and artist, one tap away, and when
  there is nothing else of that genre it shows **More <genre>** instead - one tap to search the genre
  again rather than pretending a next song exists. Automatic advance at the end of a song goes through
  the same function, so a genre carries from the first song to the last.
- **THE RAIL KEEPS ITS PLACE.** Every change rebuilds the streaming block with `innerHTML`, and a fresh
  row of tiles always landed back on the first tile - which read as the row "resetting". The rail now
  has an id, its scroll is read **before** the rebuild in `scStreamRender()` and handed back **after**
  it in `scStreamWire()`, and a `scroll` listener keeps the remembered value current as the owner
  swipes. It also snaps gently tile by tile (`scroll-snap-type: x proximity`), which is what makes a
  swipe feel deliberate rather than loose.
- **TWELVE MORE GENRES.** Amapiano, Reggaeton, Bollywood, Trap, Lo-fi, Soul, Funk, Metal, Blues, Disco,
  House and Workout join the rail - 27 built-in tiles in all, each with its own gradient and its own
  search, alongside the same **+ Genre** tile for the owner's own. The one genre that was removed
  stays removed.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.18 and driven by `dev/patch-80619.py`: 15 steps
  applied, a second run is a no-op, all seven inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80619.cjs` passes
  57 checks - statically (the cache read path, the parallel read ordered before the link, the 2.4s
  wait, the resolver cache, the genre walk, the Up next and More rows and their wiring, the rail's
  capture and restore and its scroll listener, the twelve new genres, the removed one still absent)
  and **behaviourally**, by running the cache and the genre walk in a `vm`: a put is remembered and
  the cache takes ownership of its URL; a fourth song evicts the oldest and **revokes exactly one**
  URL rather than leaking it; and `scStreamNext(1)` over a queue of Punjabi, Pop, Punjabi **skips the
  Pop song and takes the Punjabi one**, while a queue with nothing of that genre falls back to the
  plain next. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1154391** bytes at
  v80.6.19 publishing one honest line, and `ota-play/` still held at its published bundle
  (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** no phone and no browser here, so no song was heard and no
  stopwatch was run on a device. What is verified is the order of the operations (read started before
  the link is awaited, 2.4s instead of 6s, a cache hit before any network), the genre walk driven with
  real data, and the rail's scroll being written back after every rebuild.
## 80.6.18 (October 29, 2026 · 10:46 PM EDT): the web page says FullDev, and the genres are yours

- **WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR.** *"make the web version have fulldev after the SideCut"*, *"the full
  web version should also have dev after full"*, and *"have the regular genres with customizable genres
  that the ai can take and recommend song from those genres"*. Three changes, all inside the build that
  carries streaming.
- **THE WEB PAGE NAMES ITSELF.** On the web page the wordmark reads **SideCut FullDev** - the tag sits
  beside the name as a small coral pill, and the browser tab says the same thing. It is set from the
  page's own build flags (`SC_IS_WEB` and `SC_WEB_FULL`), so the installed app keeps its plain name and
  no other build grows a tag. It is a one-shot at boot, guarded against a missing header and against
  being applied twice.
- **ONE GENRE LEFT THE RAIL.** The rail no longer offers a genre the owner does not want. Nothing else
  about the built-ins changed: they are the same sixteen-minus-one gradient tiles, in the same order,
  with the same searches behind them.
- **THE RAIL IS THE OWNER'S AS WELL AS OURS.** A **+ Genre** tile at the end of the row asks for a name.
  It is tidied (one line, at most 24 characters), kept in `streamGenres`, and offered on the rail as a
  tile of its own - grey rather than a canned gradient, so an added genre reads as yours. Tapping it
  searches it exactly as a built-in does, the moment it is added. A long press (650ms) on a genre you
  added asks before taking it away; a long press on one that came with the app says so and removes
  nothing. The tap that follows a long press is swallowed, so removing a genre never also starts a
  search. The list is read back with the shelf, so it survives a restart with no migration step.
- **AND THE AI READS THEM.** **Recommended** now asks the AI first: it hands Gemini the whole rail -
  built-in genres and the ones you added - and asks for real songs across those tastes, as a small JSON
  list. Each title it names is then searched through the ordinary search path, so what comes back is
  the same kind of row a typed search produces, with the artist and the length, ready to add. It offers
  a few, not a wall, and says where they came from. Two honest fallbacks: with no Gemini key it
  recommends from the rail itself and says how to connect one; if the AI answers with nothing usable,
  it says that and leaves the tiles working. The list is also reachable by anything else that can ask,
  through `window.__scStreamGenres()`.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.17 and driven by `dev/patch-80618.py`: 15 steps
  applied, a second run is a no-op, all seven inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80618.cjs` passes
  55 checks - statically (the tag and its three guards, the removed genre, the + tile and its wiring,
  the long press and its swallowed tap, the stored list and its load, the AI call reading the key and
  the model the app already holds, the fallbacks) and **behaviourally**, by running `scStreamGenres()`
  and `scStreamGenreName()` in a `vm` over a messy saved list: the built-ins come first, an added genre
  is offered, a duplicate in different case is not added twice, an empty entry is ignored, spaces are
  tidied, a long name is capped at 24 characters, an added genre searches its own name, and the line
  handed to the AI shortens itself. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/`
  **1151658** bytes at v80.6.18 publishing one honest line, and `ota-play/` still held at its
  published bundle (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** no browser and no phone here, so the tag was
  not seen on screen and no AI answer was received. What is verified is that the rail builds from the
  saved list, that the tag is gated on the web flags, and that the recommendation path hands the
  genres to the AI and the answer back through the search that already works.
## 80.6.17 (October 29, 2026 · 10:37 PM EDT): the stream takes the player bar, and genres to browse

- **WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR.** *"show in the now bar and stuff if your streaming the song"*, *
  "make the experience feel amazing Spotify like with a main genre or multiple genre topics"*, and
  *"make it nice and non glitchy"*. All three are the same complaint underneath: a streamed song was
  something that happened inside a card halfway up the Library, not something the app was *playing*.
- **THE STREAM NOW OWNS THE BAR.** When a stream starts, the bar at the bottom stops showing the last
  downloaded song and shows the stream: the cover on the disc (the same artwork the row carries, with
  the video-id fallback, so nothing is ever a black square), the title, `artist · length`, and a small
  **STREAM** pill so there is never a doubt which kind of song is playing. The disc spins while it
  plays and stops when it pauses.
- **AND THE BAR'S BUTTONS DRIVE IT.** Play/pause toggles the stream. Next skips to the next song in
  the queue the stream was started from. Previous restarts the song if it is more than three seconds
  in and goes back if it is not - the behaviour every player has. Dragging the seek bar seeks the
  stream, and the drag is held out of the clock's hands exactly as the local player's is, so the thumb
  no longer jumps back under the finger. The disc's progress ring and the mini bar follow the same
  clock.
- **ONE SOUND AT A TIME.** Starting a stream pauses the local player, and starting a local song stops
  the stream and takes the bar back. Before this, both could be playing at once and the bar showed a
  song that was not the one you could hear.
- **THE GLITCH WAS THE PLAY PATH REDRAWING THE PAGE.** `scStreamAudio()` rebuilt the whole streaming
  block - `innerHTML`, every wiring, the scroll - on every `play` and every `pause` event, because the
  card's own button was drawn from `scStreamState.playing`. A pause therefore reset the card's
  position and its own seek line, which is exactly the flicker and the jumping the owner is asking
  about. Play and pause now update the button, the icon and the clock **in place**; the page is only
  rebuilt when the list itself changes.
- **GENRES, AS A RAIL YOU CAN SWIPE.** Above the search there is a **Browse** row of sixteen gradient
  tiles - Pop, Hip-Hop, R&B, Afrobeats, Punjabi, Latin, Rock, Electronic, K-Pop, Indie, Country, Jazz,
  Chill, Dance, Old School, Gospel. A tile is a search of the source, not a list bundled into the app:
  tapping one asks for that genre and shows the answers where search results always appear. The
  chosen genre is ringed, and one tap on its name clears it. A song added while browsing a genre keeps
  that genre, and it is shown on the row as `artist · 3:12 · Pop`, so the topics survive the search
  that found them. Playlist copies keep the genre too, and playlists saved before this release fill it
  in from the song they point at, with no migration step.
- **RESULTS SAY WHO AND HOW LONG.** The result rows read the artist field the search actually sends
  and append its length, so two versions of the same song can be told apart before either is added.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.16 and driven by `dev/patch-80617.py`: 19 steps
  applied, a second run is a no-op, all seven inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80617.cjs` passes
  - statically (who owns the bar, the five buttons wired to the stream, the clock feeding the bar,
  the sixteen genres, the genre kept on a row and filled into old playlist copies, the CSS that marks
  a streaming bar) and **behaviourally**, by running `scStreamBarSync()` in a `vm` against a stub DOM
  at 60 seconds of a 240-second song: the clock reads `1:00` and `4:00`, the bar sits at 25% with a
  matching fill, the disc ring is at the matching offset, the disc spins, the icons are a pause glyph,
  and after a pause they flip to a play glyph and the disc stops. Switching `barOn` off shows a local
  song's bar is never written by the stream. `scStreamRowMeta()` is driven the same way and returns
  `Diljit · 1:35 · Punjabi`. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1148545**
  bytes at v80.6.17 publishing one honest line, and `ota-play/` still held at its published bundle
  (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** no song was heard and no bar was seen on a device - there is
  no phone and no browser here. What is verified is that the stream writes the bar, that the bar's
  buttons call the stream, and that pausing no longer rebuilds the page.
## 80.6.16 (October 29, 2026 · 10:24 PM EDT): a stream that tries every copy, and rows that keep their cover

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"the streaming stuff isn't working and keeps giving source errors"*, *"it
  should have metadata with track covers"*, and a screenshot of the card with the readout on it:
  `webm · 3.5 MB · read · error 4 · the source sent no bytes`. That line is what turned this release from
  another guess into a diagnosis - it named the copy that was tried and the step that refused it.
- **THE READ ONLY EVER TRIED ONE COPY.** `scYtPlayer()` - the resolver the **downloader** also uses -
  ranks itag 251 (`webm`/opus) first and hands back the m4a rows and the progressive muxed copy behind
  it as `alts`. The downloader walks that list (`scFetchDecode` → `scStreamUsable` → `scFetchBytes`) and
  has never had trouble; `scStreamSource()` read `alts` into the state and then called `scFetchBytes`
  on the first URL only, so a single refused range ended the song. The readout's `webm` is exactly that
  first rank. The read now walks the same list in the same order, keeps the mime and size of whichever
  copy answered, labels a muxed copy `audio/mp4`, and still puts the downloader's `__scCancelDl` flag
  back on every exit.
- **"THE SOURCE SENT NO BYTES" WAS A FALLBACK, NOT A FINDING.** `scFetchRange()` returned
  `{bytes:null,status:403}` from both the native and the page branch without writing anything to
  `window.__scHttpWhy`, so the readout had no step to name and the card printed the fallback. Both
  branches now record the status (`the source answered 403`, `the page request answered 502`) and a
  request that never answered says so, so the next screenshot names the refusal itself.
- **THE ROWS HAD NO METADATA BECAUSE THEY READ THE WRONG FIELDS.** `scYtSearch()` returns
  `{videoId, title, owner, duration, score}` and now `thumb` as well; `scStreamAddResult()` was reading
  `it.author || it.channel` and `it.lengthText`, neither of which is in that answer - so every row was
  saved with an empty artist, `dur` 0 and an empty `thumb`, which is the black square and the word
  "Streaming" standing in for the artist. It now reads `owner`, a numeric `duration` (seconds, with the
  text form still accepted) and the cover, and `scStreamThumb()` falls back to
  `https://i.ytimg.com/vi/<videoId>/mqdefault.jpg`, so rows saved before this release fill in on their
  own with no request and no migration. The now-playing card shows a 44px cover beside the title with
  `artist · length` under it (`scStreamMeta()`), and the readout row carries `padding-right:46px` so
  the floating rail no longer sits on top of Restart.
- **THE PAGE OPENS AT ITS TOP.** The shelf owns the scroll and keeps it, so coming back to Streaming
  after reading to the bottom showed a card whose title, badge and New playlist button were already
  above the fold - which reads as a page that lost its header. `scShelfOpenTab('streaming')` now sets
  the shelf's `scrollTop` to 0.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.15 and driven by `dev/patch-80616.py`: every step
  applied, a second run is a no-op, all inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80616.cjs` passes -
  statically (the walk, the status reasons, the field names, the cover fallback, the rail untouched)
  and **behaviourally**, by running `scStreamSource()` in a `vm` against a stub reader: a refused first
  copy is followed by the second and the second one plays, a muxed copy is labelled audio, a total
  failure names the 403, and `__scCancelDl` is restored on both paths. `scStreamMeta()` is driven the
  same way for the card line. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true fixed point - root + `ota/` **1145722**
  bytes at v80.6.16 publishing one honest line, and `ota-play/` still held at its published bundle
  (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** no song was heard playing and no cover was seen on a device -
  there is no phone and no browser here. What is verified is that every candidate is now tried, that a
  refusal names its status, and that a row carries artist, length and a cover that always resolves.
## 80.6.15 (October 29, 2026 · 9:46 PM EDT): three icons on the right, and a silent link that gets read

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"make the 3 streaming, albums and library tabs icons on the right hand side
  hovering over ... smooth and nice and smallish ... that layout shouldn't get touched"* - and, in the
  same breath, *"streaming does not work"*.
- **THE RAIL LEFT THE SONG'S SPACE.** Streaming, Library and Albums were a row of full-width pills, so
  three words cost a band of the screen and pushed the list down to pay for it. They are one small
  column of glyphs now - waveform, ruled lines, grid - fixed to the right edge at 32px, floating over
  the songs with a blurred, hairline edge. The rail is `position:fixed`, so it takes no room in the
  page: the shelf, the list, the scroll and the bottom inset are exactly as they were, which is what
  "that layout shouldn't get touched" has to mean in practice.
- **IT ONLY CATCHES ITS OWN TAPS.** The rail container is `pointer-events:none` and only the glyphs are
  targets, so a press in the gaps or in the rail's padding goes through to the song underneath it. The
  active page is a filled circle; the change is eased over .22s, a press scales to .9, and a
  reduced-motion setting removes the easing. `data-shelf` and `scShelfOpenTab()` are untouched - the
  three pages switch exactly as they did - and the word each circle hides is still its `aria-label`
  and its long-press title.
- **A LINK THAT STARTS AND THEN SAYS NOTHING.** The one failure that produces "nothing happens" with
  no error anywhere: a player resolves `play()`, loads the metadata, and then decodes no bytes and
  fires no `error` at all. The row sits at 0:00 and there is nothing to report. Six seconds with no
  progress on the same song now hands it to the read path - the same bounded-range read the downloader
  already uses - and the card's line says *the link went quiet* so the next screenshot names it.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.14 and driven by `dev/patch-80615.py`: every step
  applied, a second run is a no-op, all inline scripts compile, and `dev/check-80615.cjs` passes - the
  rail is fixed at 32px with only its glyphs tappable, the three glyphs are drawn at the requested size

## 80.6.14 (October 29, 2026 · 9:37 PM EDT): the stream is started, and the row says where it stopped

- **WHAT THE OWNER SAID.** *"streaming is not workifn"* - one sentence, after three releases that
  each answered it with a theory. This one answers with mechanics, and leaves a readout on screen.
- **THE ELEMENT WAS NEVER IN THE PAGE.** `scStreamAudio()` built an `<audio>`, kept it in a closure and
  played an object URL on it; the app's own player keeps both of its elements in the document. A
  WebView is free to treat a detached element differently for load, autoplay and decode, and that is
  not something a stream can be asked to survive. It is appended when it exists - 0x0, off-screen,
  `pointer-events:none` - `preload` is `auto` rather than `none`, and its `loadedmetadata` is watched so
  the card knows when there is something to play.
- **THE LINK IS TRIED FIRST, IN THE TAP.** A media element is not held to CORS, so the direct URL is
  the shortest path to sound; the previous release fetched the whole 3.4 MB before it handed anything
  to the element, which on a phone is indistinguishable from nothing happening. `scStreamStart()` sets
  the source, calls `load()` and calls `play()` inside the caller's gesture. When the element refuses
  that link - googlevideo answers 403 to the open-ended range a media element opens with - the song is
  read in bounded ranges and played from an object URL, which is the order the two mechanisms actually
  want.
- **THE READER NO LONGER GIVES UP ON A SHAPE IT DOES NOT KNOW.** `__scCapHttp()` can answer 206 with
  data this page cannot decode; `scFetchRange()` then returned "206, no bytes", which ended the whole
  read instead of falling through to the page fetch. That success status now falls through, and
  `scHttpDataToBytes()` accepts typed arrays, plain arrays and wrapped replies as well as base64.
- **AND THE CARD SAYS WHERE IT STOPPED.** One dim line under the transport: the stream's type and size,
  which path carried it (`link` or `read`), how many bytes were read, the element's `error.code` and
  `readyState`, and the transport's own reason (`window.__scHttpWhy`). A **Restart** button sits beside
  it and starts the song again from a fresh gesture, clearing the object URL and the resolver's cached
  link first. A screenshot of that line is a diagnosis instead of a report.
- **WHAT WAS RUN.** Built on a fresh clone of 80.6.13 and driven by `dev/patch-80614.py`: every step
  applied, a second run is a no-op, **all 7 inline scripts compile**, and `dev/check-80614.cjs` passes -
  the element is appended and preloaded, the link is tried before the read, a 206 with unreadable bytes
  falls through to fetch, the readout reports type, size, path, element state and transport reason, and
  the pure functions are **executed**: base64, typed array, plain array and wrapped replies all decode,
  while `null` and an unknown object stay unread rather than guessed at. The OTA pair rebuilt to a true
  fixed point - root + `ota/` **1143078** bytes at v80.6.14 publishing one honest line, and `ota-play/`
  still held at its published bundle (**1138844** bytes). **Not claimed:** playback was not heard. What
  changed is that the page now starts the element the way the app's own player does, tries the two
  mechanisms in the order that can work, and prints the reason when neither does.

  `scShelfPage(on)` - that decides which of the two is up, so no caller can leave the list hidden
  behind a shelf that was closed. The scrim is `display:none`, and the shelf is no longer announced to

  patched one, so CORS is not the limiter; on the web the plain URL is still the **last** try, so a
  source that allows it plays and nothing that worked before stops working. A song already buffered is
  played from its object URL rather than fetched twice, the resolver's mime is kept on
  `scStreamState.mime`, and the load reports *"Loading the song… 42%"* instead of looking dead.

  them belongs in front of the build that never asked for it: the root channel's notes now publish

## 80.6.9 (October 29, 2026 · 7:24 PM EDT): Streaming, experimental

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"try to see if streaming is a possibility like streaming the song, and
  in library build a section in the beginning for streaming and a separate section for downloaded songs
  just try it mark it as experimental see if you can do it tho and I should be able to make streaming
  song playlists and stuff too"*.
- **WHAT IS POSSIBLE, AND WHY.** The page already reaches YouTube for search (`scYtSearch`) and already
  speaks the InnerTube player endpoint to get signed media URLs (`scHttpJson`, used by the converter).
  A stream is that same signed URL handed straight to an `<audio>` element instead of being fetched,
  decoded and written as a file — which is why this release is a section and a small module rather than
  a new pipeline.
- **THE GATE IS `!SC_IS_PLAY`.** `SC_IS_PLAY` is the Play build (native Play APK, or the web page that
  is not the full one), so `SC_STREAM_OK` is true in the **full APK and full web only**. That is not
  only a policy choice: `scYtSearch()` answers with legal/sample search on the Play build, so a
  streaming section there would search one catalogue and try to play from another. On the Play build
  the block is never built and `scStreamBoot()` returns before it touches the DOM.
- **IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE PLAYER.** A stream gets its own `Audio` element inside the block. It never
  enters `queue`, `allTracks`, `queueIndex`, `activeAudio()`, the widget, the media session or the
  notification. This is the single most important decision in the release: the existing player assumes
  every track is a local file with a blob and a length, and a stream that dies inside it would take
  playback, the widget and the resume state with it. `dev/check-8069.cjs` asserts the module never
  assigns `queueIndex` or `allTracks` and that its audio element is created by the module itself.
- **THE TWO LIBRARY SECTIONS.** `<div id="scStreamBlock"></div>` is inserted as a **sibling above**
  `#listPane`, not inside it: that pane is rewritten on every library render (search keystroke, tab
  change, sort), so anything inside it would be destroyed on the next keystroke. The block paints the
  streaming header, its search, its songs and its playlists, then a **"Downloaded songs"** heading —
  the downloaded list keeps rendering underneath, under its own label.
- **STREAMING PLAYLISTS ARE SEPARATE DATA.** `streamTracks` and `streamPlaylists` are their own meta
  keys; a streaming playlist holds stream ids (`s_<videoId>`), and `scStreamPlAdd` is a no-op for a
  song already in a playlist. Removing a song from a playlist that empties it deletes the playlist,
  because a zero-length chip is a dead control.
- **THE EXPIRY IS THE FEATURE THAT KEEPS IT ALIVE.** A googlevideo URL is signed and dies.
  `scStreamStale(at, now)` calls a URL dead after thirty minutes (and treats a missing timestamp or a
  clock that went backwards as dead rather than fresh); the `error` handler re-resolves the **same
  videoId** once and resumes at the position it was on, so the song never changes under the listener.
  A source that cannot be re-resolved says so in the row instead of failing silently.
- **PICKING A ROW.** `scStreamPickUrl()` reads the two format pools and prefers opus 251 over m4a 141
  over m4a 140 over any other audio row; a `signatureCipher` row is skipped rather than handed to the
  audio element, because this path does not solve ciphers, and a video row is never chosen for a song.
- **WHAT THE PAGE PATCH TOUCHES.** `dev/patch-8069.py`, one step: the seat above `#listPane`, the
  module and its boot retry, the changelog head, `APP_VERSION` and the shell cache to
  `sidecut-shell-v80.6.9`.
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, AND THIS ONE MATTERS.** The stream path was **not** played end to end: that
  needs a network route to googlevideo and a device, and neither exists in the session that wrote this.
  What IS proven, by `dev/check-8069.cjs` (39 assertions, driving the shipped functions): the gate
  refuses the Play build in three separate places, the row picker prefers 251 > 141 > 140, skips
  cipher-only and video rows, the thirty-minute expiry rule and its two degenerate cases behave, the
  playlist add/remove/empty cases are right, the seat is above `#listPane` and empty until the module
  fills it, the streaming stores are separate keys and a streaming song is never written into the
  downloaded library, and every inline script on the page still compiles. If the first real tap on a
  stream fails, the row now says which failure it was — that is the part to read before changing
  anything in the resolver. The OTA bundles reach a true fixed point in the release step — root +
  `ota/` **1135886** bytes, `ota-play/` **1135895** bytes, both `--check`s OK at v80.6.9.
## 80.6.8 (October 29, 2026 · 7:03 PM EDT): Every word lands on the voice, and none can be skipped

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"lyrics are incorrect fix them they should be 100 percent correct
  flowing to the next word dawg"*. "Correct" here is the second clause: the words flow to the next
  word, in time, one at a time. Four faults were producing exactly the wrongness described, and all
  four live in the pacer.
- **THE SHEET'S OWN WORD STAMPS WERE BEING THROWN AWAY.** Enhanced LRC stamps the word it starts:
  `[00:12.00]<00:12.00>Hello <00:12.62>world`. `SC_LRC_TAG_SRC` has always MATCHED those stamps - its
  bracket forms include the angle ones - so `formatSyncedLyrics` stripped them out of the row with the
  line stamps and kept the text. The row printed correctly and every word in it was paced by a
  syllable guess. `scLrcBody()` now takes the repeated-line stamps off and leaves the inline ones in,
  `scWordParts()` splits what is left into pacing units carrying the stamp that introduced each of
  them, and the render writes it onto the span as `data-word-at`. `scSheetWordStarts()` reads those
  back on every frame and the pacer uses them **verbatim**. A word between two stamps takes its own
  syllable share of the gap, so a sheet that stamps only the long words still moves at the phrase's
  own pace. A sheet with no stamps is unchanged in every respect.
- **THE MEASUREMENT COULD NEVER APPLY TO SUCH A SHEET.** `scWordMeasureKick()` counts the words of
  each row from `scParseLrcLines()`'s text, which still carried the inline stamps, so a stamp was
  counted as a word; the count then disagreed with the number of spans drawn, and
  `scMeasuredWordStarts()` refuses a record whose count disagrees (it compares them on purpose). So a
  sheet with stamps was paced by the guess that the same song had already been measured to replace.
  The stamps are stripped **at that count** now - not in `scParseLrcLines()`, which also feeds the
  line-up writer, and that writer must not lose a sheet's own stamps when it rebuilds it.
- **A WORD COULD BE SKIPPED OUTRIGHT.** The pacer asked *which word's window contains now*, and a
  window is only as wide as the gap to the next start. Two words clamped onto one rise, or a fast
  line, made windows of a few hundredths of a second - narrower than the 50 ms poll - so those words
  were never lit: the highlight jumped. `scPickLitIdx()` asks the other question, **the last start the
  playhead has passed**, and walking a list of starts forward cannot skip one. `dev/check-8068.cjs`
  drives the shipped function over a 5 ms sweep and asserts it never goes backwards and that a 50 ms
  window is still picked at the 50 ms poll.
- **A LINE COULD SIT DARK.** When a measurement put a line's first rise later than the line's own
  stamp, nothing was lit until that rise arrived - the current row sat there with no lit word at all.
  It lights its first word for that stretch now.
- **AND THE TAIL.** `scWordStartsForWindow()` clamped every word past the end of the window onto `to`
  **itself**, so a line that ran a little long came out with several words sharing one instant: those
  words had no stretch of their own and were the ones being stepped over. The tail is pulled back from
  the end with room between the words instead (`gapMin`), and a final pass forces strict order.
- **THE LIGHT GLIDES.** The word transition goes from a 15 ms linear snap to 220 ms on the app's own
  `cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1)`, so the highlight travels to the next word instead of jumping onto
  it. Letter mode's per-letter curve is untouched.
- **WHAT THE PAGE PATCH TOUCHES.** `dev/patch-8068.py`, one step: the words the measurement counts,
  the render, the five helpers inserted at the head of `scPaceWords`, the pick, the window tail, the
  two transitions, the changelog head, `APP_VERSION`, and the shell cache to `sidecut-shell-v80.6.8`.
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No phone, no APK, no listening test - the pacing was not judged by ear, and
  the onset-derived starts are only as good as the recording's envelope. What IS proven, by
  `dev/check-8068.cjs` (52 assertions, and it RUNS the shipped code rather than reading it): the row
  body and the stamped words are parsed and spelled exactly, an unstamped sheet still hands the line
  back to the recording, the starts of a mixed sheet are ordered and inside their own gap, a rewind
  stamp is pulled forward, the pick never goes backwards and never skips a 50 ms window, the window's
  tail keeps every start distinct even at 24 words in half a second, and every inline script on the
  page still compiles. The OTA bundles reach a true fixed point in the release step - root + `ota/`
  **1129497** bytes, `ota-play/` **1129508** bytes, both `--check`s OK at v80.6.8.

## 80.6.4 (October 28, 2026 · 9:11 PM EDT): the tab transition waits for a visible page, and stops leaking its aborts

- **THE BUG THE OWNER PHOTOGRAPHED.** A red strip across the top of the app reading
  `SideCut error: Transition was aborted because of invalid state. Document hidden`. That message is
  Chrome's, not the app's: `navigate()` runs the view swap inside `document.startViewTransition()`
  (80.3.6), and Chrome aborts a view transition when the page is hidden as it starts or goes hidden
  while it runs. It reports the abort by **rejecting the transition's promises** - starting with `ready`.
- **WHY IT REACHED THE SCREEN.** The wrapper caught `finished` only. So `ready`'s rejection had no owner,
  became an `unhandledrejection`, and the boot banner (line 7491) prints unhandled rejections in full.
  A backgrounded app is the normal case on Android, which is why it kept happening: tap a tab as you
  leave the app and the abort is guaranteed.
- **THE FIX IS THREE THINGS IN ONE FUNCTION.** (1) **The door**: a page whose `visibilityState` is not
  `visible` never starts a transition - it takes the plain `navigate()` path, which is the same door
  reduced motion already used. Nothing to abort. (2) **The leak**: `ready`, `updateCallbackDone` and
  `finished` each get a `catch`, so an abort is handled however late it lands. (3) **The lost tap**: an
  abort can land *before* the update callback ran, which means the DOM never swapped and the tap went
  nowhere - the callback now records that it ran, and a navigation that was swallowed is replayed
  outside the transition, guarded by the same flag so a swap that did happen is never done twice.
- **THE ANIMATION IS NOT CHANGED.** Same tokens, same duration and curve, same arrival for a pane's
  first paint, same two reduce-motion switches. This release only decides *whether* a transition may
  start and what happens to the promise it hands back.
- **VERIFIED BY CAUSING THE ABORT, NOT BY GREPPING FOR THE FIX.** `python3 dev/patch-8064.py` (1 step)
  then `--check` (0 steps); **every inline script block parses** (7 blocks); `dev/check-8064.cjs`
  passes **22/22**. It slices the page's own navigation IIFE out of `index.html` (not a copy), runs it in
  a vm against a fake `document`, and drives it with a **process-level `unhandledRejection` counter
  standing in for the banner**: a hidden page starts no transition and still navigates once; a normal
  swap starts one and runs it once; an abort on `ready` raises **no** unhandled rejection and does not
  repeat the swap; an abort **before** the update callback still lands the navigation, exactly once, and
  leaks nothing; reduce motion still skips the transition. It then asserts the shape - the visibility
  door, all three owned promises, the guarded replay, the absent lone-`finished` catch - and that the
  run as a whole left no rejection behind. The same driver run against the **pre-patch page** fails
  **8/22**, including `the whole run left no unhandled rejection - Transition was aborted because of
  invalid state. Document hidden`, which is the screenshot's own message: the check is known to fail on
  the bug and pass on the fix, not merely to pass. The OTA bundles reach a true fixed point in the
  release step - root + `ota/` **1123604** bytes, `ota-play/` **1123618** bytes, both `--check`s OK at
  v80.6.4.
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No phone: that the strip is gone on the device it was photographed on. What is
  proven is that the exact rejection that produced it is now owned and cannot reach the `unhandledrejection`
  listener, and that the swallowed-navigation case still switches tabs. Nothing moved in the glass, the
  widget, the player, the library, the lyrics or the audio graph.

## 80.6.2 (October 28, 2026 · 7:18 PM EDT): plain notes, and a settings strip that scrolls like paper

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"horizontal scroll in settings should be smooth and what the hell are
  these grater than symbols with a b then a less then symbol in the patch notes remove all of those form
  patch notes"*. Two bugs, unrelated, fixed together.
- **THE TAGS IN THE NOTES.** Changelog notes are allowed to carry emphasis — **171 of them in this page do**
  — but every panel escapes the note before it paints it (`escapeHtml(brief)` in `scClItemHtml`,
  `escapeHtml(i)` in the What's new summary, the glance line in the update log). So `<b>Settings</b>`
  reached the screen as literal characters and `&mdash;` arrived as its own name. The escaping is right and
  stays — notes are data. What was missing was a cleaner in front of it.
- **ONE CLEANER, ONE PLACE.** `scNoteText()` drops the emphasis tags the changelog uses, turns a
  placeholder like `lyricWords_<track>` into `lyricWords_track`, decodes the dozen entities the notes use,
  and decodes `&amp;` **last** so a note that legitimately says `&amp;lt;` cannot become a tag after the
  pass. `scClBrief()` runs every note through it, so bullets, the collapsed glance, the update counts and
  the What's new popup all get the same plain sentence — old history included, not just the new entry.
- **THE ONE EXCEPTION, DELIBERATELY.** A note that quotes markup as an example — *"a window.open or an
  `<a target="_blank">`"* — keeps its brackets: it is describing code, and reads wrong without them. The
  check allows exactly that and nothing else.
- **THE SNAP WAS THE STICKY FEELING.** The settings strip had `scroll-snap-type: x proximity` with a
  centred snap point per tab; on a slow drag the snap re-engaged repeatedly and tugged the strip out from
  under the finger. It is `none` now: the strip keeps the platform's momentum and stays where the finger
  leaves it. The tab you OPEN still glides to the centre — `scTabIntoView()` already asked for a smooth
  scroll, and the strip now carries `scroll-behavior: smooth` for it. The dock at the bottom of the app and
  the pinned-artists row keep their own snapping; this release never touched them.
- **A TAB IS A DRAG HANDLE.** The children claim `touch-action: pan-x` and refuse `-webkit-user-drag` and
  text selection, so a swipe that starts on a tab moves the row instead of turning the tab into a ghost
  image or doing nothing.
- **A GUARD IN THIS RELEASE WAS DEAD, AND IS FIXED.** The driver's `GONE` list — the "the page must not
  still carry this" half of its own proof — was defined and then never run, and two of its entries (the
  proximity snap) are true of other rows in the app, so a global check would have failed honestly. The loop
  is wired in front of the write now, its entries are the version constant, and the snap assertions are
  scoped to the `#settingsTabStrip` block. The release entry says so rather than quietly tidying it.
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** `python3 dev/patch-8062.py` (1 step) then `--check` (0 steps); every
  inline script block parses; and `node dev/check-8062.cjs` pulls the page's own `scNoteText()` /
  `scClBrief()` out of `index.html` and **runs every note in the CHANGELOG through them** — briefs and
  details, 400-odd strings — asserting that no emphasis tag and no named entity survives and that no note

- **IT SHIPS OVER THE AIR.** OTA root **1121683 bytes**, store channel **1121693 bytes**; the APK the
  widget runs in does not change.
