- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"add a transparent frosted type widgit with a frosted adjustable thing
  so you can tune it"*. One nineteenth preset, first in the list, and one 0-100 dial that owns its look.
- **THE GLASS IS REAL TRANSPARENCY, NOT A PICTURE OF IT.** `WIDGET_THEMES.frost` is an ordinary opaque
  preset with `glass: true`. At push time `scFrostGlass()` turns its two background stops into
  `#AARRGGBB`, which is what the native provider feeds `Color.parseColor` and `LinearGradient` — the
  bitmap is `ARGB_8888` and the widget root has no background of its own, so the wallpaper genuinely
  shows through the panel. No bridge call, no new native key, no APK rebuild: the page already pushes the
  theme object on every heartbeat.
- **WHAT THE WIDGET CANNOT DO, SAID PLAINLY.** A RemoteViews widget cannot blur what is behind it — there
  is no backdrop filter and no way to read the wallpaper. So the "frost" is the milk in the glass: the
  panel is mixed toward white, and both the mix and the opacity follow the dial. The blur exists in the
  preview only, because a browser is the one place it can.
- **THE DIAL.** `widgetFrost`, 0-100, default 55, kept in `localStorage` (`sidecut_widgetFrost`) and clamped
  on read so a hand-edited store cannot ask for a colour the layout has no shape for. Opacity runs
  0.44 → 0.88 and the white mix 0.12 → 0.40 on the first stop, 0.04 → 0.18 on the second, so 0 is a thin
  pane the wallpaper tints and 100 is a soft near-solid one. `input` repaints the preview only; `change`
  pushes once, so a drag is one bridge call rather than sixty.
- **THE DIAL IS HIDDEN, NOT DISABLED, ON THE OTHER PRESETS.** The row shows only when the preset is glass
  and the widget is not following the app theme (following it replaces the preset with the app's own
  colours, so the dial would tune a glass that is not being drawn). The eighteen existing presets keep the
  exact panel they had — `getWidgetTheme()` only routes through the glass when the merged theme says so.
  Fine-tune still wins over the preset: an override keeps its colour and simply gains the glass.
- **THE PREVIEW GREW A BACKDROP.** The tile moved into `scWidgetPreviewBody()` so both branches paint the
  same widget; the glass branch draws it over a strip of colour with `backdrop-filter`, so the dial has
  something to act on and the panel visibly blurs. The opaque branch is what it was in 80.5.2.
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** `python3 dev/patch-806.py` (1 step) then `--check` (0 steps);
  **every inline script block parses**; and `node dev/check-806.cjs` extracts the page's own
  `scFrostGlass()` (the function text, not a copy) and drives it at frost 0/55/100 — ARGB shape, alpha
  ordering thin→thick, both ends still translucent, white rising with the dial, dark type at every level,
  CSS getting `rgba()` and never ARGB. 29/29 green, including the dial's wiring and the cache name.
- **IT SHIPS OVER THE AIR.** OTA root **1119544 bytes**, store channel **1119552 bytes**; the APK the
  widget runs in does not change.

## 80.5 (October 28, 2026 · 3:39 PM EDT): the converters leave the web page, and the full web app gets its own link

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"have the converters only on the full build apk version not web
  version either, make a seperate web version with the converters on a different URL with full attached
  to it"*. Three builds, spelled out: the **full APK** keeps every converter; the **web page** is now the
  files-you-own build; and the same web app **with** the converters lives at **`/full/`**.
- **NO SECOND HIDER WAS WRITTEN.** Since 60.5 the page has already shipped as two builds from one file:
  CI injects `window.__PLAY_BUILD__` into the store AAB and the page then removes `convToolsCard`,
  `spCardDisc`, `ytCardDisc` and the Settings copies, rewrites Discover's how-to and gates around twenty
  entry points on `SC_IS_PLAY`. This release makes `SC_IS_PLAY` mean what every one of those gates has
  always read it as - *this build offers no converter* - and makes a plain web page qualify. One
  definition rather than twenty edits, and the web page inherits a removal path that has shipped for
  months instead of a newer one that has not.
- **THE STORE BUILD KEEPS ITS OWN FLAG.** Billing, the `ota-play/` update channel and the Play label are
  properties of the copy Google Play distributed, not of "no converters", so they move to
  `SC_PLAY_NATIVE` - the injected flag itself. Without that split, dropping the tools from the web page
  would also have dropped its card-page tips and pointed it at a bundle it does not have.
- **THE INSTALLED APP IS NEVER A WEB PAGE.** The WebView serves the bundle from `https://localhost`, so
  "is this the web" cannot be the protocol. It is `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` first, then the host:
  loopback, an IP literal or a `.local` name is a machine talking to itself (a local preview) and keeps
  the tools. A context that cannot answer keeps them too, on purpose - a player that quietly loses its
  converter is the one outcome this must never produce.
- **`/full/` IS A DOOR, NOT A SECOND COPY.** `full/index.html` is served beside the app and replaces
  itself with `../?full=1` on load, so the converters cost about 6 KB of HTML instead of a duplicate
  3.7 MB page that every release would have to keep in step. `?full`, `?full=1`, `?build=full` and a
  `/full/` pathname are all accepted. With the script off, the page is a readable splash with the same
  link. `location.replace` keeps the door out of the history, so Back leaves the app rather than
  bouncing through it.
- **THE WEB PAGE SAYS WHERE THEY WENT.** A page that silently drops a menu reads as broken, so Discover's
  how-to gains one card: *"Converters are not part of the web page"* with a link to `/full/`. Only the
  web page renders it — an installed store build never points at a converter, not even with a link.
- **THE VERSION LINE NAMES THE BUILD.** *Full*, *Play* or *Web*, because "my converter is missing" is a
  question about which build is installed. `Web build — your files only` and `Web build — full` are the
  two web answers.
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** Applied to a fresh clone of `origin/main` at 80.4: `python3
  dev/patch-805.py` (1 step), then `--check` (0 steps); every inline script block parses; `sc-805-check.cjs`
  passes and fails on the 80.4 page it replaces. It runs the page's OWN switch — extracted verbatim from

  (**tools**), a `/full/` path (**tools**), the installed app on `https://localhost` (**tools**), the
  store build (**no tools**), a local preview on `localhost:3000` (**tools**) and a `file:` page
  (**tools**). It then runs the web note against a stub DOM and checks the card it appends names `./full/`,
  and runs `changelogRich` / `changelogTitle` for both builds: the no-tools builds show the two notes that
  changed for them and none of the `[FULL]` ones, while the full build shows all four with the marker

- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No browser was driven and no phone was used: `/full/` was checked over HTTP

  it scales a bitmap and cannot clip one, so corner radius is not a setting it has and this release
  cannot rebuild the APK to give it one. It can draw whatever bitmap it is handed, so the app draws the
  corners first: `scRoundArtDataUrl()` takes the cover data URL the push was already sending, draws it
  cover-fit into a 256px square with an 18% radius (46px), and hands back a PNG data URL. Every path
  through `pushWidgetState` - blob cover, remote cover, cached cover - goes through it, because it wraps
  `send` rather than the three call sites. Cached per source (twelve entries, oldest dropped); a cover
  that cannot be decoded falls back to the original URL, which is what the widget drew before. The

  scrolls the strip to the tab you just opened, centred and clamped at both ends. It scrolls the strip
  with `scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'})` rather than `scrollIntoView`, because `scrollIntoView` on a
  nested scroller also moves the sheet it lives in. Reduce motion (either switch) jumps instead.

- **A TAP ANSWERS.** `.tab`, `.playlist-pick-btn`, `.sc-set-head`, `.settings-pick` and `.sc-set-card`
  compress to `scale(.98)` under the finger and come back on release, on the press curve. It is a
  transform, so it is the compositor's work; nothing on the page re-lays-out to answer a tap.
  **The dock pills are left to their own rule**, and the first cut of this paragraph was wrong about
  why: the dock has carried `transform: scale(0.95)` on press since 74.9, so "the dock gets no press
  animation" was never true. What is true is that its slide gesture measures every pill's rect at
  pointerdown and then drives the hot pill across those rects, so a second scale on top would move the
  very rect the gesture had just read - and would read as a double press. This release's rule therefore
  does not name `.action-pill` at all, and the harness asserts both halves: the dock's own 0.95 rule is
  still there, and the new 0.98 rule does not list the dock.
- **NAVIGATION CROSS-FADES INSTEAD OF CUTTING.** `navigate()` is wrapped once, at its export, in
  `scNavigateSmooth`: if the platform has `document.startViewTransition` and motion is not reduced, the
  change runs inside it and the frame being left fades out over the frame that arrives; otherwise the
  original function is called and returned. **Both doors are pointed at the wrapper** - the block-scoped
  binding (`navigate = scNavigateSmooth`, which is what the page's own callers resolve) and
  `window.navigate` (which is what another script block, and the Studio's own `navigate()`, resolves) -
  because wrapping only one of them is how a "smooth" release ends up smooth on two tabs and instant on
  the rest. Nothing is deferred: the change still runs synchronously inside the callback, so a caller
  that reads state on the next line sees what it always saw. A transition that throws is caught and
  retried as a plain call.
- **A SETTINGS PANE IS NOT A NAVIGATION, and it does not pretend to be.** The sheet's panes all live in
  one scroller and switch by `display`, so a view transition there would snapshot the whole sheet for a
  content swap. They take the app's existing arrival instead - `scViewIn()` on the pane that was shown -
  which is the same 0.22s fade-and-rise the main views already use and already honours Reduce motion.
- **A SCROLL BELONGS TO ITS PANE.** `overscroll-behavior: contain` on `#tabs`, `#settingsPanesWrap` and
  `#studioView` stops a list that has reached its end from dragging the page behind it, and
  `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` keeps the momentum those panes already had for WebViews that only
  honour the prefixed hint. No scroll listener was added, and no timer.
- **REDUCE MOTION, BOTH WAYS.** The Sandbox switch and the device's own setting each turn off the press
  scale, the pane arrival and the view transition. `scMotionOff()` is the single reader of both, and the
  CSS has a rule under each one - so a device that has asked for less motion gets an instant switch
  rather than a faster one.
- **PRISM.** A static palette with a dynamic backdrop, the shape every theme after `galaxy` already has:
  `dynamic:'prism'` puts `theme-dyn-prism` on the body, and four layers drift behind it on the
  `sd-dyn-drift` keyframes 60.x already ships - two soft colour pools, a deep core and a linear base,
  at 17 seconds (slower than Neon Pulse's 8, faster than Abyss's 24). Colours: `#0b0f1f` / `#161c33`
  with `#8FE3FF` and `#C6A6FF` - a blue-black rather than a grey, and accents light enough to read as
  text on both, which is what a phone theme does and a neon one does not. Free, like every theme since
  70.1.3: no `premium`, no `reward`, no lock, because both walls that used to gate themes are gone. It
  needed one object and one rule: `renderThemeOptions()` groups by `dynamic` and `applyTheme()` sets the
  body class, so the wall, the prepaint cache and the badge counter all pick it up on their own.
- **THE WIDGET'S OPTIONS ARE ONES THE NATIVE SIDE READS.** The widget is a RemoteViews layout compiled
  into the APK and drawn by `SideCutWidgetProvider`, which reads exactly `bg1`, `bg2`, `title`,
  `artist`, `accent` and `eq` out of the theme JSON the page pushes. So this release adds only what
  rides that payload: **five more presets** (Aurora, Sand, Slate, Sakura, Lime - two background stops, a
  title, an artist and an accent, the same shape as the seven that were there); **Follow the app theme**,
  which builds the widget's palette from `THEMES[currentTheme]` instead of a second palette the reader
  has to keep in step, and follows a theme change on the next state push; and **Idle battery saver**,
  which is the page's own heartbeat: a paused widget used to stop refreshing after a hard-coded 25
  seconds, and now that number is a setting - 25 seconds, 1 minute, or never - read live on every beat,
  so changing it takes effect without a relaunch.
- **WHAT THE WIDGET STILL CANNOT DO, SAID OUT LOUD.** Widget *sizes* are not an option: the provider
  inflates `R.layout.sidecut_widget` by name, so a size switch would need a second compiled layout in
  the APK - a native change this release cannot build, let alone verify. Hiding the cover, moving the
  transport and blur all live in that same layout. Nothing here is a switch that does nothing.
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** The payload was applied to a scratch tree taken from
  `origin/main` itself (`git clone --depth 1`), so the thing measured is the page this release replaces
  plus this patch and nothing else: `python3 dev/patch-8036.py` (1 step) then `--check` (0 steps);
  **every inline script block parses** (acorn, 7 blocks, 0 failures); and `sc-8036-check.cjs` passes
  **64/64** while the same driver fails **46** on the page it replaces. It proves, against
  the release's own source rather than a copy: the four motion tokens and the press rule exist and the
  dock is not in them; the three panes that own a scroll are contained; both view-transition rules and
  both Reduce-motion rules are there; this release adds no ninth duplicate id (the page has carried
  eight since long before it) and every settings pane the sheet switches to is a real element; Prism is
  in `THEMES` with its dynamic class, its palette and its backdrop; the widget's preset table has twelve
  entries and every one of them carries all nine keys the native side or the preview reads. Then it
  runs the release's own functions in a `vm` with stubs: `scNavigateSmooth` calls the original once and
  returns, runs the change INSIDE `startViewTransition` when the API exists, and skips the transition
  entirely when either Reduce motion switch is on; `widgetThemeFromApp` returns the app theme's
  background and accent for two different themes; `getWidgetTheme` switches between preset and app
  theme and still honours the fine-tune overrides and the bars flag; `setWidgetFollow` and
  `setWidgetIdle` persist what they were given and refuse a value that is not one of the three; the
  heartbeat's guard is the live setting and reads "never" for 0. The OTA bundles reach a true fixed
  point in the release step - root + `ota/` **1109886** bytes, `ota-play/` **1109896** bytes, both
  `--check`s OK at v80.3.6.
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No phone and no screenshot: the **rate** of the cross-fade and of the press
  scale on a real display was not measured, and a `vm` cannot show a composited frame - what is proven
  is which function runs, when, with what argument, and that nothing runs at all when motion is reduced.
  Prism's backdrop was verified as CSS, not as pixels. No Android build was made, so the native widget
  was not re-run: the options added are ones the unchanged native code already reads, which is exactly
  why they were chosen. Nothing moved in the player, the library, the albums, the lyrics, the tabs, the
  downloader, the Studio or the audio graph.

  not muffled"*. Three asks in one message: the anti-muffler, the merge, and the settings list.
- **THE TWO MENUS WERE ONE SUBJECT.** `#settingsPaneMore` carried a group called **Sound** and a group
  called **Playback**. Sound was not even a card: a bare header plus a body holding three panes
  (`settingsPaneRefresh`, `settingsPanePlayback`, `settingsPaneEQ` - crossfade, seek style,
  auto-volume, the assistant duck, the 8 bands, the boost, and display refresh rate inside them).
  Playback was a card holding the sleep timer, gapless, the next-album roll and the per-playlist sort.
  They are ONE card now - **Playback & sound** - and the body keeps every control that was in either
  of them, under four labels a person would name out loud: *Playback, Sleep & queue, Sound, Display*.
  The three panes were **moved verbatim** (the harness slices them out of `origin/main` and out of the
  shipped page and compares them byte for byte), so nothing inside them was edited: the same switch,
  the same slider, the same saved setting, one menu instead of two.
- **NOTHING IS LEFT OUT OF A DROP-DOWN, AND THAT IS ASSERTED, NOT INTENDED.** Every direct child of
  the pane is a section label (`.sc-mgroup`) or a card (`.sc-set-card`) with a head and a body - the
  driver counts it (`25` children: 6 labels, 19 cards, zero stray), so the claim cannot quietly rot.
  The pieces that used to sit loose between two cards are rows now: the tutorial (its replay button
  was a bare button and its text), the three layout switches that shared one box (each is its own row
  now, with the switch itself on the row), "Ask artist when importing songs" (a bare card), and

  streak and the version guide inside it. The box that wrapped the top of the pane - a bordered div
  around a list of groups, a box inside a box - is gone with its open and its close.
- **THE REGION BOUNDARY IS THE PART THAT WENT WRONG FIRST, AND THE PROBE CAUGHT IT.** The merge is a
  replacement from the `Sound` label to the `Library` label, and it is tempting to start it on the
  `</div>` above the label. That close belongs to the **seizure-warning card**, not to the wrapper -
  the wrapper closes at the FAR end of the region, after the old Sound body - so the first cut took
  that close, left the seizure card open, and swallowed everything from the merge down into it (the
  jsdom probe reported 13 children instead of 25, with the Sandbox pane nested inside More). The box's
  open tag is removed at the top of the pane and its close goes with the region, so the two cancel.
- **A ROW READS LIKE A SETTINGS ROW.** Title on the left, its own state on the right, one marker that
  turns. Four of the new rows carry the setting itself on the row (the three layout switches, the
  artist prompt), which is why their head is a `div` with `role="button"` rather than a `<button>`: a
  nested `<button>` is not legal HTML and the parser would tear the row apart. The opener therefore
  ignores a click that landed on a control which is not the row, and the driver proves it both ways -
  tapping the switch on a row does not open the row, tapping the row does. The one thing a row cannot
  hold is a slider's number, so the boost's readout is **mirrored** onto the Playback & sound row by a
  single writer (a debounced observer over the pane), which writes only when the text differs.
- **THE DROP-DOWN IS A HEIGHT, AND `display` IS STILL THE TRUTH.** `setupCollapsible` was four lines
  that flipped `display`; it is one opener now that slides the body from nothing to its measured
  height, drops the inline height when the slide lands (so the storage numbers and the DJ list can
  still grow while open), and takes `display: none` at the end of a close - which is what every other
  reader in the app reads, so nothing else had to change. The row carries `sc-open` from the first
  frame, so the marker turns with the tap. A platform that will not report a height, or a reader with
  **Reduce motion** on, flips exactly as it did before this release; a settle that is interrupted is
  dropped by a generation counter rather than fighting the next tap. The **storage** and **Check for
  updates** rows, which each carried their own click handler, are calls to this one now with what they
  do on opening passed in (`renderStoragePanel`, `renderRefreshRateOptions`).
- **THE ANTI-MUFFLER.** A boxed-in master is two things at once - a build-up around 250-400 Hz where a
  mix turns to mud (a pocket speaker, a cheap DAC, a lossy rip) and a roll-off above a few kilohertz
  where the consonants and the cymbals live - and neither is fixed by turning the volume up, which is
  why it is a switch and not another rung of the boost. Two filters on a **wet** path that sits between
  the boost and its ceiling, beside a **dry** path that is a plain 1.0: `-3.5 dB @ 320 Hz, Q 0.85`
  (peaking) and `+3.5 dB @ 3.2 kHz` (high shelf). The pair is the same size on purpose - an asymmetric
  pair is a preset with a tilt in it, and taste is what the 8-band EQ above it is for. **Off means dry
  1 / wet 0**: the signal is multiplied by 1.0 and a zero is added to it, both exact, so Off is the
  samples 80.3.4 played rather than a claim about what a biquad does at 0 dB gain. **Nothing is ever
  disconnected** to switch it - rewiring the master would have to touch the node the rest of the graph

  paths still owns the ceiling, so the cut and the lift cannot clip. One saved boolean (`antiMuffler`),

## 80.3.4 (October 27, 2026 · 7:59 AM EDT): the tabs come back where you left them, the downloader keeps the link and finishes an interrupted album, and the store build carries no downloader at all

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM, IN TWO MESSAGES.** *"discover studio and tools should all autoscroll
  to where you were last, even if you refresh, the link should save in the downloader and it should
  automatically resume downloading"*, then *"in play version of app remove any parts even related to
  downloaders or converter from the app and it's patch notes"*.
- **DISCOVER WAS PINNED TO THE TOP ON PURPOSE, AND THAT RULE IS NOW REVERSED.** `navigate()` and
  `showDiscover()` both forced `#discoverView.scrollTop = 0` on every open, with the reason written
  beside them ("so the pinned-artists + new-releases section, and not the search results below it,
  is what first shows on screen"). Both lines are gone, and the position now lives in
  `sidecut_scroll_discover` / `sidecut_scroll_studio` / `sidecut_scroll_tools` (localStorage, because
  "even if you refresh" is half the ask, and because the app's own snapshot machinery already carries
  these keys across a storage wipe).
- **THE MEMORY IS ONE TOP-LEVEL BLOCK, AND IT WATCHES THE DOM RATHER THAN REACHING INTO THREE
  CLOSURES.** The studio panes and the tab machinery live in blocks the app's own IIFE cannot see by
  name (the revamp block says as much itself), so the new block uses the one thing the app is
  guaranteed to paint: the `active` class on `#discoverView` and `#studioView`, plus - inside the
  studio view - each pane's class. One `MutationObserver` each, and a tab tap, a studio half tap, a
  view resumed after a reload and the app's own boot all land in the same handler.
- **THE POSITION IS READ WHILE ITS TAB IS STILL ON SCREEN, NEVER AT THE MOMENT OF A SWITCH.** Hiding
  a pane re-lays out the container, and a scroll container clamps `scrollTop` to the new content the
  instant anything reads it - so reading late files the incoming pane's clamped number under the
  outgoing tab, which is how Tools would open half way down an album nobody asked for. The outgoing
  number is what the scroll listener last saw; the incoming tab is restored from its own key.
- **THE RESTORE IS A SHORT SETTLE, AND A HAND ENDS IT.** Discover's results and its pinned rows
  arrive after the view opens, so a saved 4000px is not reachable on the frame the view turns active:
  the target is re-applied (every 120 ms, at most ~5 s) until it is reached, and the first real touch
  - a tap, a drag, a wheel, a key - stops it at once. Nothing remembered means the tab opens at the
  top exactly as it always did, which is also what clears one tab's position out of the container the
  other tab shares.
- **A RUN IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, BECAUSE 80.3.3's HOLD ENDS WITH THE PAGE.** The Web Lock, the
  notification and the Android wake lock all survive leaving the app; none of them survives an OTA
  reload, a storage wipe or Android killing the WebView, and an album is long enough for one of those
  to land in the middle of it. So a run records itself in `sidecut_dl_job`: the link, the format,
  where the songs were going, the plan (so a resume needs no network to plan again), the song list it
  is working through and which of them have landed.
- **"LANDED" COMES FROM THE LIBRARY WRITE, NOT FROM THE RUN.** `scAddConvertedToLibrary` is the one
  place a converted song lands, so that is what takes the song off the queue (matched by title, the
  way the run's own one-source-one-song ledger matches), and both batch runners additionally mark the
  exact slot they were handed (`scDlJobTake(i)`, index-aligned because `scRunPool` hands the slot
  number with the item). A song that failed, or one the app died before landing, stays in the queue -
  which is the whole point of writing it down.
- **THE YOUTUBE PLAYLIST RUN IS A FUNCTION NOW.** It lived inside the click handler that started it -
  a closure over `pl`, `chosen`, `fmt`, `box` and `btnEl`, reachable only by tapping Convert - and
  "automatically resume" needs the same run startable at boot with the songs that never landed. The
  body was lifted into `scYtRunChosen(pl, chosen, fmt, box, btnEl, url)` **unchanged**: the only edits
  inside it are the three record lines. That lift is proven, not asserted - the harness takes the old
  body out of `git archive origin/main` and the new function out of the patched page, normalises both
  and diffs them, and the diff is exactly the `(async function(){` line, the four record lines and
  their comments (20 lines, nothing else). The click path also gained the `.catch` the inline version
  never had, so a throw puts the Convert button back.
- **RESUME IS BOUNDED: TWO AUTOMATIC TRIES, THEN THE LINK IS THE ANSWER.** A song nobody can source
  must not start a download on every single launch for ever. After two automatic resumes the link is
  still in the box and one tap starts the run again by hand. Cancel and the little x beside either
  Convert button clear the record, so a reload never quietly begins a run the owner stopped, and a
  one-song run is written down too (resumed through its own single path, because the song's real
  title is only known while converting).
- **THE STORE BUILD LOST ITS DOWNLOADER, ITS CONVERTER AND THE NOTES ABOUT THEM.** "Remove any parts"

- **"IT'S PATCH NOTES" TOO: AN ENTRY THIS BUILD CANNOT SHOW IS NOT SHOWN.** The page already hid

  channels already understand.
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** The payload was applied to a scratch tree taken from
  `origin/main` itself (`git archive origin/main`), so the thing measured is the page this release
  replaces plus this patch and nothing else: `python3 dev/patch-8034.py` (1 step) then `--check`
  (0 steps); **every inline script block parses** (acorn, 7 blocks, 0 failures); the YouTube lift diff

## 80.3.3 (October 27, 2026 · 6:33 AM EDT): an album converts in minutes, the run keeps going in the background, and a failed song says why

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"do the loudness thing with the downloaders a they should run
  completely in the background, b they should be much faster, a 32 song album shouldn't take an
  hour to download it should be 5 minutes"*. The opening phrase was read as *the thing you asked
  for last time, applied here*: nothing about loudness in the saved files changed, the 80.3.2
  volume boost is untouched, and this release answers (a) and (b).
- **MEASURED FIRST, BECAUSE "SLOW" IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS.** `sc-8033-measure.cjs` (the session's
  scratch driver, kept out of the repo with 80.3.2's) runs the page's OWN encoders over 3.5 minutes of stereo 44.1 kHz: **FLAC 7-17 s, MP3 at 192k 12-60 s**
  of solid CPU on the build machine (the spread is machine load, not noise in the measurement).
  A 32-song album is about two hours of audio, so it was **minutes to tens of minutes of
  encoding on the app's own thread** - the thread every tap has to get through - before any
  network is counted. On top of that, every stream is fetched as bounded 1 MiB ranges
  (googlevideo refuses anything wider), 4-7 of them for a 3.5-minute track at 128-256 kbps, paid
  **one after another**; and every song waited for the one before it to be finished entirely.
  All three of those are the hour.
- **THE RANGES GO OUT TOGETHER.** `scFetchBytes` plans the stream from the first range's
  `content-range` and pulls the rest through `scDlLanes()` lanes (4), stitching the bytes back in
  range order - the file is byte-for-byte what the sequential reader produced. Proven against
  the reader that shipped: `git show origin/main:index.html`'s own `scFetchBytes` is run beside
  the new one over **eight scenarios** (plain 3.5 MiB, exactly four ranges, under one range, a
  player that reported no length, a length under the truth, a server that ignores Range and
  answers 200, a 403 half way, a 403 past the last range) and every byte is compared. Two real
  bugs in the first cut of this were caught that way and fixed: the lanes started at range 0 and
  fetched the first range twice, and a 200 (the whole file) used to be appended to the first
  range as a corrupt file - it is now taken as the stream itself.
- **SEVERAL SONGS IN FLIGHT, AND THE LANE COUNT IS A MEMORY NUMBER.** `scRunPool` + the two batch
  runners: every row goes up front, `scDownloadLanes()` songs convert at once, each song still
  lands in the library exactly as it did, Cancel still stops the run at the next song boundary
  and what finished stays. The default is **2 lanes under 3 GB of device memory, 3 normally, 4
  at 6 GB+** (`navigator.deviceMemory`), because a lane holds one song's decoded audio and a
  3.5-minute stereo track is ~74 MB of Float32 - memory is what a phone runs out of first.
  `window.__scDlTracks` overrides it for a test.
- **THE ENCODERS GET THREADS OF THEIR OWN.** `scEncoderSource()` builds a worker from the PAGE'S
  OWN ENCODER SOURCE (`Function.prototype.toString`) - `scId3v23Bytes`, `scJoinTaggedChunks`,
  `scEncodeMp3Cooperative`, `scEncodeWavCooperative`, `scEncodeAiffCooperative`,
  `encodeAudioBufferToFlac` - so there is still exactly ONE implementation of every format in
  this repository, and the worker is a place to run it rather than a second copy to keep in step.
  A worker is a thread the platform schedules on its own cores and does not throttle with the
  page's timers, which is also what keeps the encoding fast while the app is behind something
  else. The worker shims only what a worker lacks (`document`, the slice budget, a yield to a UI
  it does not have). FLAC/WAV/AIFF hand their samples over (transferred, so the page's copy is
  freed); **MP3 keeps them**, because lamejs is the one encoder that arrives from a CDN and could
  be out of reach inside a worker - so an mp3 that fails there still encodes on the page, and a
  format whose samples were handed over reports a failed song instead of writing silence. The
  crop preview, the crop save and the two Spotify single saves pass `keepSamples` because they
  re-encode the same buffer from their format menu.
- **A RUN IS NOT A WINDOW.** `scRunJobStart/Note/End` wraps each batch: a **Web Lock**
  (`sidecut-download`, shared, held until the run ends - the same mechanism the re-encode job has
  held since 74.1.7) for the whole run, the progress mirrored into the system notification, and
  the native hold below on Android. Nested runs (the retry button re-enters the runner) count
  depth, so an inner run ending never lets go of the outer one.
- **THE ANDROID HALF: `patch-joblock.py`, A NEW BUILD-TIME PATCH.** With the screen off Android
  suspends the app and a suspended app does not download; a cached process is also frozen and may
  be killed. The plugin answers `hold()` with a `PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK` plus a **dataSync foreground
  service** carrying the run's own progress (`update()`), and `release()` gives both back.
  `patch-joblock.py` writes `SideCutJobPlugin.java` + `SideCutJobService.java`, registers the
  plugin in MainActivity beside the widget and audio-focus plugins, and adds the three exact
  permissions plus the `<service ... foregroundServiceType="dataSync">` declaration to the
  manifest. Every call on the web side is a no-op when the plugin is absent (a browser, or an APK
  older than this release) and every native call is wrapped so a device that refuses the service
  still gets the wake lock. It runs after `patch-widget.py` and is idempotent; `android-build.yml`
  gained the step. **This part needs a new app build** - the release itself reaches every install
  through the OTA page, which uses the Web Lock the browser honours.
- **ONE SOURCE, ONE SONG, STILL - AND NOW WITH SEVERAL SONGS IN FLIGHT.** The claim on an upload
  moved to BEFORE the download (`scSourceClaim`): with siblings converting at once, writing the
  ledger after the decode let two tracks pick the same upload while neither had recorded it yet,
  which is exactly the failure that writes one song's audio under another's title. Per-song
  failures moved to a per-song sink (`scFail` + the run's `ctx.reason`) for the same reason -
  `window.__scSourceFail` is one slot and several songs were overwriting each other's reason.
- **THE PAYLOAD IS A DRIVER PLUS SIX MODULES BESIDE IT**, as 80.3.2's was (the edits are
  1-14 KB each instead of one 58 KB file, and a reader can find the part they want):
  `patch_8033_ranges.py`, `patch_8033_workers.py`, `patch_8033_claims.py`,
  `patch_8033_hold.py`, `patch_8033_runners.py`, `patch_8033_copy.py`. Splitting it was
  proven not to change what ships: the page and `sw.js` the modules produce are
  **byte-identical** to the ones the single-file patch produced (only the changelog's own
  clock line, which is computed at run time, was normalised out of the comparison).
- **VERIFIED ON THE PAGE THAT SHIPS.** The payload was applied to a scratch tree taken from
  `origin/main` itself (`git archive origin/main`), so the thing measured is the page this
  release replaces plus this patch and nothing else: `python3 dev/patch-8033.py` (1 step) then
  `--check` (0 steps); every inline script block parses (acorn); and **`sc-8033-check.cjs`
  passes 53/53, exit 0** - against `origin/main`'s OWN `scFetchBytes`, sliced out of
  `git show origin/main:index.html`, which is the only way "the same file" means anything. The
  driver runs the page's own bytes (its functions are sliced out of index.html by parsing it),
  so it cannot pass against a page that does not carry them. It proves: the eight byte-equality
  scenarios above; real overlap (4 ranges in flight, ~20 ms against ~31 ms sequential for six
  ranges, 18 ms against ~54 ms for nine songs at three lanes); cancellation stops dispatch;
  the claim rules (first wins, sibling refused, own re-take allowed, no ledger = no refusals);
  **a FLAC and an MP3 encoded in a worker are byte-identical to the same file encoded on the
  page**; FLAC transfers its samples and MP3 keeps them; the run holds one lock, releases once,
  survives an inner run ending, throttles its progress notes and is a no-op without the plugin;
  and both runners driven end to end in jsdom - six songs, three at a time, every row reading
  `✅ added`, and a cancelled run keeping what finished (2 of 6) with the rest reading
  `— cancelled` and the pill saying so. `APP_VERSION 80.3.2 -> 80.3.3`, the head entry above,
  `sw.js` cache `sidecut-shell-v80.3.3`, and the OTA bundles are rebuilt to a fixed point by
  `release.yml` in the same commit - root + `ota/` **1091943** bytes, `ota-play/` **1091956**
  bytes, both `--check`s OK.
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** The Java has not been compiled here - there is no Android SDK in the
  session; it is syntax-checked (java-parser) and rehearsed against a real `npx cap add android`
  project (registration, manifest, idempotency), and the **Android build workflow is the compile
  proof**. And no wall clock on a phone is quoted: the speed work was measured in parts (encoder
  cost, range overlap, lane overlap), not as an end-to-end device number. Nothing else moved -
  the player, the library, the albums, the lyrics, the boost, the tabs, the widget and the
  assistant are where 80.3.2 left them.

- **THE OWNER'S ASK, VERBATIM.** *"lyrics is not working letter by letter fix it, and add a

  driver (`sc-8032-check.mjs`, lifted out of the session after its work) boots the shipped page
  in jsdom, opens a timed sheet through the real LYRICS button, turns the real chips on and
  walks the playhead across a line. On 80.3.1: **64 frames where a word already sung was not
  fully lit** and **2 frames where the line's total lit-letter count went backwards** - the
  light was wiped off the words behind it on every tick, and the jump to the last word put
  light where nothing had been sung yet. On 80.3.2 the same driver reports **0 and 0**, with
  the current word caught mid-sweep in 56 of 70 frames.
- **FAULT 1 - THE SWEEP SKIPPED WORDS.** `scPaceWords` spread a line's words over the WHOLE
  line window (`wordDurs ... * gap`) and then cut them off at `pace`, the line's natural
  singing length. Every word past that cut had no window at all, and the `litIdx === -1`
  fallback then lit **the last word, complete**. Measured on a plain sheet whose first line
  owned thirteen seconds of the song: word 1 swept, word 2 never lit, word 3 arrived finished -
  which is what "letter by letter is not working" looks like. The words are now spread across
  `pace` itself, so every word has a window inside the stretch the pacer walks.
- **FAULT 2 - THE LIGHT DID NOT STAY.** The 73.4.4 rule wiped every word but the current one on
  every frame, so a line was one word flashing in place with nothing lit between two words.
  Letter mode now **fills the line left to right**: a word the singer has passed keeps every
  letter lit, the sung word sweeps, later words stay dark. The 73.4.4 intent survives - nothing
  is left DIMMED behind the light, no gold travels along the sheet, and the passed words are
  touched only where a letter is not already lit so a finished word never re-runs a transition
  and never flickers. `scLettersWipeOthers` runs **once per line change** (not per tick) so the
  song cannot turn into a wall of gold by the second verse.
- **VOLUME BOOST, 0 TO +15 dB, UNDER THE EQ.** `scBoostGain` is a GainNode on the master: both
  decks' limiters land on it, and it feeds `scBoostGuard` and then the assistant duck's
  `scDuckMaster`, so it multiplies the mixed signal as the last thing before the speakers.
  +15 dB is 10^(15/20) = **5.62x**. A near-flat DynamicsCompressor after it is the soft ceiling
  that keeps a loud master loud instead of crackling - and at 0 dB that compressor is a
  **straight wire** (`ratio 1`, threshold 0), so Off is the same signal the app made before this
  release rather than "nearly". The slider applies on `input` and writes on `change` (one saved
  setting per drag), `boostDb` is restored beside `autoVolume` in the boot restore, and
  `setBoostDb` calls `ensureAudioGraph` first so moving it before anything has played still
  takes effect.

  About & updates - every collapsible header carrying `sc-set-head`, every body `sc-set-body`

  variants. The three loose buttons that floated between the rollback list and the DJ card (the

## The Android version code (October 26, 2026): the bundle's number comes from the build's run

- **THE OWNER, WITH A SCREENSHOT OF PLAY.** `SideCut-5.0.55-release.aab` refused with *"Version code 512000
  has already been used. Try another version code."* The ask was one word: *"update"*.
- **WHY 512000 WAS SPENT TWICE.** The 5.0.55 bundle in the `apk-80.2.8-release` release (built 25 October, run
  566) carries `versionCode` **512000** *and* `APP_VERSION` **80.2.8** - it was uploaded, so Play owns the
  number - and the rebuild made after 80.3 / 80.3.1 carried the same 512000 because both took it from
  `package.json`'s `androidVersionCode` pin, which nothing bumps but a person. The app is built more than once
  per package.json `"version"` *precisely* because it ships over the air between Play uploads, so a
  hand-maintained number is the wrong shape for it. (Same failure as 5.0.54's 511722, one layer up.)
- **THE NUMBER IS NOW THE RUN'S.** `.github/workflows/patch-version.py` computes
  `versionCode = 512001 + 10 * (GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER - 567) + (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT - 1)`. Run numbers cannot repeat
  or go backwards, a re-run only changes the attempt, ten attempts are reserved per run and the stride between
  runs is those ten, so the sequence is monotone by construction: 567/1 -> 512001, 567/2 -> 512002, 568/1 ->
  512011. **No run number is a hard failure, not a fallback to a pin.** The script exits if the gradle
  versionCode/versionName replace did not take, prints what it wrote, and `--print-code` prints the same number
  for anything that wants to check an artifact against it. `androidVersionCode` is gone from package.json.
- **A REJECTED UPLOAD STILL SPENDS ITS CODE**, so a rebuild is a NEW dispatch - "Re-run all jobs" gets a new
  number only while the attempts of that run have codes left. `dev/version-code-check.py` drives the script
  through 58 consecutive builds, both attempts of each, the spent block (566) and the missing-run case: **14/14**.
- **`workflows` IS NOT A GITHUB_TOKEN SCOPE.** The first attempt to land this from a workflow failed at the
  push - "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/android-build.yml`
  without `workflows` permission" - and `permissions: workflows: write` is not a thing (the run does not even
  parse). A commit that edits a workflow file needs a token that carries that permission; GITHUB_TOKEN never
  does, however the `permissions:` block is written.

## 80.3.1 (October 26, 2026 · 8:14 AM EDT): a song that stops in its first seconds comes back, and the crash banner stops blaming a helper

- **THE OWNER, WITH A SCREENSHOT.** A song parked at **0:02** with the play button showing,
  and the red banner reading *"Playback stopped while it was starting, so the audio-focus
  helper has been switched off - songs play normally now. It comes back in the next
  update."* The ask was three words: *"audio issue fix"*.
- **THE BUG THAT PARKS THE SONG IS THE INTERRUPTION LATCH, AND IT OUTLIVED THE PRESS.**
  `audioFocusInterrupted` tells `scUndoPlatformPause`, the 30 s heartbeat and
  `scSecondLook` to BELIEVE an automatic pause instead of undoing it. It was cleared by a
  focus GAIN, by `scNoteCallState(false)` after a call, and by `scTransportResume()` -
  which only the media-session play / previous / next handlers call. **The app's own
  play/pause button called `a.play()` and nothing else**, so `onPlayEvt` ran with the latch
  still set. After one real interruption (a call, another app keeping the audio) every
  later pause in that session was obeyed and nothing could touch it: press play, something
  pauses the song two seconds in, and it stays at 0:02 for the rest of the session.
  `onPlayEvt` now drops the latch when the start is not `revivingAudio` and no call is up,
  and `audioFocusInterruptedAt` records when it was set. **Reproduced and fixed with one
  driver** (`sc831-bug.mjs`): 80.3 parks the song (`focus-loss` is the last recorded stop),
  80.3.1 puts it back (`platform-pause after 2000ms - replayed (unrequested)`).
- **THE OUTSIDE PAUSE HAD A 1.2-SECOND WINDOW.** `blockSpuriousStop` refuses a stale
  lock-screen / notification pause only within 1.2 s of the start and 0.5 s of playhead -
  shorter than the notification/session hand-over on the installed app - so a stale press
  that landed at 0:02 was obeyed as if a finger had pressed it. It now refuses within 4 s
  and 2.5 s of playhead, up to three per attempt, recording `refused-auto-pause-media-session`
  each time. A genuine second press is obeyed exactly as before (driven in the harness).
- **THE BANNER SWITCHED A HELPER OFF THAT IS NOT IN THE PLAY PATH.** The recorder wrote
  `sidecut_audiofocus_off` for the rest of the version on a death during "starting
  playback", which makes `capAudioFocus` null for the session: no focus listener, no
  `callState()`, no `duckState()`. Since **58.8.4** `AUDIO_FOCUS_REQUESTS_OFF` is true -
  asking for focus on the app's behalf is what made Chromium pause its own element - so
  there is no focus request in the play path for that helper to be blamed for, and the
  switch-off bought nothing while costing a real call pausing the song and the assistant
  duck. It is gone; the death is written to `sidecut_playback_stopped_at_start` instead
  (with no `APP_VERSION` in it - that const is declared further down the page, the same
  trap 73.4.7 found in the media-notification recorder), and the banner no longer stacks a
  second message over the first.
- **A RELOAD IS NOT A CRASH.** The same banner fired for a page that had simply reloaded
  itself - an update hand-over, a refresh, a WebView restart - because `_scRestart` only
  forgave a boot less than 30 s after the previous one. The recorder now reads
  `PerformanceNavigationTiming.type` (with `performance.navigation.type === 1` as the
  fallback): a boot whose navigation type is `reload` is the app loading itself again, and
  a reload counts as a normal death.
- **WHAT DID NOT CHANGE**: requests stay off, a real call still stands the song down and
  brings it back, a message blip is still undone at any point in a song and in the
  background, a user pause and a finished song are still believed, DJ Mode still owns its
  own sound, and the revive budget still bounds all of it. Driven, not grepped: a call is
  still latched, a press during that call does not clear the stand-down, and the song comes
  back when the call ends.
- **VERIFIED** with `sc831-check.mjs` (jsdom, the shipped page, a stub phone) -
  **51 passed, 0 failed** - covering: the release metadata and the six notes, the four
  changes being present and nothing re-enabled, the latch ending on the app's own press, a
  platform pause at 0:02 being undone and recorded, a stale lock-screen pause at 0:02 being
  refused while a press 40 s in is obeyed, a call stand-down surviving a press and coming
  back when the call ends, a reloading boot showing no banner and writing no switch-off, a
  real death still speaking in plain words and recording itself, and no console error from
  the page. The page was driven **before and after** with `sc831-bug.mjs` to prove the
  first assertion is a real one.
- **THE BUNDLES.** Root 1080313 bytes, Play 1080327 bytes, rebuilt to a true fixed point
  in the runner before this entry is written, and settled again by deploy.yml on the push.
  Both `--check`s green on the tree that ships.
- **THE LESSON.** A guard that refuses to undo a pause is only as good as the thing that
  ends it. Every door that starts playback has to end the memory of an interruption - and
  the app's own button is the one door a person actually uses.

## 80.2.10 (October 26, 2026 · 7:21 AM EDT): a new release announces itself once instead of every day, and the count is the list you can see

- **THE OWNER, AFTER A STRING OF RELEASES.** *"why does the new releases keep showing
  the new release every single friken day after the release came out I only need to see
  it once and it says +4 other releases when there is only 1 release in total fix this
  crap dude"*. Both halves are one bug with a long tail.
- **THE APP READ ITS OWN STORED ROW AS A NEW FIND.** `fetchArtistReleases` stores a
  one-track release under the SONG's name - every catalog files it as `<Song> - Single`,
  and the wrapper is dropped by `scSingleTitle` - but its catalog pass keyed the row on
  the CATALOG's name (`alb:<collectionName>|<day>`). The key it had just written never
  matched on the next pass, so the same single came back as "fresh" on every check:
  boot, the six-hour check, a return to the app, Fetch latest. Each run appended another
  copy to `pinnedReleases`, and each run had `totalNew > 0`, which is what fired
  `scReleaseAlert` again - the once-a-day announcement.
- **THE COUNT WAS THE RUN, NOT THE LIST.** `scReleaseAlert` was handed the raw finds of
  one run, capped at five and aggregated across every pinned artist, so one artist's
  single could be announced as `"Song" is out (+4 more)` while the panel - which
  de-duplicates by title and day and stops at a month - showed a single row. That is the
  "+4 other releases when there is only 1 release in total".
- **BOTH NAMES ARE KEYS NOW.** The stored-key set answers to a row's own title AND to
  the same title with the `- Single` wrapper folded away, and the catalog pass keys the
  drop the way it is stored (checking the catalog's name too, for rows an older build
  wrote). A drop already in the list is not added again, whichever name it arrives
  under.
- **THE ANNOUNCEMENT READS THE LIST.** `scReleaseAnnouncements` takes
  `window.__scReleaseList(31)` - the same de-duplicated, month-bounded list the Home
  bubble, the panel and the Discover section paint - and drops what has been read, what
  has already been announced, and what is still on the way. `scReleaseAlert` marks every
  row it announces as `alerted` and saves before it speaks, so no boot or check can say
  the same drop twice, and its `+N more` is the number of OTHER drops in that list.
- **THE COPIES LEFT BEHIND ARE COLLAPSED.** `scCollapseReleaseDuplicates` runs on load
  beside the junk prune: same normalised title (with the wrapper folded) and the same
  day is one row; a read or announced copy makes the survivor read or announced; and the
  artwork, link, preview and kind a later copy brought are kept. The copies earlier
  builds made on every check stop being counted anywhere.
- **THE BELL READS THE SAME LIST.** `hasLandedUnseenReleases` used to scan every stored
  row at any age, so a drop too old for the panel to show - and the copies of it - kept
  the badge lit for ever. It reads `__scReleaseList(31)` now, so the bell and the panel
  cannot disagree.

  `fetchArtistReleases`, `window.__scReleaseList` (block 2's), `scReleaseAnnouncements`,
  `scReleaseAlert`, `scReleaseKey`, `scCollapseReleaseDuplicates` and

## 80.2.8 (October 25, 2026 · 3:06 PM EDT): the lyrics follow the voice through slow-then-fast, a change of language and the silence after a line - and the phone's size ladder stops going backwards

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR TWO THINGS IN ONE UPDATE.** *"add to the same update a fix
  with the lyrics that makes it absolute correct with tempo changes and language
  changes slow then fast breaks after lines everything fix that"*, and, of the Home
  bubble sizes that shipped in 80.2.7, *"fix it"*.
- **THE LYRICS WERE PACED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY SINGING.** `scPaceWords` gave every
  word a share of the line's window by syllable weight, at one rate from this line's
  timestamp to the next one's. That is exact only if the singer holds one tempo for the
  whole line. It is wrong for exactly the four cases named: a line sung slow then fast,
  a song that changes language mid-line (syllables per second change, and no weight
  table can know which half is which), a stamp seconds away because the singer stopped
  (the window IS that gap, so the sweep crawled into the silence), and a chorus repeated
  at a different tempo.
- **THE WORDS ARE NOW TIMED BY THE RECORDING.** A sung word is an attack, and the app
  already computes a rising-energy envelope for the track (`scOnsetEnvelope`, 20ms hops,
  used by the auto-alignment). `scWordStartsForWindow` reads that envelope inside the
  line's own window: with at least as many rises as words, the words are the strongest
  attacks in order (two rises closer than 90ms are one word, extras are dropped from the
  weakest, so a consonant cluster or a drum under the voice cannot split a word); with
  fewer rises than words, the words are shared out across the rises that are there. It
  never looks at the words themselves, so it is language-blind, and a rise after a long
  silence is simply the next word.
- **FALLBACK IS THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, EXACTLY.** A window with fewer than two rises (a held
  note, a whisper, a track that is not on the device) returns `null` and the pacer runs
  the syllable share it has always run. A sheet with no timestamps at all never reaches
  the measurement, because there are no windows to measure.
- **MEASURED ONCE, CACHED.** `scWordMeasureKick` decodes the track the first time
  word-by-word or letter-by-letter is switched on for a song, writes
  `lyricWords_<track>` to the meta store, and returns immediately on every later tick -
  including a remembered "no file for this track" record, so a song that cannot be
  measured is not re-scanned twenty times a second.
- **THE PACER READS IT FIRST.** `scMeasuredWordStarts` matches the live line by its own
  timestamp and word count (a sheet edited since the measurement is never paced by the
  old numbers), and the pacer lights the word whose measured window holds the playhead;
  before the first rise nothing is lit, and past the last rise the last word holds, so a
  line cannot walk into the gap behind it. The letter wave rides the same window, so
  letters and words cannot drift apart.
- **THE PHONE'S LADDER.** 80.2.7 made the walk one ascending line, but `@media
  (max-width:480px)` still overrode the full rung to 170px while Roomy stayed 179, so a
  phone drew 158, 179, **170**, 230, 260 - one step backwards in the middle of the
  ladder, on the only screen the chip is used on. The override is gone.
- **VERIFIED, ON THE SHIPPED SOURCE.** Its own harness (not a gate, run in the session
  that wrote it) extracts `scWordStartsForWindow` and `scPaceWords` from `index.html` and
  drives them: slow-then-fast lands on 10.2/11.6/13.0/13.4/13.8/14.2 where the rises are;
  a break (tag 18s away, singing done by 11.2) keeps the last word at 11.2; a held line
  with 2 rises for 5 words stays ordered inside its window; a window with one rise
  returns `null`; the pacer lights 0,1,2,3,3 through a measured slow-then-fast line,
  holds the last word past its rise, lights nothing before the first rise, and still
  falls back to the syllable path when there is no measurement. In headless Chrome at
  390px the ten rungs render 60/84/96/118/146/158/179/200/230/260, strictly ascending,
  with the full rung at its own 200; at 1024px the ladder still ascends
  (60/84/96/140/146/158/179/220/230/260). The page boots with no script error.
- **THE BUNDLES.** Root 1073776 bytes, Play 1073791 bytes, rebuilt to a true fixed point
  in the runner before this entry is written, and settled again by deploy.yml on the
  push. Both `--check`s green on the tree that ships.
- **WHAT ONLY A REAL SONG CAN SHOW.** The decode-and-measure path runs on a local file
  with a timed sheet; the pacer and the reader are verified, and the decode path reuses
  the primitives the auto-alignment has shipped for releases. Open a song with
  word-by-word on, and the first play of it is the one that measures.

## 80.2.5 (October 25, 2026 · 1:44 AM EDT): albums only come from you now, and an album can be deleted from its own three dots

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR TWO THINGS.** "sometimes they're making random albums with
  singles and stuff idk why it shouldn't be doing that and in the album 3 dots it
  should have an option to delete the album with confirmation". The albums were
  real and they were the app's doing: two paths made an album without being asked.
  This release stops both, and gives the card's menu the row that removes one.
- **THE LAUNCH.** `scAlbumsRecoverDeleted()` step (3) made an album out of every
  album tag on the files that no entry held and that at least two songs carried -
  and, for a name the archive knew, out of a tag only one song carried. The tags on
  a phone are whatever the files arrived with (a site's idea of the album, the
  song's own name in the album field, one "single" shared by two songs), and the
  entry it wrote was stamped `manual:true` from birth, so it was indistinguishable
  from an album the owner made. That is the whole of the report. The pass now
  restores only what the app itself took: names in `sidecut_albumsArchive`, written
  by the one sweep that ever removed an entry, and each one comes back with the song
  list it had at that moment. Nothing else is invented, and a tombstoned name is
  skipped. Turning tags into albums is still there, where a person asks for it:
  Manage albums -> Rebuild albums from tags.
- **THE RECORD TAP.** `openAlbumForCurrentSong()` (a tap on the mini turntable)
  called `ensureAlbumSaved(tag)` and so made an album out of the playing song's tag
  on the spot - often a one-song album named after the file. It now opens the album
  only when the tag IS an album you have, and falls through to the existing song
  jump when it is not. A jump is a question about the library, not permission to add
  to it.
- **THE DELETE.** The album card's three dots grows a third row, `Delete album`, in
  the danger colour, under the sort and the hand reorder. It opens a confirmation in
  the app's own sheet language - the album named, "Its N songs stay in your library
  - only the album goes, and it will not come back on the next launch", Keep it /
  Delete album. `window.confirm()` is deliberately not used: the Android WebView can
  swallow it and answer false, which is how the panel's Delete button once came to
  look broken.
- **UNDO, AND THE TOMBSTONE.** `deleteUserAlbum(name, opts)` now returns whether it
  deleted, remembers the entry and its place in `albumOrder`, and toasts with Undo:
  Undo puts the entry, its songs and its position back and deletes the tombstone, so
  the album is exactly as it was. It no longer reopens Manage albums unconditionally
  - only when Manage albums is the popup on screen - so deleting from a card cannot
  replace the list the owner is looking at.
- **WHAT DOES NOT MOVE.** The songs, their album tags, every other album, the album
  order, and the whole 80.2.4 sort are untouched. Deleting an album deletes a list,
  never music.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/staircase-check.cjs` gains section **[11]** and is **136/0**,
  and the section travels alone in `dev/patch-gate-8025.py`, which refuses to pass
  unless every claim of it is in the gate. `dev/albums-manual-check.cjs` is
  rewritten where it promised the old rule: it now proves a missing entry is NOT
  invented from its tag, and that an archived album is still put back whole - it is
  **61/0**.
- **THE NEW SUITE.** `dev/album-auto-delete-check.cjs` drives a real boot of the
  patched page on a library whose files carry tags nobody made albums for:
  **52/0**. No card appears for a shared tag, a song-named tag or a loose tag; the
  archive is the only thing restored; the record tap makes nothing; the card menu's
  third row asks first; Keep it changes nothing; Delete removes, tombstones and
  leaves every song and tag alone; Undo puts it back with its place and clears the
  tombstone.
- **THE REPIN.** `dev/repin-8025.mjs`: live pin 80.2.4 -> **80.2.5**, adjacency
  `PREV` 80.2.3 -> **80.2.4**, both regex spellings swept, `--check` clean in 0.

## 80.2.4 (October 24, 2026 · 10:19 PM EDT): an album card gets its own three dots, and an album sorts into the order it really plays

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR ONE THING, IN TWO PLACES.** "add a way in albums and 3
  dots to sort an album by if it's an actual album then in that actual order get
  this from album history". An album's songs have only ever been in the order they
  were imported, which is almost never the order the record plays in, and Album
  History already knew the order. This release connects the two.
- **THE CARD.** Every album card in Albums now carries the same three dots a song
  row carries. A tap opens an album menu: `Sort into the album's real order` and
  `Reorder songs by hand` - the sheet a long press already opened, so the menu is
  not a one-button dead end. The tap stops at the button; the header's own tap
  folds the card and must not fold it on the way in.
- **THE SONG.** The same sort is a row in the song's three-dot sheet - `Sort album
  "<name>" into its real order` - and it is outside the Albums-only block the hand
  reorder sits in, because a song knows its album in every view. It lands in the
  sheet's Organize group, not a group of its own.
- **THE READ.** `scRealFetch` is the pair Album History makes: the iTunes album
  search, then the collection lookup by id in the storefronts the app already
  walks (default, US, IN, GB), then Deezer's album search and its own track
  endpoint. A collection only counts when its NAME agrees with the album, so a
  similar record is never filed in, and the tracks are sorted by disc then track
  number rather than trusting the reply's order.
- **THE FILING.** `scRealApplyOrder` rewrites the album's own `trackIds` - the one
  store the cards, playback and the queue all read - so nothing else needs to
  change. Each real track claims one song, in the record's order; a song the
  album does not name keeps its place at the END, in the order it already had, so
  a sort never drops a song. A list that names none of the album's songs leaves
  the album exactly as it was and says so.
- **THE MATCH.** Titles are compared after the decoration only a file carries is
  folded away - a remaster year, a deluxe tag, a featuring credit, a trailing
  live note - and every loose match sits on a word edge, so a one-word title never
  claims a different song.
- **THE CACHE.** The list is kept per album in `sidecut_albumRealOrder`, with the
  artist it was read for, so a different record with the same name is never
  reused; forty albums deep, oldest out first. A cached list is used before the
  network is asked, so the second sort is instant and works in flight mode, and it
  is thrown away only when it names none of the album's songs.
- **UNDO, AND NO LIES.** Every sort carries Undo, which puts the old order back;
  an album of one song says there is no order to sort, an album Album History has
  nothing for says that and moves nothing, and a sort that fails says so rather
  than reporting a change it did not make.
- **THE GATES.** `dev/album-real-order-check.cjs` is a boot of the patched page -
  **35/0**: the card's dots open the menu without folding the card, the menu's
  first row files the album into the store's order with the unnamed song kept at
  the end, the cache is written with its artist and source, Undo restores, a
  second sort reads no network at all, the song sheet carries the row in a
  non-Albums view and in the Organize group, an album the store knows nothing
  about is untouched, and a one-song album refuses. `dev/staircase-check.cjs`
  gains section **[10]** (**108/0** overall).
- **THE REPIN.** `dev/repin-8024.mjs`: live pin 80.2.3 -> **80.2.4**, adjacency
  `PREV` 80.2.2 -> **80.2.3**, both regex spellings swept, `--check` clean.
- **THE CHANGELOG HEAD HAS EIGHT NOTES** on purpose: `test-738` requires at least
  seven, no apostrophes, the words widget / player / lyrics / letter, and no
  downloader or converter term.
- **THE OTA BUNDLES.** Root 1064254 bytes, Play 1064267, rebuilt to a fixed point
  in the runner and both `--check`s green on the tree that ships.

  taking the tier's colour, and a card glow that warms from bronze to ice. The streak
  cards keep their own three rings and 26 bits, because `paintCeremony(host, 0)` is
  what they ask for.
- **THE TRIGGER IS THE PLAY COUNTER, NOT A TIMER.** `commitPlay` - the one place a play
  is counted - calls `SC80.checkPlays()` after it writes the count, behind a guard, so
  a missing hook can never stop a play from counting. A start (`bootPlays`) and a
  return to the foreground (`visibilitychange`) check the same rung, because a play
  heard with the screen off lands in the stats with no card on screen. The HIGHEST rung
  crossed gets the card and every rung below it is recorded at the same time
  (`markPlaysThrough`), so a library restored with thousands of plays already in it
  says its piece once instead of queueing nine popups.
- **THE RECORD LIVES IN STUDIO.** Tools, Milestones gains a Plays block: the next rung
  and how far along it is, the awards already won with their dates, a Replay on each,
  and a Preview 10,000 plays button. `data-sc80-plays` is wired through the same
  delegated handler the streak replays use.
- **THE STREAK CARD IS UNTOUCHED IN WHAT IT SAYS.** `celebrate()` now resets
  `data-kind`/`data-tier`, hides the medal, restores the Milestone kicker, the DAY
  STREAK unit and the Keep it going button, and paints three rings - so the two
  celebrations share one overlay without either inheriting the other's look. Its own
  copy, its own record and its own replay are unchanged.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/staircase-check.cjs` gains section **[9]** - the ladder, the tail,
  the medal, the ceremony per tier, the medal stylesheet, the trigger, the Studio block

## 80.1 (October 22, 2026 · 10:16 PM EDT): the corner flight, under the number it should have had

- **80.0.10 WAS NEVER A VERSION, AND THIS REPOSITORY ALREADY SAID SO.** The comment
  directly above `APP_VERSION` has carried the rule since 60.1 - "the third number
  stops at nine: 60.0.9 is followed by 60.1 (never 60.0.10)" - and `AGENTS.md` says
  it twice in the 80 line: "NEXT RELEASE: `80.1`". The release that shipped the
  corner flight, the covering bar and the working plus was numbered 80.0.10 anyway.
  The owner's correction was one line: "it should be v80.1 bro READ THE AGENT MD".
- **SO THIS RELEASE MOVES THE NUMBER, AND ONLY THE NUMBER.** `APP_VERSION` 80.0.10 ->
  **80.1**, the cloud block's two banners, the changelog head's version and stamp
  (with one note saying why), and the shell cache
  `sidecut-shell-v80.0.10` -> **`sidecut-shell-v80.1`**. The flight, the bar and the
  sheet are byte-for-byte what 80.0.10 shipped; the page's hash before this patch is
  the tree that release produced.
- **NO ORPHAN ENTRY.** The 80.0.10 changelog entry is not kept under a number that
  never existed - it becomes the 80.1 entry, so the list reads 80.1, then 80.0.9.
  That is also why the adjacency `PREV` stays **80.0.9**: it is the release before
  this one, and 80.0.10 was no release at all.
- **WHAT THIS RELEASE STILL CARRIES** (the work the owner asked for): five 46px icon
  treads joined edge to edge in the bottom right corner, one riser a step, the plus
  closing the flight; a full-width mini player flush with the bottom edge, its inset
  part of the bar, the scrub line its top edge and long titles ending in an ellipsis;
  and the add-songs sheet as a screen-level panel above the bar, with its own X,
  Escape, the backdrop and a close after you pick - the fix for a sheet that opened a
  full screen above the top edge.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/staircase-check.cjs` moves its four release strings (banner,
  APP_VERSION, shell cache, changelog head) and stays **68/0**.
  `dev/patch-gate-801.py` checks that it arrived that way.

  left at **80.0.9**, both regex spellings and the cache swept, `--check` clean in 0.

## How a release reaches GitHub

- **THE SANDBOX HAS NO WRITE CREDENTIAL. THE GITHUB APP CONNECTION IS THE CREDENTIAL.**
  Checked exhaustively while shipping 80.0.3: no `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` / PAT in
  `env`, no `~/.git-credentials`, no `~/.netrc`, no `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, `gh auth
  status` says not logged in, `~/.ssh` holds only `known_hosts` (`git@github.com` ->
  *Permission denied (publickey)*), `/workspace/repo.git` is the local base repo with no
  remote, and `git push` fails with *could not read Username for
  'https://github.com'*. Read access works (`git fetch`, `git ls-remote`,
  raw.githubusercontent); write access does not. **Do not spend another session hunting
  for a token that is not there.**
- **WHAT DOES WORK: the connected GitHub app (AnekTheGreat).** A file lands as an
  ordinary commit through the app's create/update-file call - one file per commit - and
  the release workflow is started with the app's workflow-dispatch call. 80.0.3 shipped
  exactly that way: six payload commits (`dev/patch-8003.py`, its revisions diff, the
  repin, the gate block, `dev/release-entry.md`, `dev/release-gates.sh`, the proof) and
  then `release.yml` with `version=80.0.3`, which produced commit `328fa64` - patch,
  repin, gate block, OTA rebuild, battery and the release commit all inside the runner.
- **VERIFY EVERY UPLOADED FILE BY BLOB SHA, NOT BY EYE.** `git hash-object <file>` before
  the upload must equal the `content.sha` the app returns afterwards (80.0.3: patch
  `dbcf1639`, revisions `5f8b4f60`, repin `c1996bdd`, gate block `ba3b47f8`, entry
  `96cc9e2f`, battery `62465f29`, proof `5fc7a496`). A mismatch is a transcription error,
  and the workflow's proof step stops the release rather than committing a wrong page.
- **NEVER RE-EMIT `index.html` OR THIS FILE THROUGH THE APP.** `index.html` is 3.4 MB and
  this file is ~860 KB; both are larger than a tool call can carry, and that is the whole
  reason a release is a payload. `dev/patch-<N>.py` edits the page **inside the runner**;
  `dev/release-record.py` edits this file **inside the runner**. AGENTS.md changes only
  from an Actions job (a release, or a one-off note like `dev/agents-shipping-note.py`),
  never by hand from a sandbox.
- **REHEARSE FROM `git archive origin/main` BEFORE DISPATCHING.** In a throwaway
  directory: apply the patch, the repin and the gate block, then require that
  `index.html` and every `dev/test-*.mjs` / `dev/*-check.cjs` are byte-identical to the
  tested tree, and that `sh dev/release-proof.sh <version> | sha256sum` equals the hash in
  `dev/release-<N>.proof`. The workflow enforces the same two things, and a release that
  skips the rehearsal only finds out after the battery.
- **A REVISION TO A PENDING RELEASE GOES IN THE PATCH, NOT INTO THE WORKING TREE ONLY.**
  The payload is reapplied to a clean `origin/main` by the runner. When the owner changes
  their mind mid-release (80.0.3: the pill cut side by side, and the Look-and-feel card
  out of Settings), fold it into `dev/patch-<N>.py` - 80.0.3 carries the second half in
  `dev/patch-8003-revisions.py` as one unified diff applied with `patch -p1` - and update
  `dev/release-<N>.proof`. A page edited only in the sandbox is a page that never ships.

## 80.0.4 (October 21, 2026 · 9:23 PM EDT): the Studio tab is cut the way the Library tab is

- **HOW THIS RELEASE REACHED GITHUB - AND WHY THAT KEEPS COMING UP.** The sandbox that
  cuts a release has **no git write credential**: no `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` / PAT in
  `env`, no `~/.git-credentials`, no `~/.netrc`, no `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, `gh auth
  status` says not logged in, `~/.ssh` holds only `known_hosts` (`git@github.com` ->
  *Permission denied (publickey)*), and `git push` fails with *could not read Username
  for 'https://github.com'*. Reads work (`git fetch`, `git ls-remote`); writes do not.
  The credential that does exist is the **connected GitHub app (AnekTheGreat)**: files
  land through its create/update-file call and the workflow starts through its dispatch
  call. 80.0.4 went up that way - `dev/patch-8004.py`, `dev/repin-8004.mjs`, the gate
  block, the store block, this entry and the proof - each verified by blob SHA
  (`git hash-object` before, `content.sha` after), then `release.yml` with
  `version=80.0.4`. **Do not hunt for a token that is not there; use the app.**
- **AND IT IS IN THE REPOSITORY'S MEMORY NOW, NOT JUST IN A CHANGELOG.** Asking the
  same question every session is what the top of `AGENTS.md` is for, and `AGENTS.md` is
  ~860 KB - bigger than any API call can carry - so the note cannot be hand-carried out
  of a sandbox either. `dev/agents-shipping-note.py` holds it, and this release's record
  step runs it: `dev/release-record.py` writes the entry and then the note, in that
  order, so the note lands directly under the title, above the newest entry, and a
  session that reads one screenful of memory finds out that the credential is the app
  connection before it goes looking for a git token. Both halves are idempotent
  (marker-based), and a note that fails to insert is printed and skipped rather than
  failing a release.
- **THE OWNER'S CORRECTION.** "the diagonal for tools and studio should be like the one
  for library and albums except top left to bottom right." 80.0.3 shipped a seam that
  leaned - 60% of the pill's width at the top to 40% at the bottom - which is not the
  Library pill's construction at all. The Library pill has been one straight line from
  corner to corner since 70.0, with a name in each of the two triangles.
- **SO IT IS THE LIBRARY CUT, MIRRORED.** `#studioHalf` is
  `clip-path:polygon(0 0, 0 100%, 100% 100%)` - the lower triangle, its name in the
  bottom left corner - and `#toolsHalf` is `polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%)` - the upper
  triangle, its name in the top right one. The seam is one SVG line from `0,0` to
  `100%,100%`: top left to bottom right, exactly the other diagonal from the Library
  tab's `100%,0 -> 0,100%`.
- **TOOLS IS STILL ON THE RIGHT.** The owner asked for that in 80.0.3 and it survives
  the mirror: with this seam the right-hand region is the upper triangle, so Tools owns
  it and Studio owns the lower one. The two names now sit in opposite corners, the way
  Library and Albums do, instead of both on one centre line.
- **ONE TABLE, THREE CONSUMERS.** The seam is written down once, in `SC_DOCK_SPLITS`:
  `studioBtn` becomes `line: (xn, yn) => xn - yn` (the same signed-distance form the
  Library cut uses) and `edge: 0.5`. The hit test that decides which half a finger is
  over, the sliding highlight that lights it and the drawn SVG line all read that one
  entry, so the half a tap lands on, the half that lights and the side of the line that
  is drawn cannot disagree - which is what let this release be a geometry change rather
  than a rewrite.
- **THE GATES MOVED WITH IT, AND ONE OF THEM GOT STRONGER.**
  `dev/revamp-check.cjs` [6] now asserts the line at `0,0 -> 100%,100%`, both clip
  polygons, and that the names sit in opposite corners (bottom left / top start) -
  **106/0**. `dev/album-follow-dock-check.cjs` derives the expected highlight from the
  seam itself, and adds the other side of it: a drift over the pill's top right lights
  the Tools half and opens Studio on Tools - **108/0** (it was 106/0; the new checks are
  the Tools drift). `dev/studio-70-check.cjs`, untouched, still passes **570/0**.
- **NOTHING ELSE.** The bar across the top, the player on the safe area, the bubbles, the

- **THE REPIN.** `dev/repin-8004.mjs`: the live pin moves 80.0.3 -> **80.0.4**, adjacency
