## 80.0.2 (October 21, 2026 · 8:02 AM EDT): the assistant duck, to your taste - choose how far the music steps back

- **THE OWNER'S REQUEST WAS ALREADY SHIPPED, AND THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF IT.**
  80.0.1 answers "step the music back when I hold the power button and talk to
  Gemini" - it ducks, and it comes back when the phone says the request is over.
  What it could not do was say HOW FAR: one fixed 20% and no way to ask for less or
  more. `dev/patch-8002.py` is the whole change, and it is deliberately thin - the
  engine 80.0.1 built (master gain after the limiters, `duckState()` on the plugin,
  the tap, the eight-second wait, the one-minute cap) is not touched.
- **THE LADDER STARTS ON THE OLD VALUE, ON PURPOSE.** `SC_DUCK_LEVELS =
  [0.2, 0.15, 0.25, 0.4]` and `assistantDuckLevel` boots to the first rung, which is
  exactly what 80.0.1 stepped to. A listener who never touches the button hears no
  difference at all after updating, and the gate pins that as a check of its own.
- **THE ENGINE READS A VARIABLE, NOT A CONSTANT.** The only line changed inside the
  duck is `scDuckSetLevel(SC_DUCK_LEVEL, true)` -> `scDuckSetLevel(assistantDuckLevel,
  true)`. Everything downstream - the ramp, the fallback to element volume on a build
  with no graph, the recording tap staying above the node - is 80.0.1's, unchanged.
- **A MID-DUCK CHANGE DOES NOT DROP THE DUCK.** Changing the depth while the music is
  stepped back calls the same `scDuckForAssistant` that applies a duck, so the new
  level is ramped in over the same short ramp - not released and re-applied, which
  would put the music at full volume for a breath in the middle of a sentence.
- **THE CHOICE IS A ROW, NOT A HIDDEN NUMBER.** Settings - More - Playback and sound
  gains "Step down to" under the Assistant duck switch, cycling 20 / 15 / 25 / 40 and
  written to its own meta row beside `assistantDuck`, so it also rides a library
  backup. A meta value off the ladder (a hand-edited row, an older file) falls back to
  the first rung instead of a level the engine would have to guess at.
- **THE NEW GATE MEASURES THE LAYER, NOT THE ENGINE.**
  `dev/assistant-duck-depth-check.cjs` (wired into the extra arm by
  `dev/patch-gate-8002.py`): **36/0** on this tree and **19 of its 36 checks FAIL on
  the pristine 80.0.1 page**, which is what makes it a measurement rather than a
  description. It boots the page three times - a fresh library, one stored at 15%, and
  one stored off the ladder at 33% - because a restore that is never exercised is not
  a restore. `assistant-duck-check` is untouched and still describes 80.0.1 exactly.
- **THE REPIN.** `dev/repin-8002.mjs`: the live pin moves 80.0.1 -> **80.0.2**, the
  adjacency `PREV` moves 80.0 -> **80.0.1**, and the quoted sweep runs after `PREV`
  and `OWN` are normalized, so a gate that describes its own release keeps describing
  it. 127 edits across 52 gate files, `--check` clean in 0.
- **THE OTA BUILD IS ONE PASS BEHIND BY DESIGN - WATCH THE SIZES.** The zip embeds a
  copy of root `manifest.json` that records the size of the zip it lives inside, so
  the first build after a page edit is stale by construction. Both channels are built
  until `--check` reports a fixed point, and the numbers in this entry are read from
  `ota/updates.json` and `ota-play/updates.json` after that point (root 1030072 bytes,
  Play 1030086).
- **AND THE COMMITTED BUNDLE IS NOW BYTE-STABLE, WHICH IT WAS NOT ON 80.0.1.**
  `dev/ota-update-check.cjs` regenerates the bundle and compares the zip's bytes;
  that check is RED on a pristine `git archive origin/main` (54 passed / 1 failed,
  `c8463c5e64 -> 7e45147cb9`), and the cause was in `dev/ota-fixpoint.mjs`: it
  seeded root `manifest.json` from `ota/updates.json` (`url: 'update.zip'`, relative
  to `ota/`) while `dev/ota-bundle.mjs` writes it back as `url: 'ota/update.zip'` -
  two forms of the same byte count, so every generation embedded the other one, the
  zip's size never moved, and a size-only fixed point declared victory while
  `deploy.yml` re-committed the bundle after every push. The fixpoint now seeds the
  form the build writes back: it settles on the first pass, two regenerations are
  byte-identical (root `871e94cb05`, Play `2798ca9045`), and the check is green at
  **55/0** on the bundle this release commits.
- **TWO PRE-EXISTING REDS, BOTH PROVEN NOT THIS RELEASE'S** (identical counts on a
  pristine `git archive origin/main`): `media-controls-check` **60 passed / 1
  failed**, "and it no longer fires every half hour"; `album-follow-dock-check` **104
  / 1**, "and its notes name what the release does" - a gate that requires the HEAD
  changelog entry to name the album pill dock, which is red on 80.0.1 for the same
  reason. Everything else in `dev/gates.sh` is green: 62 of 64 suites, plus
  `audit-calls` 0 unresolved and `check-dom` 0 integrity failures.
- **WHAT THIS RELEASE DOES NOT DO.** It does not change the four ways a duck ends, the
  cap, the call path, the native plugin, or the tap-to-release. It does not add a
  second duck engine: the deck-volume design built in this chat's 80.2 branch was
  deliberately dropped rather than shipped beside 80.0.1's master gain, because two
  things stepping the same music is how a volume bug starts. The Ask SideCut drawer
  and microphone work (80.1) is still not on this lineage and is not part of this
  release.
## 80.0.1 (October 20, 2026 · 11:35 PM EDT): the assistant duck - the music steps back for an assistant and comes back on its own

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR THIS, VERBATIM**: "when you like are talking to an ai such as
  holding down your power button to talk to gemeni or any ai, SideCut should let you talk
  to the ai while playing the music at a lower volume letting you talk to the ai and then
  at full volume when your done talking to the ai." The page half is `dev/patch-8001.py`;
  the native half is in `.github/workflows/patch-audiofocus.py`.
- **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, AND WHY IT WAS NOT JUST "TOO LOUD".** An assistant takes
  the audio the same way a call does, so Android sends the same `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`
  that a messaging blip sends (the 73.6 note explains why this app cannot tell them apart
  from the event alone). 73.6 answered that loss by ignoring it and putting the element
  back - correct for a blip, wrong for an assistant: the song came back at FULL volume over
  the person you were talking to. The duck is the missing third answer, and the system's
  own `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN` when the assistant stops is what ends it.
- **THE MASTER GAIN, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** `scDuckMaster` is one gain node between
  the limiters and `audioCtx.destination`; the limiters no longer land on the speakers
  directly. That is deliberate and it is the reason a single number can step the WHOLE mix
  back at once - both decks, the DJ Mode engine and the Studio chain all land on a limiter,
  and every one of them is above this node. **The element volume is NOT used when a graph
  exists**: the crossfade owns it, and writing it there would fight the blend. It is used
  only as a fallback on a build whose AudioContext never came up, and the original value is
  captured once and restored exactly. The recording tap stays on the limiter, so a
  recording or a SAVE COPY captures the UNDUCKED signal - a duck must never end up baked
  into a file.
- **THE FOUR WAYS A DUCK ENDS, AND THE CEILING.** The phone's own answer (the plugin's
  `duckState()`, polled only while a duck is held); eight seconds after the last signal;
  a tap anywhere (`pointerdown` in the capture phase, which never steals the press from a
  button under the finger); and - the one that matters - a hard ceiling of **60 seconds**
  from the first signal, however many arrive (`scDuckUntil = Math.min(now + HOLD,
  startedAt + MAX)`). Without that ceiling a stream of duck requests could hold the music
  quiet indefinitely. `scDuckApplied` is set BEFORE the level write, so the app's own gain
  change cannot be read back as a fresh signal and start a loop.
- **A CALL IS NOT AN ASSISTANT, AND THE STALE DUCK IS THE TRAP.** `scDuckForAssistant`
  refuses while a call is up, and `scStandDownForCall` now UNDUCKS as it pauses - without
  that, a duck held when a call starts would leave the resume-after-call path playing at
  20%. A permanent focus loss (another player keeping the speakers) unducks too, since the
  music is not coming back to be ducked. Both were found by the new gate, not by reading.
- **THE NATIVE HALF SAYS ONLY WHAT IT KNOWS.** `duckState()` answers "is the duck over?"
  from the last focus event it was sent plus the audio mode, and returns "over" only on
  POSITIVE evidence (a gain, or no call and no transient loss on record). A duck Android
  applied without telling anyone therefore leaves the web layer's own bounded wait in
  charge rather than being cancelled early. `holdingFocus` is tracked beside it.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/assistant-duck-check.cjs` (new, wired into the extra arm by
  `dev/patch-gate-8001.py`): **41/0** here and **19 of its checks FAIL on the pristine 80.0
  page** (the API is undefined, the master node is absent, the limiter lands on the
  destination), which is what makes it a measurement of the feature rather than a
  description of it. It drives the real page against a fake Web Audio graph, and it needed
  a real one - `audio-focus-check` had to be retargeted for the same reason, because with
  no graph the duck rides the element volume and the audit would have measured the
  fallback.
- **FOUR GATES PINNED WHAT THIS RELEASE CHANGES, AND ALL FOUR ARE RETARGETED, NOT
  WEAKENED** (owned by `dev/patch-gate-8001.py` so the release reproduces): `audio-focus`
  (the duck is obeyed now, through the master gain, with the song still playing and the
  element volume untouched), `test-70` (the limiter still reaches the speakers, through the
  master gain, and nothing bypasses it), `revamp-check` (it DESCRIBES 80.0, which is no
  longer the head, so it reads its own entry by version - the OWN split), and `test-736`
  (its transient-loss check read the log's LAST line and the duck now records its own line
  after it, so the log is scanned and both halves are pinned).
- **THE REPIN.** `dev/repin-8001.mjs`: `PREV_RELEASE` 80.0 -> **80.0.1**, the 29 adjacency
  gates move 75.1.2 -> **80.0**, and the historical gates stay put. Two lessons are in it.
  (1) **Adjacency is keyed on HOW a gate derives its neighbour, not on the text it
  contains**: `revamp-check` compares its OWN entry's neighbour, so it is not an adjacency
  gate and its `PREV` must not move - the set is `entries[1]` AND not `ownIdx`. (2) **`OWN`
  is a release name like `PREV`, not a stale pin**, so the quoted sweep must hold it out
  and the stale check must exempt it, or a gate that describes 80.0 gets rewritten to
  describe itself.
- **THE RELEASE REPRODUCES FROM THE 80.0 TIP.** `patch-8001.py` + `patch-gate-8001.py` +
  `repin-8001.mjs` + the OTA rebuild over a clean `git archive HEAD` checkout produce a
  tree that is **byte-for-byte identical, bundles included** (`diff -rq` clean). The
  native plugin file is owned by `patch-gate-8001.py` for exactly this reason - it is a
  hand-edited file that the release must be able to rebuild.
- **OTA, AND THE DEPLOY BUG THIS RELEASE UNCOVERED - READ THIS ONE.** The zip carries a
  copy of root `manifest.json`, and that manifest records the size of the zip it lives
  inside, so **one build is always one pass behind**: it seeds the embedded manifest from
  the PREVIOUS bundle's size. `--check` compares the two and fails. `deploy.yml` built the
  bundle once, **committed it**, and only THEN ran `--check` - so the publish step pushed a
  bundle that could not pass its own verification, the verify step failed, and both the
  Pages upload and the deploy were SKIPPED. That is why 80.0.1's first Deploy run is red
  (run 39543091189, step "Verify the published bundle is current") and why the site kept
  serving 80.0. **Fixed here**: `deploy.yml` now runs the repo's own `dev/ota-fixpoint.mjs`
  (seed from the built size, rebuild, repeat until a rebuild produces the size it was
  seeded with) BEFORE the commit, and the `--check` moved ABOVE the commit so a bundle
  that cannot pass is never pushed to main. The lesson generalises: **a publish step must
  verify before it commits, and it must run the same convergence the repo already has.**
- **THE BYTE COUNTS ARE TOOLCHAIN-SPECIFIC, SO TRUST CI'S.** This sandbox has no `zip`
  (see the shim note below), and the shim's output differs from the runner's real `zip`:
  locally the settled bundle is **1028909** sideload / **1028924** Play, while the
  PUBLISHED bundle - built by the runner's real `zip` and what actually ships - is
  **1028400** sideload / **1028415** Play. Both are self-consistent (the embedded manifest
  matches the zip), and what an installed app fetches is `ota/updates.json`, which is
  written from the real built size either way. **The committed bundle should be CI's** -
  do not fight it with a locally built one. A local `ota-update-check` byte-identity
  failure is this difference and not a defect.
- **THE DEPLOY IS GREEN AFTER THE FIX.** Run 39544845134: every step succeeded - the
  publish, the verify (now above the commit), the commit, the upload and the Pages deploy.
  The live `ota/updates.json` reads v80.0.1, and the live `ota/update.zip` is 1028400 bytes
  with an embedded manifest that agrees and an `index.html` carrying both `APP_VERSION
  = '80.0.1'` and `scDuckForAssistant`. The 80.0.1 fix reaches an installed app on the next
  poll.
- **ONE TRAP WORTH RECORDING**: `dev/test-66429.mjs` execs `ota-update-check`, which
  regenerates the bundle as its byte-identity test, so a run of it can leave the tree
  mid-cycle with the embedded manifest one pass behind - run the bundler after the
  battery, not only before.
- **THE SANDWICH NOTE**: this sandbox has no `zip`/`unzip` and no root, so `.shim/zip` and
  `.shim/unzip` (Python `zipfile`, gitignored) stand in. **The zip shim must APPEND**: the
  bundler builds the archive in three passes that accumulate, and a shim opening 'w' on
  every call produced a 52 KB bundle that was missing index.html entirely.
- **PRE-EXISTING REDS, ALL PROVEN NOT THIS RELEASE'S** (identical counts on a pristine
  80.0 checkout in /tmp/base800): `media-controls-check` 66/1 (the months-old "fires every
  half hour"), test-658 8, test-705 5, test-716 1, test-719 2, test-720/721/722/723 1 each,
  test-6641/6642/66422/66424/66425/66426 1-2 each, test-66428 1, test-6052 2, test-6058 1,
  test-60510 1, test-play 2, and test-7252's crash (`scPauseDeck is not defined` inside its
  own eval). `test-718` was red here and GREEN on pristine - a real regression - and it was
  the OTA manifests still naming 80.0; the rebuilt bundles fixed it (46/0).
- **VERIFIED GREEN HERE**: assistant-duck-check 41/0, audio-focus-check 47/0, revamp-check
  92/0, test-736 76/0, test-70 182/0, test-6643 90/0, studio-70-check 570/0, the whole
  extra arm, the OTA trio (guard 20/0, update 52/0, bootapply 24/0, loop 26/0),
  audit-calls OK (6161 declared names across 5 blocks), check-dom 0 integrity failures.
- **NOT VERIFIED ON A DEVICE.** jsdom has no real audio and no Android focus callbacks, so
  the duck is proven as a gain-node contract and as a driven page, not heard on a phone.
  The real test is holding the power button and talking to Gemini over a playing song, then
  taking a call mid-duck. The native half reaches a phone only in an APK built after this
  commit; the web half rides the OTA.
- **NEXT RELEASE**: `80.1` for the next feature, or `80.0.2` for a fix inside this one.
  Shell cache `sidecut-shell-v80.0.1`.

## 80.0 (October 20, 2026 · 6:06 PM EDT): the Massive Revamp - replayable milestones, Studio split down a diagonal, and a second layout that is always one tap from the original

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR ALL OF IT IN ONE RELEASE, WITH ONE RULE.** "one shot
  done", and "REMEMBER YOU SHOULD ALWAYS HAVE THE OPTION TO REVERT BACK TO THE OG
  WAY WITH TABS ON THE BOTTOM". So every new arrangement hangs off a body class
  the new block adds (`sc80-cloud`, `sc80-pa-grid`) and the ORIGINAL is the
  default: with both switches off the page is 75.1.2. Everything is in
  `dev/patch-800.py` + `dev/revamp-800.css` + `dev/revamp-800.js`.
- **MILESTONES.** A streak that reaches 3, 7, 14, 21, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200,
  250, 300, 365, 500, 730 or 1000 days now opens the app with a celebration made
  for that number: the number, the unit, three expanding rings and confetti, a
  line that says what the streak is. It plays once per milestone (the record is
  `localStorage.sc80Milestones`, days -> timestamp) so it stays a moment instead
  of a nag, and every milestone that has been reached is listed in Studio with
  its date and a Replay button. The boot check reads `__scStats()` and retries for
  ten seconds, because the streak loads out of IndexedDB and an early read is
  legitimately zero.
- **STUDIO IS TWO TABS, CUT ON THE DIAGONAL.** One pill, split corner to corner
  from the bottom right to the top left - the same diagonal the Library pill has
  carried since 70.0 - with Studio (the work: DJ, Crop, Edit rack, clip, cleanup,
  FX, karaoke, sampler, looper, sleep, practice) on one side and Tools on the
  other. Tools takes the badges wall, the storage cleaner, Auto-DJ, gestures, the
  batch tag editor, batch on selected, the milestones and the layout switches.
  `renderStudio` is wrapped AND watched by a MutationObserver, because the Studio
  block repaints itself from several places inside its own closure; the split is
  rebuilt on whichever of the two arrives first and the chosen tab is remembered.
- **PINNED ARTISTS, TWO WINDOWS.** Four in a row is still the default and still
  exactly 75.1.2. The new option is eight smaller squares in a 2 x 4 window with
  the rest scrolling. The rail also glides now: `scroll-behavior: smooth`, a mouse
  wheel that moves the rail instead of the page, and a snap that only engages
  once the scroll is already slowing down (a snap that fights a flick is what
  "not smooth" meant).
- **TABS THAT MOVE.** The dock carries one highlight layer that slides between
  pills by transform instead of four pills repainting their backgrounds, the pill
  and tab colours cross-fade over 280 ms, and the active library tab scrolls
  itself to the middle of the strip when the strip changes.
- **THE CLOUD LAYOUT.** Round floating bubbles on Home, the four tabs as a
  vertical glass dock down the right, the player keeping the bottom, and a small
  now bar in the top right with the track, the artist and play/pause. The header
  bell, refresh and gear move onto the listening-stats bubble beside the Ask
  SideCut sparkle and forward the real clicks; if the stats bubble is hidden they
  land on the greeting row, so Settings can never be unreachable. The "your files
  / no ads, ever" line is gone in this layout, which is what was asked for.
- **BACK TO THE ORIGINAL.** Both switches live in Settings -> More -> The new
  look, and again in Studio -> Tools -> Look and feel. They are live (no restart)
  and remembered in `sc80Layout` / `sc80PinnedLayout`.
- **PATCH NOTES HAVE A SECOND LAYER.** `items` stays an array of plain strings -
  one sentence each, which is what every gate and every older panel reads - and a
  parallel `details` array carries the explanation. `changelogRich()` pairs them
  and `scClItemHtml()` draws a `<details>` whose summary is the sentence. A note
  with no detail is still a plain bullet, so every release before 80.0 renders
  exactly as it did.
- **THE DUPLICATE UNSORTED TAB IS GONE.** The strip drew the virtual Unsorted tab
  and then walked the playlists object, which holds a real `Unsorted` key created
  the first time a song had no playlist. The stored key is storage, not a tab, so
  it is skipped by name and the virtual one is the only one that renders.
- **BIGGER SCREENS.** Breakpoints at 600, 760 and 1000 px: the bubble cloud goes
  three or four across, the panes keep a readable measure and centre, and a
  landscape phone shrinks the right-hand dock.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/revamp-check.cjs` boots the page in jsdom (87 checks): the
  80.0 notes are sentences with details long enough to be worth opening; one
  Unsorted tab with a real Unsorted key in playlists; the row is the default and

  the now bar and the three bubbles on the stats card and classic takes every one
  of them away; the celebration opens with the number, records itself, closes,

  split on the bottom-right-to-top-left diagonal with the six non-studio sections

  Settings switches work in both directions; nothing threw. `dev/patch-gate-800.py`

- **OTA.** The root bundle is `1023359` bytes and the Play channel is

- **ONE CARRIED RED, NOT CAUSED HERE.** `media-controls-check` fails "and it no
  longer fires every half hour" on `dev/native-updates.js`, which is untouched by

## 75.1.2 (October 20, 2026 · 6:32 AM EDT): four pinned artists at a time, and Ask SideCut reads the whole sentence

- **THE OWNER ASKED FOR TWO THINGS.** "ask SideCut should be smarter, pinned
  artists plateu should have 4 displayed at one time with scrolling potential
  unlimited". The rail is `dev/patch-7512-rail.py`; the drawer is
  `dev/patch-7512-ask.py`.
- **THE RAIL IS FOUR-UP, NOT FIXED-WIDTH.** The chips were 72px in a card that
  is about 316px wide on a phone, so the fourth artist was cut in half and the
  rail read as if it ended there. A chip is now
  `calc((100% - 3 * var(--pa-gap)) / 4)` of the rail itself, so exactly four sit
  inside the card and the fifth starts at the edge. Nothing is capped: the width
  comes from the container, not from how many pins there are, so two pins and
  twenty scroll the same way. `proximity` scroll snapping settles a swipe on a
  chip edge without fighting a fast flick. The header now carries the pin count,
  because "there is a fifth artist" used to be discoverable only by swiping.
- **THE DRAWER LEARNS THE REST OF A SENTENCE.** 75.1 could plan a playlist, a
  crossfade, DJ mode and an album. Anything else fell through to a single
  "Carry out: ..." step that the acting layer usually could not carry out, so Do
  it closed the drawer and said "Nothing was changed". Now: "play <song |
  artist | playlist>", shuffle and repeat, next/back/pause/resume, questions
  answered from the library's own numbers (songs, hours, playlists, pinned
  artists, albums, what is playing, most played), and the sentence AFTER a plan
  ("add these too", "take these out", "undo that", "make it 8").
  `lastRun`/`lastUndo` are what those follow-ups point at.
- **PLAY GOES THROUGH THE APP'S OWN PATHS.** `__scPlayPlaylist` opens a playlist
  as itself so the next song is the next song in it, and `__scPlayTrack` is the
  same tap-a-song path the Home bubbles use. Shuffle and repeat are written
  through `__scSetShuffle`/`__scSetRepeat`, which move the state the player's own
  buttons move - including the queue resync the shuffle button does - and report
  the old value so Undo can put it back.
- **IT STOPS PRETENDING.** A sentence it cannot carry out gets no Do it button:
  it says it cannot do that one and lists what it can. The knowledge base is only
  consulted for a real match now (`_aiFuzzyMatch` at 60, not its floor of 35,
  where one shared word scored 40 and "flibbertigibbet the garden hose" came back
  as a confident answer about the converter).
- **TOLERANCE, NOT GUESSING.** One edit is accepted on the long command words
  ("palylist", "shufle"), the crossfade takes a written number ("crossfade six

## 74.9 (October 17, 2026 · 11:49 PM EDT): Cropping needs no network to write a file, tagged WAVs play, the pill is the standard, Ask SideCut floats

- **THE OWNER'S REPORT, VERBATIM**: "after cropping a song it just doesn't play the song anymore fix that this is stupid it should be able to fuffil this
  simple ahh request it should be able to do everything", plus "The pill shape should be the standard for tabs on by default, pill should be smooth moving
  between tabs smoothly, and I wanna move this ask SideCut button somewhere else maybe I change up bubble and add overlaying bubbles and stuff".
- **THREE DEFECTS UNDER THE FIRST COMPLAINT, ALL PROVEN IN A REAL BROWSER** (`harness/crop-play-check.mjs`: import → play → drag the selection → save → it
  must keep playing → re-tap → reload → still plays; encoder reachable (stereo and mono) and BLOCKED - 42/42): (1) the save called the plain
  `scEncodeAudio`, which returns null when lamejs (a CDN script) has not arrived - offline it died with "encoder produced no output" and nothing was
  cropped; it now runs `scEncodeAudioCooperative` (loads the encoder itself, yields between slices) and falls back to WAV when MP3 is ungettable. (2)
  **THE TAGGED-WAV SIZE FIELD WAS WRONG TWICE**: the RIFF writers padded an odd ID3 chunk but recorded the UNPADDED length, BIG-endian - a 41-byte tag read
  as 0x29000000 (687 MB), the chunk ran off the end of the file, and Chromium refused the WAV wholesale (error 4). Both WAV writers now store little-endian
  padded sizes (AIFF keeps big-endian - FORM is big-endian - and gains the pad byte). This had made EVERY tagged WAV the app wrote unplayable: crops,
  conversions, clips. (3) the resume-after-crop swallowed `play()` rejections and seeked before metadata existed; it now runs `recoverAudio` and waits for
  `loadedmetadata`.
- **THE PILL IS THE DEFAULT.** `sidecut_dockPill` reads on unless explicitly '0', so fresh installs arrive joined; the Gestures switch still takes the dock
  apart and writes '0'. The glide is proven by sampling the thumb MID-transition (110ms into the 0.24s spring it sits strictly between the two tabs) -
  `harness/v749-ui-check.mjs`, **13/13**.
- **ASK SIDECUT MOVES TO BUBBLES.** The Home-header sparkle is gone; the same button (same id, so the delegated drawer listener and `ai-button-check` 40/0
  keep working) floats bottom-right above dock+player (`#scAskBubbles`, fixed, `--sc-dock-h` stack), with two smaller overlaying bubbles peeking behind it

## 74.8 (October 17, 2026 · 5:20 PM EDT): Listening time follows the song, not the app window

- **THE OWNER'S REPORT**: "the listening stats aren't working in SideCut like it doesn't go up in time when I'm listening outside of the app or with headphones
  like it should". Two independent blockages, both in the page: the counter itself began `if(document.hidden) return;` ("Don't count time when app is
  backgrounded" - exactly backwards for a player), **and** the battery saver at the top clears every interval over 500 ms while hidden, listing the listening
  counter among the timers it stops. Either one alone was enough; with the screen off, neither the guard nor the timer let a second through.
- **THE CLOCK NOW.** It is the playhead against the wall clock, not a count of ticks: each tick banks `min(position moved, real time passed + 0.5s)` with a
  fractional carry, so a tick the OS throttled to once a minute still banks the whole minute, and a span the WebView was frozen through is recovered by the next
  tick instead of lost. A seek forward is not listening and a seek back is not a debt (the wall-clock bound), pausing adds nothing, and no source adds nothing.
  The timer asks the saver to keep it alive (`window.__scKeepAliveTimer`), the partial second is banked on `visibilitychange`, `pagehide`, `pause` and `ended`,
  and the total is persisted every 30 counted seconds instead of every 60 ticks. `checkPendingPlay()` runs in the same tick, so plays from the lock screen count.
- **THE GATE.** `dev/listen-time-check.cjs` (wired into `dev/gates.sh`) drives the shipped clock through a fake `Date.now` and a stubbed media element:
  ten backgrounded seconds add ten, a **ten-minute freeze** is recovered by one tick, pause/seek/no-source add nothing, and `window.__scStats().listenSeconds`
  is the number the stats screen reads. **12/0** here, **6 named reds** on the shipped 74.7 page (no drivable clock, the guard still there, no keep-alive, and
  the rest cannot run).
- **PROVEN BY THE REDS, NOT BY READING.** The first draft of the gate asserted ten seconds while advancing the playhead a second per 6 ms of wall clock - the
  clock correctly paid 5.06 and the gate was wrong; the harness now moves both clocks together, which is what "playing" means.
- **VERIFIED ON THE SHIPPED TREE**: the full battery, **56 suites green** (ai-button 40/0, listen-time 12/0, album-follow 105/0, check-dom 0, audit-calls 9016
  comments). Two reds, both carried or environmental: `media-controls-check` 66/1 (the months-old half-hour failure) and `ota-guard-check` once under load
  (17/3, then **4 consecutive runs at 20/0**, including three in a row after the battery) - timing-sensitive, not version-sensitive. OTA at a fixed point:
  **992776** (`ota/` + root manifests) / **992788** (`ota-play/`), both `--check`s OK with 6 notes each.
- **NOT VERIFIED**: nothing ran on a phone. Background counting is proven with a fake clock in jsdom, not with the screen actually off; the real test is one
  song played with the phone locked, then looking at Total listening time.
- **NEXT RELEASE**: `74.9` for another fix inside 74.8, or `75.0` for the next feature. Shell cache `sidecut-shell-v74.8`.

## 74.7 (October 17, 2026 · 4:52 PM EDT): The Ask drawer was invisible - the button worked, and only the keyboard showed

- **THE OWNER, THE SAME WORDS TWICE**: "the ai button literally doesn't do anything ... only the keyboard randomly open[s] up". 74.6's fix - the multi-select bar's
  sparkle had lost its listener to a redraw - was a real bug and is still right, but it was **not** what he was describing. This is: the drawer opened on both
  sparkles, focused its input, and painted nothing.
- **WHY.** The drawer is built from the studio's sheet component, `.sc-sheet`, which ships **hidden** (`opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px)`) and is revealed only
  by `.sc-sheet-backdrop.in .sc-sheet`. Ask SideCut's backdrop is `#scAiBackdrop`, not `.sc-sheet-backdrop`, so that reveal never matched. `open()` appended the
  drawer, added `in` to the backdrop, and focused the input 60 ms later (the keyboard), while the sheet itself stayed a fully transparent layer over most of the
  screen. A thumb sees nothing; the keyboard is the only evidence anything happened.
- **PROVEN ON THE SHIPPED 74.6 BUNDLE** before the change: jsdom resolves the cascade, and `getComputedStyle(#scAiSheet).opacity` was **"0"** with the backdrop
  `in`; after the one rule it is **"1"** (`transform` goes from `translateY(14px)` to `translateY(0)`). `dev/patch-747-ask-visible.py` is the edit.
- **WHY 74.6 DID NOT CATCH IT.** `dev/ai-button-check.cjs` asked for the class `in`, the input, and a plan - all true of an invisible drawer. It now reads the
  **computed opacity** at both ways in (Home header and the bar): **40/0** here, **2 named reds** on the shipped 74.6 page (`[0]` both times). Presence, class and
  focus are not visibility; the cascade is.
- **THE RELEASE.** `dev/patch-747.py` (74.7, `sidecut-shell-v74.7`, eight head notes) and `dev/repin-747.mjs` (111 edits across 79 gates). OTA at a fixed point:

- **VERIFIED ON THE SHIPPED TREE**: `ai-button-check` 40/0, `album-follow-dock-check` 105/0, the rest of the battery green - 56 suites exit 0. The **only** red is
  the carried `media-controls-check` 66/1 ("fires every half hour"), months old and untouched here.
- **NOT VERIFIED**: nothing ran on a phone. The proof is the cascade in jsdom plus the gate that reads it; the felt result of the drawer appearing under a thumb is
  the owner's to confirm once the published bundle he polls has moved, which is this commit.

  away the first time the bar was drawn. The 33/0 gate missed it because it only asked that the button **existed** (`ok(!!doc.getElementById('selectAskBtn'))`) and
  never pressed it: presence is not a handler.
- **THE FIX.** One delegated listener on `document` (capture phase, and the click stops there so the drawer opens on the tap that asked for it), matching either id
  on the way up. A re-render can no longer strand it, and the header goes through the same path so the two cannot drift. `dev/patch-746-ask.py` is the edit
  (`--check` probes the shipped page).

  with three, and reads the context chip both times. **38/0** here; **5 named reds** on the shipped 74.5 page (bar button opens it, its context, the redrawn one,
  its context, and the count) while the header check stays green - the control that proves the red is this bug and not the harness.
- **THE RELEASE.** `dev/patch-746.py` (74.6, `sidecut-shell-v74.6`, eight head notes) and `dev/repin-746.mjs` (110 edits across 78 gates, then one more:

## 74.1.9 (October 16, 2026): The album follows the song, the views arrive, the dock can be one pill - and two repairs the same owner asked for

- **THE SECOND ROUND OF 74.1.9: "make the app nicer to use", and three faults on the destructive paths.** Found by following what a thumb presses, then proven on
  the page before the change. (1) **"Clear playlist" and "Delete all songs" removed nothing and said "Deleted"**: both are drawn only in the playlist / All Songs view
  and both call `deleteAllInView()`, whose whole body is an `if(libraryMode === 'albums')` branch followed by `toast('Deleted')` - so in the two places they exist the
  branch was false. Driven on the old page with `window.confirm` stubbed to **true**, Clear playlist on a three-song list left the list unchanged and the toast read
  `"Deleted"`. (2) **every song delete asked through `window.confirm()`**, which this file documents the Android WebView as swallowing (it returns false) - the exact
  reason `modalConfirm()` was added for playlist delete in 71.9; the covers reset, both "album already exists - merge?" paths and the update-reload prompt were the last
  four, and the page now has **no `confirm(` call at all**. (3) **a delete was final.** `scDeleteSongs()` is the one path now (deleteTrack and deleteAllInView both
  route through it): it asks in the app, snapshots the track at its index, its index in **every** playlist, its queue slot and its IndexedDB record (`dbGet` before
  `dbDelete`), and `scUndoSongDelete()` puts all of it back - a fresh object URL, memberships spliced at their old indexes, the record written back so it survives a
  restart, and the now bar back with the song paused if it was the one playing. `deleteAllInView`'s three cases now keep three different promises (clear the playlist /
  delete from the library / remove from albums with per-id album positions restored by Undo), and the duplicates review is one delete with one undo.
- **THE GATE THAT DRIVES IT:** `dev/undo-delete-check.cjs` (wired into `dev/gates.sh`) presses the row kebab, the confirm sheet and the toast's Undo: **56/0** on this
  tree, **17 named reds** on the pre-change page. The old-page control above is the bug in one line: unchanged storage, rows still on screen, toast `"Deleted"`.
  `dev/patch-74110-destructive.py` is the record of the 11 edits (`--check` probes the shipped tree). The toast is a `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region and can
  be flicked up (24px) without the click that follows opening the song list behind it.
- **HARNESS NOTE FOR THIS WORKSPACE.** The full battery needs **jsdom 30** (for `requestInterceptor` and for this page's modern CSS - jsdom 26 reports
  `Could not parse CSS stylesheet` on a stylesheet this tree did not touch) and `acorn` resolvable from the repo. With both, `sh dev/gates.sh` is green except the
  carried `media-controls-check` failure, which a pristine `git show HEAD:index.html` reproduces. OTA after the whole release: **984 576** bytes sideload, **984 586** Play,
  fixed point reached in two passes.
- **THE BUBBLE SIZE THAT WAS MISSING, AND THE RESET THAT DID NOT RESET.** *"there should be like an inbetween settings for the bubble size like in the middle but without all that
  gap but not too little"*. Home jumped automatic **118px** -> tall **158px** with nothing between, and Sandbox's height stepper moved in whole 118px steps (118 or 236 - the
  card-with-a-hole). Now: a **Medium** preset at **146px** (`hb-size-medium`, in the expand chip's cycle between small and automatic, with `justify-content:center` so its extra
  height is shared above and below the words), and **half steps** on H (`HB_EXACT_STEP = 0.5`, so 1.5x = 177px, stored as a clean 1.5). The chip's walk gained Medium and the
  first tap on an untouched bubble still goes to tall. While driving it, the gate found that **`Reset to automatic` cleared only `homeBubbleExact`** - the chip's presets live in
  `homeBubbleSizes`, so a chip-sized bubble stayed sized while the toast promised otherwise; it clears both now. `dev/home-bubble-size-check.cjs` (in `dev/gates.sh`): **23/0** here,

- **THE AI BUTTON, BUILT: ASK SIDECUT.** *"do the ai thig push that"*. The drawer lives in the Studio block beside `window.SCACT`: a sparkle in the **Home header**
  (`#homeAiBtn`) and one on the **multi-select bar** (`#selectAskBtn`) open `#scAiBackdrop`, whose context chip names the selection. A sentence becomes a **PLAN** of typed

  declared grammar, not a model; a question falls through to the shipped knowledge base (`__scAiLookup`).
- **THE AI BUTTON IS SAVED, NOT BUILT.** The owner's *"ai button that I can ask anything with like my songs and it'll do it ... save that idea for later"* is written up
  in `AI_ASSISTANT_PLAN.md`: what already exists (the Settings -> Support assistant, the 70.0 acting commands), what is missing (a way in from the music, the library as
  context, a typed tool surface, a preview + undo for bulk plans), and the gates it would need. Nothing in this release touches the assistant.

- **Two messages, one release.** The first asked for three things (the album to follow the song, the views to arrive smoothly, a pill dock under Studio -> Gestures); they
  are section 1-3 of `dev/release-entry.md`, pinned by the gate block `[11s]` and driven by `dev/album-follow-dock-check.cjs`. The second message arrived from the phone
  while the release was being prepared: *"frequent lag spikes inside the app while doing multiple things simultaneously"*, and *"the Spotify to mp3 converter will
  frequently confuse songs by the same artist while downloading a song and often duplicate the same song in different metadata, this often happens when downloading albums
  ... it should download the correct audio"*. Both are in 74.1.9, and both are their own section of `dev/patch-7419-page.py`.
- **THE CONVERTER'S IDENTITY WAS A SUBSTRING TEST, AND AN ALBUM IS WHERE IT SHOWS.** One album is one artist's whole run, so `scArtistMatch` cannot separate its tracks, and
  the length gate is +-60s - two tracks of one record routinely sit seconds apart. That leaves the title gate as the only thing between them, and **both** title gates
  (`scTitleMatch`, and `scTitleStrong`, which is what lets a 15-60s-off decode stand in as the closest cut) asked `vt.indexOf(want) !== -1`: `"Yaar"` is contained in
  `"Yaarian"`, `"Pind"` in `"Pind Waliyan"`. Track A therefore accepted B's upload, and 72.5's own run guard then refused B *its own source* as already claimed by a
  sibling - one audio file filed twice under two sets of tags. **The guard was not the bug; the gate that let the wrong upload in was, and the guard is what turned one
  mis-attribution into the duplicate the owner sees about once an album.** Containment is now a **run of whole words** (space-padded, in both gates) and the word-overlap
  fallback counts words rather than substrings. A **shared whole word** is deliberately still accepted by the title gate - `"Pind"` IS a word of `"Pind Waliyan"` - and
  what takes that upload away from the short track is the run's claim, which is the second guard of the pair.
- **THE SLICE THE UI GETS BACK.** The cooperative encoders hold the main thread for `SC_ENCODE_SLICE_MS` (90ms) at a time, which is about five dropped frames, and every
  file this app makes goes through them: the app stuttered for as long as a file was being made. While the page is **visible** the budget is now one frame
  (`SC_ENCODE_FRAME_MS = 12`, read at both call sites as `document.hidden ? SC_ENCODE_SLICE_MS * scBackSliceMul() : SC_ENCODE_FRAME_MS`); while it is **hidden** the budget
  is exactly what it was - a hidden page has no frames to drop, and the long slice is what makes background work finish soonest, which is the reasoning 66.0 recorded when it
  moved 55 -> 90. `test-662`'s 90ms pin is therefore **not** moved. Since a smaller slice pays the wake-up more often, `scYieldToUI()` is a `MessageChannel` macrotask now
  (a browser clamps nested timers to 4ms and may paint between macrotasks) with the `setTimeout(0)` fallback kept underneath.
- **MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED.** `dev/converter-identity-check.cjs` slices the three deciding functions out of the shipped page and runs them for real: **37/0** on the prepared
  tree, **26/11** on the same page with the four edits undone (the bug cases red, the pins that predate 74.1.9 green). The same file drives the page's own slice logic and
  its own `scYieldToUI()` over calibrated synthetic work: the longest unbroken block of main thread fell from **106ms to 19ms**, the number of wake-ups rose from 16 to 100,
  and the wall clock for the same work moved by a few percent. `studio-70-check` is **570/0**, 55 of its checks in `[11s]`.
- **A STAMPED LYRIC SHEET WAS TRUSTED, AND THE NUDGE COULD NOT REACH THE ERROR.** The third report against this release: *"the lyrics for multi language songs is crazy it like
  doesn't play for 50 seconds while the audio is already playing and then starts really late and the lyrics needs to be accurate"*. `showLyrics()` re-timed a sheet only when it had
  NO stamps (or looked like the old even split), so a sheet that carried its own timings - LRCLIB's synced entry, or one the model timed - went on screen unmeasured, and the only
  correction on offer was the per-song nudge, **clamped to +-15s**, which is narrower than the error it exists to fix. Both halves are fixed: `scLyricsSheetOffset` measures a
  stamped sheet against the recording (`scAutoAlignLyricsToAudio`, called from that same branch, skipped entirely for a sheet the owner pinned by hand with Line up), and the
  ceiling is `SC_LYRICS_OFF_MAX = 120`.
- **THE MEASUREMENT THAT DID NOT WORK, AND WHY THE PROBE IS THE POINT.** The first cut matched every stamp to its NEAREST onset and took the median difference. A sheet fifty
  seconds late is late into a different part of the singing, where every line still has an onset a second away, so every per-line difference came back ~0 and the sheet measured as
  PERFECT - `dev/lyrics-timing-check.cjs` came back red on the case it was written for, on its first run. What a uniform offset does move is the SHAPE of the song, so that is what
  is measured now: where the singing runs (the same envelope and quiet floor the layout already uses, `scFindQuietGaps`), against where the words begin. The recording's own length
  cannot be the second half of the question either, because a late sheet's tail is past the end of THIS file by exactly the amount it is late - so what is checked instead is that
  the shifted words stay inside the song. A miss smaller than 8s is left alone (that is the nudge's job), a sheet whose words would land in a measured break, run past the singing,
  or leave the singing uncovered is refused rather than forced, and a song with a long instrumental opening is not touched at all: its own singing starts late too, so the difference
  is zero.
- **THE CARD THAT APPEARS WHEN A SONG IS SAVED now leads with the ACTION.** *"the in tab thing that shows up after you download a song should be replaced with open library"*.
  `scConvertPillDone` had the run's sentence as the pill's TITLE and the way into the library as small print under it, so the one thing anyone wants at the end of a save read as a
  report. The title is `Open library` now, the run's sentence sits underneath it with `· tap to open`, and the tap-through - `scOpenLibraryAfterDownload()` - is unchanged. The flag
  (`_opened` - *did this run fill the library?*) is worked out BEFORE the label is written, which is the one ordering a later edit could get wrong.
- **THE HALF OF THAT CARD THAT WAS ALREADY WRONG, AND ONLY SHOWED UP ONCE THE LABEL WAS THE ACTION.** `_opened` was a SUBSTRING test on the run's own sentence -
  `/library|added/` - so `"Cancelled - nothing was added"` counted as a filled library (it contains "added"), and so did the batch line for a run where every track failed,
  `"0 songs added to your library - 3 failed"`. On 74.1.8 that misreading was small print under a report; with the action as the title it would have been the pill's whole face, and
  the note above ("a run that saved nothing keeps its own text") would have been false, so it is fixed here rather than described. The test refuses the count as well as the words
  (`!/could not|nothing was added|(\D|^)0 songs/` - the `\D` so that "10 songs added" still counts), a run stopped part-way with songs saved still leads with `Open library`, and
  `[11s]` section (8) DRIVES the real function - `scConvertPillDone` is sliced out of the shipped bytes and run over a synthetic pill - for all four shapes: the label, the small
  print and what a tap actually does are read from the code that ships, not from bytes that describe it. **Proven both ways**: with only this guard undone, `studio-70-check` is
  **567 passed / 3 failed** - the byte pin and both of the driven shapes that should be red - while the filled run and the run stopped part-way stay green (that page is the
  shipped page with one `_opened` line put back, and nothing else).
- **WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** Nothing here ran on a phone. The converter fix is proven at the level of the gates that decide, not by converting a real album end to end, and the
  stall figures are this harness's, not a phone's - the felt difference while scrolling during a conversion is still the owner's to judge.

## 74.1.8 (October 15, 2026 · 7:56 PM EDT): Re-encode works again - the slice helper the encoders call lives with them now

- **The report, in the owner's words** (a screenshot of the phone): *"Re-encode failed: scBackSliceMul is not defined"*. Every song, every rate. 74.1.7 shipped a storage
  cleaner whose Re-encode button could not compress anything at all.
- **THE CAUSE, BECAUSE THE CAUSE IS THE RELEASE.** The page is four inline `<script>` blocks and each one is its own program with its own scope. 74.1.7 added
  `scBackSliceMul` - the hidden-slice multiplier that makes a background compress do three slices of work per wake-up - to the **last** block, the Studio module, beside
  the rest of the background job. The two encoders that read the slice budget (`scEncodeMp3Cooperative`'s block loop and `scEncodeWavCooperative`'s sample loop) live in the
  **first**, the app's own 2.5 MB script. A bare identifier is resolved lexically, in the scope of the function that *uses* it, and never in the scope of whichever block
  published a reference to it - so both encoders threw. **It threw on the FIRST block of the loop, not late**, because the slice test is
  `Date.now() - sliceStart >= SC_ENCODE_SLICE_MS * scBackSliceMul()` and `>=` evaluates both of its sides: the multiplier is called whether or not a slice is due. That is
  why every re-encode failed instantly and uniformly, rather than a long one failing after a while. Nothing was damaged - the throw came before a single byte - but the button
  did nothing, on the whole library.
- **WHY THE GATES SAW NOTHING, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** 74.1.7's own block `[6f]` drove the job with `win.__scEncodeMp3` **stubbed**, so the real encoder never ran;
  and its question about the multiplier went through `SC70.backSliceMul()` - the *module's* own copy, which was defined, and answered 1 and 3 correctly. **The gate asked the
  module about itself, and the module passed.** The feature every check pointed at was never executed. A stub in the place of the thing under test is not coverage of it.
- **THE FIX IS ONE FUNCTION MOVING HOUSE.** The real `scBackSliceMul` is defined in the app's own block, beside both call sites, and published as `window.__scBackSliceMul`
  the same way `__scEncodeMp3` already was; the Studio's copy becomes a six-line alias that reads the published function **at call time**, so there is one implementation and
  no second copy to drift. Nothing else on the page changed: not the rates, not the sheet, not the job, not the lock, not the record, not the reorder.
- **THE NEW GATE `[6g]` ASKS THE PAGE THREE QUESTIONS, in order of how general they are**, and the first is the one that would have caught this without knowing anything
  about it: **no inline script block may call an `sc`-prefixed helper that only another block defines.** It needs no list of names to keep up to date, and on 74.1.7 it named
  `scBackSliceMul` **and nothing else in the whole 3.2 MB page**. Then it proves the published function is *live* (it overwrites `window.__scBackSliceMul` and requires
  `SC70.backSliceMul()` to go through the overwrite - a copy cannot pass that), and finally it **runs a real re-encode with only `lamejs` stood in for** - the CDN script jsdom
  never loads, which is the same stand-in the app's own engine is - through the app's decoder, its cooperative block loop, its slice boundary, its job record and its file swap.
- **PROVEN BOTH WAYS IN REHEARSAL, like the layout gate 74.1.7 added.** With the 74.1.7 page and only this gate added: **506 passed, 9 FAILED**, and one of the nine is the
  phone's own message reproduced word for word - `a re-encode through the real encoder does not report a failure (Re-encode failed: scBackSliceMul is not defined)`. On the
  prepared tree: **515 passed, 0 failed**, `[6g]`'s fifteen checks included. The gate also had to be made crash-proof to earn this: its first draft called the published
  function directly, and on 74.1.7 that `TypeError` killed the suite and cost the reader the eleven blocks after it - a red must be a report, not an exception.
- **THE RELEASE BATTERY**: 51 suites, every one green except the single red this repository has carried for months - `studio-70-check` **515/0** (fifteen of those checks are `[6g]`),
  `ota-update-check` 52/0, `check-dom` 0 failures, `ota-guard-check` 20/0, `ota-bootapply-check` 24/0 - and the release's own report is committed at `dev/gates-report.txt`.
- **WHAT THIS FIX DOES *NOT* CLAIM.** Nothing here ran on a phone. That the re-encode works is proven in jsdom through the real encoder *and* in the shipped bytes; how it
  feels under a thumb is unconfirmed. The background caveat 74.1.7 recorded still stands untouched: a WebView with no foreground service can be killed outright by Android,
  and a killed run is reported rather than resumed automatically.
- **BOTH CHANNELS SHIP TOGETHER**: `ota/update.zip` and `ota-play/update.zip` are rebuilt from this page to a true fixed point (the zip embeds the root `manifest.json`, which
  records the zip's own size), at 976033 bytes for the sideload channel and 976045 for the Play one, and the page inside each carries `APP_VERSION` and, for Play,
  `__PLAY_BUILD__`.
- **ONE RED IS RECORDED AND NOT FIXED**: `dev/media-controls-check.cjs`, "and it no longer fires every half hour", 66 passed / 1 failed - the same single failure a pristine
  clone of main reproduces.
- **Nothing else moved**: the player, the albums, the home widget, the letter-by-letter lyrics and every saved song and setting are where 74.1.7 left them.
## 74.1.7 (October 15, 2026 · 6:57 PM EDT): a compress that carries on, a Re-encode button that asks the rate, and playlists you can reorder

- **The asks, in the owner's words** (from a screenshot of Studio on the phone, then two more messages): *"it should be able to re encode in the background and it looks really weird fix it why are their
  protruding lines"*, *"have an option to re encode to a higher quality various options should appear"*, *"you should be able to reorder playlists in manage playlists"*. Four things, one release.
- **THE PROTRUDING LINES WERE THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN REGRESSION, AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING WHY.** 74.1.6 turned the left of a cleaner row into a `<button>` so the tap that aims at a song name lands on
  the song - and a button may only hold phrasing content, so the name and the artist became `<span>`s. A span lays out **inline**, and an inline box ignores `overflow: hidden` and
  `text-overflow: ellipsis` *completely*: the nowrap text painted straight across the Re-encode button and off the right of the screen, which is exactly what the screenshot shows. The two lines are
  `display: block` again, the text column clips, and the row itself clips as a last resort, so nothing a song is called can leave the row.
- **THE GATE THAT CATCHES IT READS COMPUTED DISPLAY, NOT TEXT.** jsdom has no layout engine, so a screenshot cannot be taken in it - but `getComputedStyle` does resolve the page's own stylesheet, and
  "this line is an inline box" is the fault itself. Block [6c] of `dev/studio-70-check.cjs` walks every row's three text boxes and fails if any of them is inline. **Proven both ways in rehearsal**:
  500/0 on the prepared tree, and 497/3 with only those two `display: block` declarations removed - and the three that go red are precisely the three that name the fault
  (`.sc-store-name:inline, .sc-store-sub:inline`).
- **THE RE-ENCODE BUTTON ASKS WHICH RATE NOW, 96 TO 320 KBPS.** `REENCODE_RATES` is `[96, 128, 160, 192, 256, 320]`, and the button opens a sheet under its own row: each rate says what it would do to
  **that** song in MB, worked out from its own length (`scEstDelta`), with the rate set at the bottom of the cleaner marked as such. A rate **above** what the file already reads is offered and named for
  what it is - `grows the file by 2.0 MB`, in coral, with the reason on the row - because re-encoding a 128 kbps file at 320 cannot put back detail the first encode threw away. The sheet says that once,
  plainly, rather than dressing it up as an upgrade.
- **A COMPRESS CARRIES ON WHEN YOU LEAVE THE APP.** The job holds a **Web Lock** (`sidecut-reencode`, exclusive) for its whole life - a page holding a lock is exempt from the browser's background
  freeze and intensive timer throttling, which is the difference between a compress that finishes in your pocket and one that stalls when the screen goes off - and the **slice budget triples while the
  page is hidden** (`scBackSliceMul`: a hidden page is woken less often, so each wake-up does three slices of work for the same wall clock).
- **IT SAYS WHERE IT IS, AND IT NEVER HALF-WRITES A SONG.** The cleaner carries a strip with the song, the rate and the percentage the encoder reported, and the row's own button reads `Encoding…` until it
  is done. The run is written to `sidecut_encodeJob` **before its first byte** and cleared when it ends; if the phone kills the app outright, the next render of the cleaner says so, names the song, says the
  song itself was never touched (the stored file is only replaced after the encoder has produced its bytes) and offers the same rate again - said once, not as a banner.
- **WHAT THE BACKGROUND FIX DOES *NOT* CLAIM.** The Web Lock is what the platform honours; an Android WebView with no foreground service can still be killed outright by the OS, and a killed run is not
  restarted automatically (it is reported, with the file untouched). Nothing here was tested on a device - the job, its lock and its record are driven in jsdom, and the shipped bytes are proven by the
  bundle; how it feels under a thumb on the phone is unconfirmed.
- **PLAYLISTS CAN BE REORDERED FROM MANAGE PLAYLISTS.** A `Reorder` control turns the panel into a list of names with `▲`/`▼` arrows - the panel's rows already carry up to five buttons, and a sixth and
  seventh would leave no room for the name. The move writes the **same order the tab strip's own drag writes** (`playlists` + the `meta` row), the Library tabs follow it, and Library and Favorites stay
  first: they are pinned by every path in the app, so their arrows are honestly disabled (`always first`) rather than silently doing nothing.
- **REGRESSION COVERAGE**: the release's own blocks `[6c]`–`[6f]` in `dev/studio-70-check.cjs`, 75 new checks, **500/0** for the file. `[6f]` stubs `navigator.locks` and proves the lock is taken *before*
  the encode and **held while it runs**, that the run is written down, that a killed run is reported once - the parts a machine without a phone can hold the app to.
- **ONE BEHAVIOUR PIN MOVED, AND IT IS RECORDED**: 74.1.6's block [6b] tapped the Re-encode button and expected an encode at once. That door is one tap longer now (the sheet opens, the sheet's rate runs),
  so `dev/repin-7417.mjs` walks it through - what that block exists to prove, that the tap which opens the bubble never swallows the button beside it, is unchanged.
- **THE RELEASE ORDER BUG THAT COST 74.1.5 SEVERAL RUNS IS FIXED AND RECORDED.** `dev/ota-update-check.cjs` asserts the tree's OWN bundle is already on `index.html`'s `APP_VERSION`, and the release
  rebuilt the bundles AFTER the battery - so every run died on that one suite ("manifest v74.1 vs APP_VERSION v74.1.5") and passed 52/0 re-run alone, because that suite regenerates the bundle itself and
  leaves the tree fixed for the next reader. The rebuild now runs BEFORE the battery, because the battery has to measure the tree that gets committed. It was never a flake.
- **THE RELEASE MACHINERY IS GENERIC NOW.** `dev/release-gates.sh` (the battery and its report), `dev/release-record.py` (the AGENTS.md insert, idempotent, version read from the page) and
  `.github/workflows/release.yml` are shared by every release; a release supplies its own `dev/patch-<ver>.py`, `dev/repin-<ver>.mjs`, `dev/release-<ver>.proof` (the proof of the prepared tree, byte for
  byte) and this entry.

## 74.1.6 (October 15, 2026 · 4:11 PM EDT): a song in the storage cleaner opens its own bubble

- **The ask, in one line** (from a screenshot of Studio on the phone): *"I should be able to click on the name of the song and the bubble for it pops up showing the mb and full
  artist name."* The row it pointed at read `Karan Aujla, Mxrci, Seshnolan ...` and `Alka Yagnik, Illa Arun · 19.7 MB...` - both clipped, because a cleaner row is ONE line of a
  24-row list with a Re-encode button at the end of it.
- **What the bubble shows**: the whole song name and every artist in full, the exact size on this phone in MB, the length, the album when the song has one, how many kbps the file
  reads at (bytes x 8 / seconds - nothing here trusts a tag, because a tag can say anything), and what the button beside the row would win at the bitrate already chosen above:
  `wins back 1.6 MB`, or plain `nothing to win` when the file is already at or under that rate.
- **THE ROW IS A DOOR NOW, AND THE DOOR IS A BUTTON.** The cover, the name and the line under it are one `<button data-act="storeinfo">` with `aria-expanded`, so a keyboard and a
  screen reader reach it and the tap a person aims at the song name lands on the song. The Re-encode button is a second control beside it and keeps its own job - the tap never
  swallows it. One bubble at a time: tapping the same row closes it, tapping another moves it. The bubble is the row's immediate next sibling in the cleaner list, which is what makes
  it read as hanging under that row.
- **WHY THE BUBBLE IS THE ONLY PLACE THOSE TWO THINGS CAN BE READ.** `.sc-store-name` and `.sc-store-sub` clip with `text-overflow: ellipsis` on purpose; `.sc-info-name` and
  `.sc-info-artist` set `white-space: normal` and never clip. That pair of rules IS the feature, so the gate checks the stylesheet and not only the text - jsdom has no layout, and a
  `textContent` check cannot see an ellipsis.
- **THE GATE DRIVES IT, IN `dev/studio-70-check.cjs` BLOCK [6b].** It makes one song's credit a six-name string and its file 4 MB, then: taps the row, reads the bubble, and holds it
  to arithmetic computed in the test itself rather than to the app's own formatter (4.0 MB, 2:37, about 214 kbps, `wins back 1.6 MB at 128 kbps`); checks the row clips and the
  bubble does not; closes it; moves it to another song; and clicks the Re-encode button to prove the tap target did not eat it. 27 new checks, 425 in the file, all green.
- **THE RELEASE ORDER BUG THAT COST 74.1.5 SEVERAL RUNS IS FIXED AND RECORDED.** `dev/ota-update-check.cjs` asserts the tree's OWN bundle is already on `index.html`'s
  `APP_VERSION`, and the release rebuilt the bundles AFTER the battery - so every run died on that one suite ("manifest v74.1 vs APP_VERSION v74.1.5") and passed 52/0 re-run alone,
  because that suite regenerates the bundle itself and leaves the tree fixed for the next reader. The rebuild now runs BEFORE the battery, because the battery has to measure the tree
  that gets committed. It was never a flake.
- **THE RELEASE MACHINERY IS GENERIC NOW.** `dev/release-gates.sh` (the battery and its report), `dev/release-record.py` (the AGENTS.md insert, idempotent, version read from the page)
  and `.github/workflows/release.yml` are shared by every release; a release supplies its own `dev/patch-<ver>.py`, `dev/repin-<ver>.mjs`, `dev/release-<ver>.sha256` (the proof of the
  prepared tree, byte for byte) and this entry. The 74.1.5 workflow is left where it is and finds no payload, so it does nothing.

## 74.1.5 (October 15, 2026 · 3:22 PM EDT): the top-artists bubble opens the artist, and the storage cleaner shows every size in MB

- **The ask, in one line**: an artist in the home Top artists bubble should open when you tap their song, every song should say how big it is in MB, and Studio's storage cleaner should
  say it too. The three land together because that bubble's rows were the only list on the home screen with NO click handler at all - an artist could be read and never be opened.
- **THE PAGE SHIPPED FROM INSIDE THE REPOSITORY, AND FROM NOW ON IT CAN ONLY SHIP FROM THERE.** `index.html` is ONE 3.24 MB file, and the machine that prepares a release has no git
  credentials and cannot push a file that size - the API carries whole files as call arguments, at any encoding. So the release is a payload plus a workflow:
  `dev/7415-payload.tar.xz.b64` carries `dev/patch-7415.py` (the page edits; idempotent, and `--check` says whether the page is behind) and `dev/repin-7415.mjs` (the gate repins);
  `.github/workflows/apply-page-patch.yml` unpacks them, applies them over the checked-out tree, proves the result against `dev/release-7415.sha256` byte for byte, runs the battery and
  the bundle `--check`s, and only then commits. **This is the first release that could be cut from a host with no credentials at all.**
- **A WORKFLOW CANNOT PATCH A WORKFLOW, AND THE FIRST PUSH OF THIS RELEASE PROVED IT.** Run 38657960997 of `apply-page-patch.yml` passed its first eight steps - payload intact,
  page patch applied, repins applied, and **the whole 50-file tree matching `dev/release-7415.sha256`** - and then failed in the retarget step, whose own work was correct and whose
  *guard* was not. The guard asked `git diff --name-only` what had moved and required the answer to be exactly the two gates, but the tree it runs on already carries the page patch and
  every repinned gate UNCOMMITTED, so the answer was all fifty files. It now measures what **this step** moved: the whole diff EXCLUDING the two gates is hashed before and after and has
  to be bit-identical, and both gates have to differ. Fixing it from inside the repository is impossible and that is a platform rule, not a bug: the Actions token is refused
  (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow ... without 'workflows' permission`), so **any release step that would commit a file under `.github/workflows/` can never
  push.** The commit's own path allowlist admitted `.github/`; it does not any more, because that is a release that can only fail at the last step.
- **TWO GATES WERE ASKING THE HEAD FOR AN OLDER RELEASE'S WORDS, AND WERE RETARGETED BY HAND.** `dev/test-740.mjs` (74.0) and `dev/test-741.mjs` (74.1) each held the HEAD changelog
  entry to the words of the release they describe. The repin moves the head pin under them every release, so at 74.1.5 they were asking THIS release's notes (the artist bubble, the
  storage cleaner) for the last two releases' words: **test-740 52/1 and test-741 84/1 on the tree as it was prepared.** Each now finds the entry for ITS OWN version and asserts against
  that - the same fix 71.8 gave test-705, and the rule this file already carries: **a gate that describes a release must read its own entry by version.** Nothing was weakened: 74.0's notes
  still have to name the skip and the album, 74.1's still have to name the back roll and the restored play, and each file gained one check that its own entry is still in the changelog at
  all. **The prepared release was red before this; it is green after.**
- **THE OTA BUNDLE IS AT A TRUE FIXED POINT.** The zip embeds the root `manifest.json` and that manifest records the zip's own size, so the bundle needs a pass to agree with itself:
  publish the measured size into the embedded manifest, rebuild, repeat. Root `ota/update.zip` **955929** bytes and the Play channel `ota-play/update.zip` **955942** bytes, both
  v74.1.5, both `--check`s OK, and the eight bundle files the last release touched are the eight this one touches. `deploy.yml` then finds nothing to publish, which is what a landed
  release looks like.
- **This entry ships as `dev/release-7415-entry.md`**, with `October 15, 2026 · 3:22 PM EDT`, `955929` and `955942` filled in by the workflow at commit time, so the release's prose is a file of its own

## 74.1 (Oct 12, 2026 · 6:20 PM EDT): both buttons walk the albums, and a restored play knows which record it is
- **The owner's ask, verbatim**: "The next buttons and back buttons still dont bring you to the next album or previous album". 74.0 had made the SKIP button roll forward,
  so this is about what that release left out - and it named two causes, neither of which was the condition 74.0 changed.
- **1. BACK HAD NO ROLL AT ALL.** `hardAdvance` asked the roll only at the TOP of the queue, so `#prevBtn`, the lock screen / headset back and the lyrics-panel
  Previous could only ever wrap inside the album you were in. It now asks at BOTH ends: `if(next < 0)` rolls back, `if(next >= queue.length)` rolls forward, and
  `scAlbumRollQueue(dir)` points the index at that album's FIRST song forward or its LAST song going back. The button's own rule is untouched - a song more than
  three seconds in is restarted, not stepped past.
- **2. THE ROLL COULD NOT TELL WHICH ALBUM IT WAS IN.** It trusted `queueAlbumName` and then demanded the queue be that album's ids in that exact order, so two
  real shapes failed silently. (a) A play RESTORED after a relaunch, an OTA reload or a widget resume: `savePlaybackState` never wrote the album down, so the queue
  came back with no idea it was a record - which is the shape the report was made from (open the app, tap play, press skip). (b) The grouped album header in All
  Songs (`renderListInner`'s `.track-ga-play`): it played an album's songs with no album behind them. The album is now read off the queue (`scAlbumForQueue`), most
  certain first - the queue's own tag, else the playing song's album tag, else the ONE album whose songs are exactly this queue - and a queue two albums both claim
  answers null rather than a guess. `savePlaybackState` writes `album: queueAlbumName || null` and `restorePlaybackState` reads it back (dropping a name that is no
  longer an album), and the grouped header passes `g.album` when the tag names one of your albums (and passes nothing when it does not, so DJ Mode's context rule
  and the focus rule see exactly what they saw before).
- **THE GUARD IS SHARPER, NOT LOOSER.** Comparison is by SONG, because a shuffled album or a library-order tag group is still that album - but the no-tag case is
  STRICT: with nothing named anywhere, the queue must be the album's songs in the album's own saved order. So a playlist that happens to hold one album's songs in
  a different order still wraps inside itself, and 73.5's rule (a library-wide queue, a mix or a search result never rolls) is intact. The option still refuses
  everything, both directions.
- **TWO GATES PINNED THE 74.0 SHAPE AND WERE RETARGETED BY HAND**, with the reason in each file. `dev/test-735.mjs` [2] lifted the roll out of the page and its
  slice started at `scAlbumRollNext` - which is a one-line call now, with `scAlbumForQueue`/`scAlbumRollOrder`/`scAlbumRollStep` above it - so the lift starts at
  `scAlbumForQueue`, the harness is handed `allTracks` (reading the album off the playing song is one of the answers now) and drives both directions; it also pins
  the back-roll line and the two derivation claims. `dev/test-740.mjs` [2] pinned the old order-and-length guard and the two-argument call: the guard needle is the
  same-songs check now, and its old driven claim "at its first song it wraps inside the album, not backwards into another one" is the exact behaviour the owner
  asked to change, so it is pinned the way it ships (back goes to the previous album's last song).
- **VERIFIED**: NEW `dev/test-741.mjs` (**85 checks**): [1] release metadata; [2] the rules read out of the file (one reader per question, the set-and-order guard,
  both directions served by one step, hardAdvance asking at both ends, the save and the restore, the grouped header's tag, the option); [3] DRIVEN across THREE
  boots that share one store - back lands on the previous album's LAST song (queue, index, album, now bar and the new `__scAlbumForQueue` hook), back mid-album is a
  song step, a late song still restarts, the first album wraps to the last both ways, the grouped All Songs header (reached through the real sort sheet - Artist +
  album) rolls both ways, a playlist still wraps inside itself, the option off wraps inside the album in both directions, then a RELAUNCH comes back with the queue,
  the index AND the album and rolls both ways, and a PRE-74.1 SAVE (the album field deleted, exactly what an older build wrote) rolls anyway because the album is
  read off the songs. **The gate fails 41 of its 85 checks on the 74.0 tree** - every back, header, saved and derived claim - while the metadata and the 74.0

## 74.0 (Oct 12, 2026 · 6:05 PM EDT): the skip button rolls into the next album too, because a record ending and a record being skipped are the same question
- **The owner's ask, verbatim**: "The albums should go to the next album with the skip button too not just airing in to the next one". 73.5 had shipped the roll
  for a song that reached its own end and had SAID SO in its own notes - "Only a song that really ends rolls on. The Next button stays inside the album you are
  in" - so at the end of a record the one control a listener reaches for did the opposite of what the app was about to do by itself a second later.
- **THE FIX IS ONE CONDITION, IN ONE PLACE.** `hardAdvance(dir, wrap)` (index.html ~:29102) has lost its third argument: 73.5's `if(natural && dir > 0 && ...)`
  is `if(dir > 0 && scAlbumRollQueue() >= 0)` now. Every forward step off the last song of an album goes through that line - the player's **Next** (`#nextBtn`),
  the lock screen / headset skip (`mediaSetActionHandler('nexttrack')`), the Next button in the lyrics panel, and the end of the song (`onEnded` now calls
  `hardAdvance(1, true)` with no third argument) - so a skip and a handover cannot disagree again. The crossfade handover (`maybeStartCrossfade`) and the
  gapless cut in `onEnded` were already natural-end paths and are untouched.
- **WHAT THE ROLL STILL REFUSES, IT STILL REFUSES**, and the guards were deliberately left alone: `scAlbumRollNext` answers only for a queue that IS one album
  (its ids, in its order, all live), so a playlist, a mix, a search result, an Albums-tab play-all, or a queue that merely CARRIES an album name keeps its own
  order and wraps inside itself; `autoNextAlbum` is still ON by default and still answers null when off, so Next then wraps inside the album you started; and
  **Previous is untouched** - it still wraps inside the album you are in rather than jumping backwards into another one. The Playback description now says the
  skip button does the same on the last song.
- **TWO GATES PINNED THE OLD RULE, AND BOTH WERE RETARGETED BY HAND** (the only gate edits this release that are not a version pin). `dev/test-735.mjs` [2]
  asserted `hardAdvance(1, true, true); // the album ends` and `if(natural && dir > 0 ...)` - exactly the rule the owner asked to have changed; both lines read
  the shipped code now (no third argument, `dir > 0` alone), with 73.5's own words quoted beside the reason. `dev/test-739.mjs` [1] quoted 73.9's note words
  (`refetch`, `single`, `album`) off `entries[0]` - true only while 73.9 was the head, so the next release made a gate that describes 73.9 fail for saying
  nothing about refetching; it finds its own entry by a frozen `const OWN = '73.9'` and reads that, the same fix 73.6.2 gave test-7317 and 71.8 gave
  test-716/717. Any gate whose VER moves while its content pins quote its OWN release needs this shape.
- **THE DATE STAMP IS A GATE, AND IT CAUGHT THIS RELEASE.** The first stamp written here (8:20 PM EDT) is 00:20 UTC on the 13th, and `dev/test-6643.mjs`
  fails "and not one of them in the future" against a clock at 22:27 UTC. The stamp is **6:05 PM EDT** (22:05 UTC, 22 minutes before the tree was verified) -
  the same character length, so the bundle bytes did not move. Recorded because the check is right and the temptation was to read it as a stale gate.
- **VERIFIED**: NEW `dev/test-740.mjs` (**53 checks**): [1] release metadata; [2] the rules read out of the file; [3] DRIVEN on the real page in jsdom - three
  albums listed in their own order, an album played from its LAST row, `#nextBtn` landing on the NEXT card's first song (queue `t4,t5`, index 0, album
  `Aurora Sessions`, now bar `Clash`, the focus rule following the album that took over), a fresh mid-album Next walking the same album, Previous still wrapping
  inside it, the LAST album coming back round to the first, the option turned OFF through **Settings - More - Playback** making Next wrap inside the album (and
  back ON making it roll, with no restart), and a playlist and a library-wide queue keeping their own order. **The gate fails 12 of its 53 checks on the 73.9

## 73.9 (Oct 10, 2026 · 1:05 PM EDT): a refresh only adds the new ones, and a removed single cannot ride back in
- **The owner's ask, verbatim**: "Why do singles refresh and albums refresh refetch every single one that even I deleted it should only refetch new ones
  not delete ones". It is the same sentence 72.1 answered ("Refetching albums or singles shouldnt refetch every single or album that was deleted too"), and
  72.1 only closed the RESURRECTION half. Driven against the shipped 73.8 tree, two defects survived, both from the same shape: a refresh rebuilt a list
  from the ONE reply it had just fetched.
- **1. A SHORT REPLY DELETED ROWS THE LIST ALREADY HAD.** `__refetchSingles` (`window.__refetchSingles`, ~:45782) rebuilt every artist group from that
  reply, and `__singlesRefreshArtistGroup` (the per-artist ↻, ~:45800) swapped a group's rows for it. One storefront having a bad minute - or a single
  filed under another store id - was enough for a song that was on the list to vanish, and a reply that carried nothing left an empty state over a group
  that had songs. Measured on a stub: a reply without `Luna` took Luna off the list, and the ↻ did the same to its own group.
- **2. THE REFETCH FALLBACK HANDED BACK A REMOVED SINGLE.** When a reply carries nothing (`!totalFound && !kept.rows`), the refetch falls back to the
  SAVED list: `loadCachedDiscoverPopup('🎵 Singles')`. A remove HIDES the row where it stands (`row.style.display = 'none'`) and `__scSnapshotDiscoverPopup`
  copies what is on screen, so the saved body still contains it - the Discover button cleaned what it opened, that loader did not. Measured: remove all
  three singles, refetch, and the popup drew a removed one (Echo) again.
- **THE FIX, IN TWO PARTS.** (a) ONE cleaner, `scCleanRemovedRows(bodyHTML)`, exported as `window.__scCleanRemovedRows`: it strips the play buttons, drops
  a singles row by the id it was removed under OR by its name, drops an album row by its collection id OR its name, drops the junk titles the lists already
  refuse, and then drops an artist group left with nothing to show. `cleanCachedSinglesBody` is now that function (same name, same callers) and
  `loadCachedDiscoverPopup` runs it on every saved body before opening it - so no reader of a saved list can hand back a removed row. Its app helpers are
  `typeof`-guarded because dev/v609-check.cjs and dev/report-634-check.cjs extract this source and run it on its own. (b) A refresh MERGES: the rows an
  artist already has (read back out of the saved snapshot through the same cleaner, keyed by track id AND normalized title so another storefront's copy of
  the same single is not added twice) are kept, then only the reply's genuinely new songs are added - `_scSavedRowsFor` / `_scNewSingles` / `_scTotal`, the
  subtitle now counting `kept.rows + _scShownRows` instead of the raw reply. `__singlesRefreshArtistGroup` does the same with the group's live rows
  (`_keptRows` + `_newRows`), so a refresh can only add. `__singlesDeepRefreshArtistGroup` (the retired ⚡ chip's handler, still wired for a saved popup
  from an older build) is now a one-line delegation to that refresh - its `includeHidden: true` fetch and its "all, including removed" toast are gone, and
  `includeHidden` no longer appears anywhere.
- **WHAT DID NOT MOVE.** 72.1's rule is intact: `var skipHidden = true;` and `isSingleHidden(sr.trackId || sr.collectionId, sr.trackName)` in
  `fetchArtistSingles`. `hideSingle`/`hideAlbum` still write id + `t:`-name, Recently Deleted still holds a removal for thirty days, and the ALBUM side was
  verified unchanged (a removed album stays gone across `Refetch albums`).
- **VERIFIED**: `dev/test-739.mjs` (new, **62 checks**). [1] release metadata; [2] the rules read out of the file (one cleaner, the loader uses it, the
  fetch still filters, the merge marks, the old `bodyEl.innerHTML = matched.length` swap gone from EVERY renderer, the deep handler delegating); [3] the
  Singles list DRIVEN on a stub iTunes: refetch -> add a new single (the list is one row longer, not rebuilt) -> starve the reply of Luna (Luna stays) ->
  per-artist ↻ with the same short reply (the group keeps its songs) -> remove ALL four rows and refetch (the popup draws none of them back and no removed
  name is in the body at all); [4] an album DRIVEN: remove it, `Refetch albums`, it does not come back. **The gate fails 30 of its 62 checks on the 73.8
  tree** - among them "a reply without Luna keeps Luna" (old: `Jaan,Naina,Echo`), "the per-artist refresh keeps the songs the group already shows" (old:
  the same), "a refetch after that draws none of them back" (old: drew `Echo`). `dev/repin-739.mjs` (new, from repin-738) does A/B/D/E/F3: VER 73.8 ->
